audit_record.bug_semantics: During ZIP extraction, a local attacker able to mutate the extraction directory can replace an already-validated parent directory with a symlink before OpenClaw opens the destination pathname. The later pathname-based write follows the rebound parent and can create or truncate a file outside the extraction root with the OpenClaw process's privileges; leaf-only O_NOFOLLOW protection does not bind mutable parent traversal to the checked directory identity.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Original feature implementation. Commit 3a6ee5ee00176c88aee32bb8bfd543780014c079 first added the production ZIP extractor in src/infra/archive.ts with a lexical path.resolve/string-prefix containment check followed by separate mkdir, asynchronous ZIP decoding, and fs.writeFile(outPath, data). That check/use separation created the parent-symlink TOCTOU window at inception; later streaming and partial symlink-hardening changes retained the same mutable-parent pathname resolution and are not origins.

review_record.bug_semantics: OpenClaw's ZIP extractor constructed an output path under the extraction directory, checked path and symlink state, and only afterward opened that pathname for truncating/writing. A local attacker able to mutate the extraction tree could replace a checked parent directory with a symlink during that gap, causing an entry such as slot/target.txt to resolve outside the extraction root and clobber the external target. O_NOFOLLOW protected only the final path component; it did not bind parent resolution to the object that had been checked.
review_record.flaw_origin: Original feature implementation. Commit 3a6ee5ee00176c88aee32bb8bfd543780014c079 first added the production ZIP extractor in src/infra/archive.ts with lexical containment checking followed by mkdir and fs.writeFile(outPath, data). Subsequent streaming and symlink-hardening commits changed the sink but preserved the same check/use separation; in particular 4b226b74f5fd3b106a83a6347fd404172e2fd246 added parent checks and O_NOFOLLOW on the leaf without making parent traversal race-safe.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The Zalo webhook router matched a registered route using the normalized URL pathname, but unauthenticated failure accounting used the raw req.url, including its query string, as part of the key in a process-global Map with no maximum size or expiry. An attacker could repeatedly POST to the same reachable valid webhook path with an invalid or missing secret while varying ?nonce=..., causing every 401 to create and retain a distinct webhookStatusCounters entry and eventually exert memory pressure or trigger OOM. The similarly raw-URL-keyed rate-limit map was also unbounded, although that path ran only after successful target authentication; the unauthenticated advisory path is the 401 status-counter insertion.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 added Zalo webhook ingress hardening, including anomaly accounting and rate limiting. In extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts it introduced webhookStatusCounters as an unbounded Map, recordWebhookStatus() as an unconditional insertion for security error statuses, and calls that passed req.url for pre-authentication 401 responses. This composed a normalized route match with attacker-controlled raw-URL keying and unbounded retention; later commit 453664f09d0911cc1829d22c63f664f0ad2c8c10 only moved the already-vulnerable logic into monitor.webhook.ts.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/advisories/GHSA-wr6m-jg37-68xh states that unauthenticated query-string churn on one valid Zalo webhook route caused unbounded in-memory key growth, with affected versions <= 2026.2.26 and patched versions >= 2026.3.1; the assigned API bundle expresses the package range as < 2026.3.1 and first patched version 2026.3.1.

At a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3, src/plugin-sdk/webhook-targets.ts:28-40 parses req.url and matches only normalizeWebhookPath(url.pathname), proving that distinct query strings reach the same registered route. In extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts, the BIC adds the unbounded webhookStatusCounters Map at line 95, derives status keys as `${path}:${statusCode}` and inserts them at lines 169-171, and passes raw req.url on unauthenticated/ambiguous 401 paths at lines 202 and 208. It also uses raw req.url for the post-authentication rate-limit key at lines 212-216.

Direct parent-tree verification: git grep -n -E 'webhookStatusCounters|recordWebhookStatus|rateLimitKey|req\.url.*statusCode' e0aaf2d399753e0a80d73409f30567394ee4a8b5 -- extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts returned no matches. The parent handler still returned 401 for invalid/ambiguous secrets but had no status-counter insertion or raw-URL-keyed rate-limit state. The a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 diff directly adds all parts of the flawed mechanism, so the immediate parent lacks it.

Fix commit 43cad8268d46a3663c79be831f2cacb015114882 changes extensions/zalo/src/monitor.webhook.ts to use the matched resolver path for 401 accounting (lines 138, 151, 157), replaces the counter with createBoundedCounter(maxTrackedKeys=4096, ttlMs=6 hours) at lines 55-58, replaces the rate-limit Map with createFixedWindowRateLimiter(maxTrackedKeys=4096) at lines 46-50, and uses the bounded helpers at lines 117 and 164. Its regression test sends 200 unauthorized requests with different query nonces and asserts status-counter size 1; a separate authenticated churn test asserts rate limiting and state size 1. The same commit's CHANGELOG entry explicitly describes Zalo query-string normalization and bounded security tracking.

review_record.bug_semantics: The Zalo webhook handler resolved a registered target from URL.pathname, but then keyed process-global security-tracking maps with req.url, which includes the attacker-controlled query string. Repeated POSTs to one valid route with distinct queries therefore created distinct webhookStatusCounters entries even before authentication (the 401 path), and authenticated query churn likewise created distinct rate-limit entries and bypassed the intended per-route limit. Neither Map had a size bound or expiry, so a reachable webhook permitted unbounded memory growth and availability loss.

The pre-existing webhook route itself predates this commit, but its immediate parent had none of this vulnerable tracking state. Commit 453664f09d0911cc1829d22c63f664f0ad2c8c10 later moved the same logic to monitor.webhook.ts without originating the flaw.

audit_record.bug_semantics: A tenant able to create or update Fission Function or Environment CRDs could request SYS_TIME in securityContext.capabilities.add on a tenant-controlled container or init container. The v1.24.0 admission validator and executor merge sanitizer used a fixed denylist containing only SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, and DAC_OVERRIDE, so SYS_TIME passed both layers and reached the resulting pod. Without restrictive Pod Security Admission on the function-pod namespace, CAP_SYS_TIME permits clock_settime(CLOCK_REALTIME) against the node-wide, non-time-namespaced real-time clock, corrupting wall-clock-dependent state for co-tenants. The separate OCI-default-capability concern was not fully addressed by this advisory's fix.

primary_record.bug_semantics: Fission's tenant-facing Environment and Function validation and its executor merge defense used a fixed six-entry denylist for securityContext.capabilities.add. SYS_TIME was not listed, so a tenant with Function/Environment CRUD could request SYS_TIME in a PodSpec container or initContainer (and, after the same policy was reused, a bare Runtime/Builder Container), pass admission, survive merge sanitization, and run with CAP_SYS_TIME. Without a restrictive cluster PSA policy, clock_settime(CLOCK_REALTIME) can then rewrite the node-wide, non-time-namespaced real-time clock and disrupt every co-tenant's certificate windows, leases, token expiry, scheduling, and time-series integrity. The denylist also could not remove OCI-runtime default capabilities; that separate structural concern was explicitly not fully repaired by this advisory's final fix.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated user able to create and run workflows could supply the Git node with a staged working repository whose configured push remote was another attacker-controlled local repository. For push and pushTags, vulnerable releases left Git's file transport enabled, causing local git-receive-pack to run receive-side hooks in the target repository as the n8n process. Setting core.hooksPath=/dev/null on the initiating repository did not suppress hooks in that local receive target. The fix validates configured remotes and removes file from GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL for write operations when hooks are disabled.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The original Git node accepted a workflow-selected baseDirectory, constructed simple-git for that repository, and exposed git.push() without restricting repository-controlled local remote targets or Git's file transport. That original trust-boundary crossing, rather than a later move, import, refactor, or aggregate landing, is the flaw origin.

review_record.bug_semantics: Repo.clone() and Repo.clone_from() accepted caller-controlled clone options and ultimately rendered separate_git_dir (or raw --separate-git-dir in multi_options) as git clone --separate-git-dir=<path>. The default allow_unsafe_options=False check consulted Repo.unsafe_git_clone_options, but through 3.1.58 that denylist omitted --separate-git-dir. Git therefore created the repository metadata tree at an attacker-chosen path outside the intended clone destination and left a gitdir pointer at the destination, permitting arbitrary directory/file creation within the process's filesystem permissions and possible later hook execution.
review_record.flaw_origin: 00c5497f190172765cc7a53ff9d8852a26b91676 is the smallest GitPython commit that created the vulnerable public Repo.clone behavior: it replaced fork_bare(), which always supplied bare=True, with clone() and changed the invocation from self.git.clone(..., **options) to self.git.clone(..., **kwargs), removing the forced-bare constraint while promising that all kwargs go to git-clone. That made a lone separate_git_dir option reach a normal clone. b425301ad16f265157abdaf47f7af1c1ea879068 later added clone_from(), 57d053792d1cde6f97526d28abfae4928a61e20f merely added Cygwin polishing for an option already forwarded, e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 introduced an incomplete clone denylist for multi_options, and 5c59e0d63da6180db8a0b349f0ad36fef42aceed extended that same incomplete denylist to kwargs; none is an earlier first-writer than 00c5497f190172765cc7a53ff9d8852a26b91676.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The public, unauthenticated GET /ready readiness route attempted a database connection and SELECT 1 inside a broad exception handler, then serialized str(e) into the JSON response. A caller able to provoke a database/driver error could therefore receive internal database hostnames, IP addresses, ports, connection parameters, driver details, and potentially credentials embedded in the exception text.

audit_record.bug_semantics: IndexFile.from_tree accepted one to three caller-controlled treeish values, appended them after GitPython's own --index-output=<temporary-index> argument, and passed the resulting argv to git read-tree without rejecting option-shaped treeish values or inserting --. An injected --index-output=<attacker-path> was therefore parsed as a later Git option and overrode the internal destination, clobbering any writable path with a Git index blob. IndexFile.reset inherited the same flaw by delegating its commit argument to from_tree, while IndexFile.merge_tree independently appended its caller-controlled base and rhs values to an unguarded read-tree invocation.

primary_record.bug_semantics: IndexFile.from_tree accepted one to three caller-controlled treeish values, appended them after GitPython's own --index-output=<temporary-index> argument, and passed the resulting argv to git read-tree without rejecting option-shaped treeish values or inserting --. An injected --index-output=<attacker-path> was therefore parsed as a later Git option and overrode the internal destination, clobbering any writable path with a Git index blob. IndexFile.reset inherited the same flaw by delegating its commit argument to from_tree, while IndexFile.merge_tree independently appended its caller-controlled base and rhs values to an unguarded read-tree invocation.

review_record.bug_semantics: IndexFile.from_tree appends caller-controlled treeish values after its own --index-output=<temporary-index> argument and invokes git read-tree without an unsafe-option guard or option/operand separator; reset delegates its caller-controlled commit to from_tree, while merge_tree appends caller-controlled base and rhs values to another unguarded read-tree invocation. Supplying --index-output=<attacker-chosen-writable-path> is therefore parsed as an option, and Git's last-occurrence-wins behavior overrides from_tree's temporary path, replacing the chosen file with a valid DIRC git-index blob. The attacker controls the destination, not arbitrary replacement bytes, yielding destructive arbitrary file overwrite rather than code execution.
review_record.flaw_origin: babf5765da3e328cc1060cb9b37fbdeb6fd58350 is the original implementation of Index.from_tree, not a move or refactor: it created arg_list, appended GitPython's own --index-output temporary path, extended the same argv with unvalidated *treeish, and called repo.git.read_tree(*arg_list, **kwargs). Its direct parent has no from_tree or read_tree sink. f6c8072daa942e9850b9d7a78bd2a9851c48cd2c later added the independently vulnerable merge_tree base/rhs forwarding, 58fb1187b7b8f1e62d3930bdba9be5aba47a52c6 later made reset delegate to from_tree, and af32b6e0ad4ab244dc70a5ade0f8a27ab45942f8 merely moved the extant implementation into the index package; none supersedes the earliest true BIC.

audit_record.bug_semantics: When a plugin lacked READ_FILES, PluginSandbox attempted to confine filesystem access by replacing only builtins.open with restricted_open. pathlib.Path.open/read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes and io.open retained independent file-opening paths, and pathlib/io were available to plugin code, so an untrusted plugin could read or modify paths outside the sandbox's allowed directories without passing _is_safe_path.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef created the plugin sandbox and first implemented _restrict_file_operations as a single-name monkey patch: it assigned builtins.open = restricted_open but did not interpose io.open or pathlib.Path methods. The same commit advertised a zero-trust security sandbox, made this incomplete hook the READ_FILES enforcement boundary, and therefore originated the bypass rather than merely moving or refactoring existing vulnerable code.

In the validated clone, `git log d0be3e9^ -L 479,512:openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` follows the vulnerable function through formatting and policy changes to 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef, whose added lines 217-251 call _restrict_file_operations when READ_FILES is absent and replace only builtins.open. Independent `git log --all -S'builtins.open = restricted_open' -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` and `-S'def _restrict_file_operations'` each return only 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef. `git diff --name-status 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` reports `A`, directly proving the entire vulnerable file and mechanism are absent from the immediate parent tree. `git cat-file -p 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef` proves the one-parent topology, human author/committer, Claude Code generation line, and Claude co-author trailer. `git show d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f` shows the direct repair: save and replace io.open plus pathlib.Path.open/read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes/unlink/mkdir/rmdir, route each through the sandbox path check, and restore every original method afterward. Its immediate parent e0c999ea44429e8de00b4acb3ba570efdc733092 had added pathlib and io to shared blocked-module constants as precursor hardening, while d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f is the advisory-named commit that directly interposes the bypassing APIs. `git tag --contains` places the BIC first in v1.3.0 (and all v1.3.x tags) but not v1.2.1, and places the fix first in v1.4.0 and later tags, matching the patched boundary.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle begins with the normal, one-parent feature commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef: its parent has no plugin_sandbox.py, and it introduces both the claimed READ_FILES boundary and the incomplete builtins.open-only enforcement. pathlib.Path uses pathlib/io entry points rather than the replaced builtins name, so the advisory's Path and io proof of concept bypasses the exact mechanism written by that commit. Later commits 642fb2bdec8af6f1d592c322dfa98647e145fcef and 35499f201ae2dc531d1194f6810c953d8b9af78b changed restoration and allowed-path policy while retaining that same single-hook design; ccb60e1a29ef67700128ca54eb25a95413d71ff1 only reformatted the relevant line. review_record.bug_semantics: A plugin executing without PluginCapability.READ_FILES was supposed to be confined to the sandbox temporary directory and explicitly safe paths. The sandbox enforced that policy only by replacing builtins.open with restricted_open. Plugin code could instead import pathlib or io and call pathlib.Path.read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes/open or io.open; those independent entry points never reached restricted_open, so the plugin could read or modify arbitrary host files, for example Path('/etc/passwd').read_text(), despite lacking the file capability. The repository advisory specifically describes the bypass in threading mode and notes that process isolation had a separate broader restriction failure.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef is the smallest public first-writer: it creates plugin_sandbox.py and the plugin subsystem, advertises file-system capability enforcement, but _restrict_file_operations patches only builtins.open. Its single parent 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a has no plugin_sandbox.py at the affected path. Its immediate parent e0c999ea44429e8de00b4acb3ba570efdc733092 had already added pathlib/io to shared AST/import blocklists, but d0be3e9 completes the fix for references bound before sandbox execution and is the repository advisory's named direct fix. `git tag --contains 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef --sort=version:refname` starts at v1.3.0 and includes v1.3.0-v1.3.6; `git tag --contains d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f --sort=version:refname` starts at v1.4.0. `git diff --stat v1.2.1..v1.3.0 -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` shows the sandbox file absent from v1.2.1 and present in v1.3.0, while `git diff v1.3.6..v1.4.0 -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` shows the builtins-only implementation replaced by the io/pathlib coverage. Thus released v1.3.0 through v1.3.6 are affected and v1.4.0 is the first tagged fixed release.
review_record.reasoning: The security boundary and its flawed implementation arrive together in the BIC: there was no earlier plugin sandbox for a human change merely to expose, move, or activate. The BIC explicitly promises capability-based file restrictions yet implements only one Python file-opening surface, leaving commonplace equivalent APIs unrestricted. The direct parent lacks the entire affected file, and line/pickaxe history rejects later refactors as first-writers. The BIC commit object itself explicitly attributes generation and co-authorship to Claude. Because AI-authored code created both the new attack surface and the root protection-mechanism failure, rather than merely carrying an old defect or contributing a later flawed change, the appropriate closed verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.

audit_record.bug_semantics: A malicious repository can put traversal components in a .gitmodules section name. GitPython parses that attacker-controlled section name without validation, assigns it to Submodule._name, and during Submodule.update(init=True) uses it to form <parent git dir>/modules/<name>. The resulting escaped path is passed to directory and clone operations, so initialization creates an attacker-controlled Git repository outside the intended clone directory.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc introduced _module_abspath() with os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name) and changed the initialization branch of Submodule.update() from the tree-backed submodule path to this unchecked name-derived path before Repo.clone_from(). That is the first causal connection between an untrusted .gitmodules name and the filesystem repository-creation sink; the pre-existing unchecked sm_name() parser alone did not create this attack path.

evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc states that <=3.1.57 is affected and >=3.1.58 is patched. It identifies the flow sm_name(section) -> Submodule.iter_items() assigning sm._name -> _module_abspath() joining parent_repo.git_dir/modules/name -> clone/filesystem operations, and documents a released-3.1.57 PoC that creates /tmp/gitpython_poc_escaped_root/modules_dir while core Git rejects the suspicious name.

At 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc, git/objects/submodule/util.py sm_name() returns section[11:-1] unchecked; git/objects/submodule/base.py iter_items() reads n = sm_name(sms) and assigns sm._name = n. The same commit adds _module_abspath() at then-lines 204-210, whose Git-file branch returns os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name).

The 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc diff changes the Submodule.update() initialization branch from module_path = join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path) to module_path = self._module_abspath(self.repo, self.path, self.name), after which Repo.clone_from(self.url, module_path, n=True) creates the repository. The path value in the parent was constrained by the required pc.tree[path] lookup; the newly used section name was not validated.

Immediate-parent tree verification: git rev-parse 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc^ returns a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f. git grep on that exact parent tree finds neither _module_abspath nor a git_dir/modules/name join. Direct inspection of the parent update branch shows only join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path) feeding Repo.clone_from(). The BIC tree contains _module_abspath at base.py:204, the unchecked join at :206, and update's call at :422.

git log -L over _module_abspath traces the function through formatting/type-only edits to its zero-line addition in 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc. The next commit 67680a0877f01177dc827beb49c83a9174cdb736 extracts the same behavior into _clone_repo() and is therefore a refactor, not the BIC; the vulnerable update-to-clone path already exists in 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc.

Release boundary: git for-each-ref --contains identifies 0.3.6 as the earliest release tag containing the BIC. Peeled tag commits are 0.3.5=a2d39529eea4d0ecfcd65a2d245284174cd2e0aa (does not contain the BIC) and 0.3.6=4df4159413a4bf30a891f21cd69202e8746c8fea (does contain it). Thus this exact name-based mechanism first shipped in 0.3.6 and persisted through the advisory's last vulnerable release 3.1.57.

The direct patch e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06 (commit subject 'Validate submodule names before filesystem operations', message naming GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc) adds _validated_name(), rejecting empty, absolute/drive-qualified, and '..'-component names before the modules/name join and other filesystem mutations. It landed on the mainline through merge commit 2212c6396dac0b2a8f03fc2e6708c72b6f363cc9 (PR #2202).

Follow-up direct commit 4299c990e1ca21896f9485277caf7bb0ae5b404c moves validation before the Git-version path branch and landed via f67029c3a28de20f12e537b87a1a1ff801c521d7. Both merges and both direct commits are ancestors of peeled tag 3.1.58=30be45d786e95023e23c616fec5cbabca861b44c; e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06 is not an ancestor of peeled tag 3.1.57=ccbd573ac4ab52ccdcf395c400e600d5809bcc88. The 3.1.58 changelog explicitly lists GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc.

review_record.bug_semantics: A repository-controlled .gitmodules section name is parsed unchanged by sm_name(), assigned to Submodule._name, and, on Git versions using gitfile submodules, joined to <parent git dir>/modules. A name containing ../ components therefore escapes that directory. During submodule initialization, GitPython creates parent directories and clones with --separate-git-dir at the escaped location, allowing a malicious repository whose otherwise tree-validated submodule path is legitimate to create and populate a Git repository at an attacker-chosen filesystem path.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc introduced _need_gitfile_submodules() and _module_abspath(), whose modern-Git branch returned os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name), and changed update() to use that name-derived path for directory removal and Repo.clone_from(). The already-existing iter_items() flow obtained name by slicing the attacker-controlled .gitmodules section header with sm_name() and performed no validation. This commit created the first name-to-filesystem sink; later commit 67680a0877f01177dc827beb49c83a9174cdb736 refactored cloning into _clone_repo() and added --separate-git-dir but was not the first vulnerable implementation.
review_record.ai_marker: No BIC commit-object AI signal. `git cat-file commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc` shows author and committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com> and a conventional message ending `Relates #233`; it has no AI Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, agent marker, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc states affected <=3.1.57 and patched >=3.1.58, identifies sm_name() -> Submodule._name -> _module_abspath() -> _clone_repo(), and records a released-3.1.57 PoC in which name '../../../../../../tmp/gitpython_poc_escaped_root/modules_dir' makes sm.update(init=True) create the escaped repository while core Git rejects the suspicious name.

Run `git show --format=fuller 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc -- git/objects/submodule/base.py`: the non-merge commit adds `_module_abspath`, returning `os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name)` for Git >=1.8, and changes update() from its checkout-path destination to `self._module_abspath(self.repo, self.path, self.name)` before cloning. `git show 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc:git/objects/submodule/base.py` lines around iter_items show `n = sm_name(sms)`, tree lookup by the separate `path`, then `sm._name = n`; util.py shows sm_name merely returns `section[11:-1]`.

Direct-parent proof: `git cat-file -p 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc` names sole parent a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f. `git grep -n -E '_module_abspath|separate_git_dir|git_dir.*modules|modules.*name' a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f -- git/objects/submodule` returns no matches, and the parent's update() uses `join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path)` and clones there. Thus the immediate parent lacks the vulnerable name-derived module path.

Origin cross-check: `git log -L 304,313:git/objects/submodule/base.py 6e61b1d3bdcd2d9b81bac4eb4d17c18b270e5787` traces _module_abspath through formatting/type-only edits back to its addition in 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc; `git log --all --reverse -S'_module_abspath' -- git/objects/submodule/base.py` likewise identifies 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc as the first substantive addition. The commit has one parent and is not a move, revert, release commit, merge, or squash aggregate.

Release-boundary proof: `git describe --contains --tags 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc` returns `0.3.6~35`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc 0.3.5` exits 1, while `git tag --contains 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc --sort=version:refname` begins at 0.3.6 and includes every maintained line through 3.1.57. History therefore narrows the source introduction to release 0.3.6 even though the advisory expresses the vulnerable upper bound as <=3.1.57.

Fix proof: `git show e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06 -- git/objects/submodule/base.py test/test_submodule.py` adds _validated_name(), rejects empty, rooted/drive-qualified and `..` names, validates before filesystem operations, and adds an exact traversal regression asserting no escaped directory is created. Mainline merge 2212c6396dac0b2a8f03fc2e6708c72b6f363cc9 has e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06 as its second parent. Follow-up 4299c990e1ca21896f9485277caf7bb0ae5b404c moves validation ahead of the legacy branch. `git tag --contains` places both direct commits first in 3.1.58, and the 3.1.58 changes.rst names GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc; 3.1.57 precedes them.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated n8n member could keep attacker-controlled responseText containing script while making the expression-capable respondWith parameter resolve to redirect. renderFormCompletion read responseText independently of the response mode, omitted its sandbox Content-Security-Policy for redirect, and passed the raw value to a Handlebars template whose triple-brace responseText branch precedes the redirect branch. A visitor submitting the public form therefore received attacker HTML without the sandbox, allowing script to execute same-origin with the visitor's n8n session.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 7ea920dbe742c0ca7c79c9df749aa7d7c898c571 had intentionally made responseText raw while adding an unconditional sandbox CSP, so it did not yet create the advisory's same-origin execution path. The smallest causal commit is 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c: it made the CSP conditional on respondWith not being redirect while leaving responseText independently loaded and rendered. It is a focused single-parent implementation/test change, not a move, import, revert, or aggregate.

Re-run evidence resolves this for the primary. The first-party GHSA-rmr5-775f-jvm2 affected/patched tables say <1.123.69/>=1.123.69, <2.33.4/>=2.33.4, and <2.34.1/>=2.34.1 and describe the redirect-expression/raw-responseText CSP bypass. primary_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated n8n member could preserve attacker-controlled responseText containing script while making the Form node's expression-evaluated respondWith resolve to redirect. renderFormCompletion loaded responseText regardless of the selected response mode, omitted the sandbox Content-Security-Policy whenever respondWith was redirect, and passed both values to a Handlebars completion template that preferred responseText and emitted it with triple braces. A visitor submitting the public form therefore received the attacker's raw HTML without the sandbox and the script executed from the n8n origin with the visitor's session context.
primary_record.flaw_origin: The mechanism was assembled in two steps. audit_record.bug_semantics: The unified FastAPI server enabled both JWT-protected modules by default while supplying public, hardcoded 39-character HS256 signing secrets for each module. Startup validation checked only that each secret was at least 32 characters and that the two values differed, so both defaults passed. Because TokenAuth.verify_token() trusted any correctly signed token with the module issuer and the route dependencies returned the attacker-controlled sub claim without requiring that client_id to exist, anyone knowing the source could forge a bearer token for an arbitrary client_id and reach authenticated keyserver upload/revocation and telemetry event APIs.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Single-parent commit 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 created openssl_encrypt_server/config.py with the two known JWT defaults and the length-only validate_config(), and simultaneously created the HS256 TokenAuth and protected route dependencies that consumed those secrets. The immediate parent has no openssl_encrypt_server/config.py at all, and all-ref -S/log -L history identifies this commit as the first writer of the vulnerable defaults; no smaller pre-existing or reconstructable member commit contains them.

audit_record.bug_semantics: TagReference.create() accepted caller-controlled path/reference positionals and passed them directly as (path, reference) to repo.git.tag() without an option terminator or unsafe-option inspection. A reference such as --file=/secret was therefore parsed by git tag as its file-input option, and GitPython returned the file contents through the annotated tag message. The later kwargs-only guard inspected Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), so it still omitted both vulnerable positional values.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The vulnerable forwarding sink was first implemented in 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365: it replaced TagReference.create()'s NotImplementedError with args = (path, ref) followed by repo.git.tag(*args, **kwargs). Commit 3af0c2516c5e18c829da30338614688f6b69b49c was a later incomplete mitigation, not the origin: it added a --file/-F denylist but passed an empty positional list to the checker. Historical moves and formatting commits preserved the 2009 sink and are not BICs.

review_record.bug_semantics: TagReference.create() accepts a caller-controlled positional reference and forwards it as the second positional argument to git tag without an option terminator. A value such as --file=/path/secret is consequently parsed by Git as the tag-message file option, creates an annotated tag, and returns the file contents in-band through tagref.tag.message. Commit 3af0c251 later added a default unsafe-option check, but it called Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), so the positional path and reference were outside the check while keyword spellings were blocked.
review_record.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365 (2009-10-23): it replaced TagReference.create's NotImplementedError stub with args = (path, ref) followed by repo.git.tag(*args, **kwargs), first making the attacker-controlled positional reference reach Git's option parser. The 2026 AI-authored 3af0c2516c5e18c829da30338614688f6b69b49c is an incomplete attempted hardening, not the origin: its direct parent already has the exploitable raw positional sink, and its kwargs-only check merely fails to close that pre-existing path.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated user able to run a workflow can control the Edit Image node's Draw Text value. n8n line-wraps that value and passes it to gm.drawText(). gm 1.23.1 quotes the value as an MVG string and escapes double quotes, but does not first escape attacker-supplied backslashes. A crafted backslash can therefore neutralize gm's added escape before a quote, terminate the intended text primitive, and inject another MVG primitive that makes a blind outbound request or opens a local file.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The vulnerable text-to-gm.drawText() flow is already present in the parentless public root 9cb9804eeec1576d935817ecda6bd345480b97fa. That object is a 257-file initial release import rather than the smallest source change. Public history contains no pre-root member commit or parent tree, so the true commit that first authored the vulnerable boundary cannot be recovered and the aggregate root is rejected as the BIC.

primary_record.bug_semantics: The authenticated workflow-controlled Edit Image Draw Text operation word-wraps its text parameter and passes the resulting string to gm.drawText(). gm 1.23.1 constructs a quoted GraphicsMagick MVG -draw argument and escapes double quotes, but it does not escape backslashes already supplied by the caller. An attacker can place a backslash immediately before a quote so gm's added backslash is itself escaped, closing the intended MVG text primitive and allowing a following attacker-selected MVG primitive to make a blind outbound request or open a local file.

That root is a 257-file, 42,436-line initial import rather than the smallest source commit, and no pre-root public commit/member history exists from which to identify the commit that actually authored the flawed mechanism.

review_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated user who can run a workflow can supply crafted Edit Image / Draw Text input. The node line-wraps that value and passes it unchanged to gm.drawText(). gm 1.23.1 encloses text in an MVG quoted string and escapes double quotes but not attacker-supplied backslashes. A backslash can therefore alter the escaping of a following quote, terminate the intended text primitive, and inject another MVG primitive, causing GraphicsMagick to make a blind outbound request to an attacker-selected address or open a local file.

primary_record.bug_semantics: search_files checked the literal user-supplied glob for a slash-delimited '..' segment before calling fast-glob, but did not validate the paths produced by glob expansion. A pattern such as '{a,..}/SECRET.txt' contains no literal '..' segment, passes the check, and can expand to '../SECRET.txt'; the tool then joined that result to the resolved working directory and either returned the outside filename or read matching lines from the outside file, disclosing files readable by the n8n OS user.
primary_record.flaw_origin: PR #30670 replaced the parent implementation's bounded readdir-based collectFiles traversal with fastGlob(name, { cwd: resolvedDir }) and added only assertPatternStaysInside(name). The new pre-expansion lexical check rejected explicit absolute paths and literal '..' segments, but the result path was consumed by path.join(resolvedDir, fp) without post-expansion canonicalization or containment checking. That change first created the advisory's path-confinement bypass.

audit_record.bug_semantics: With allow_unsafe_options at its safe default, a caller can put an unsafe Git option such as --upload-pack=<attacker command> in the value of a single-character kwarg such as n. The guard examines only the kwarg name, which is n in the original implementation and -n after candidate reconstruction, but transform_kwarg emits the value as a separate argv token. The check therefore misses the attacker-controlled option that Git executes. The defect first affected fetch, pull, and push, was later copied to clone/clone_from, and was later centralized and extended to ls_remote, revision traversal/iter_commits, blame, and archive.
audit_record.flaw_origin: e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 is the smallest real BIC: it introduced default unsafe-option guards for Remote.fetch, Remote.pull, and Remote.push and fed check_unsafe_options only list(kwargs.keys()), while the existing single-character kwarg transformation emitted an option-like value as a second argv token. 5c59e0d63da6180db8a0b349f0ad36fef42aceed later propagated the same mistake to clone/clone_from. 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 later replaced the existing key-list checks with the still-key-only _option_candidates helper and added more guarded APIs; it expanded/refactored the already-present mechanism rather than introducing it.

review_record.bug_semantics: GitPython's unsafe-option guards reconstructed candidate options from kwarg names but did not inspect a single-character kwarg's value. With the normal split_single_char_options=True transformation, a call such as clone_from(..., n="--upload-pack=<attacker command>") passes validation as candidate '-n' and is then emitted as two argv tokens, '-n' and '--upload-pack=<attacker command>'; Git interprets the second token and runs the supplied upload-pack command. The shared candidate builder exposed the same value-smuggling primitive through guarded clone/clone_from, fetch, pull, push, ls_remote, revision/iter_commits, blame, and archive paths unless allow_unsafe_options was explicitly enabled.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 introduced the shared _option_candidates guard and its guarded call sites. Its loop derived candidates solely from each kwarg key (for a one-character key, '-<key>') while the already-existing transform_kwarg code emitted a non-boolean one-character kwarg value as a separate argv token. That incomplete security remediation created the guard/value semantic mismatch; the later merge af027be78693962c233cc989915f40e9b135f3a5 is only a carrier, not the BIC.

audit_record.bug_semantics: CredentialsPermissionChecker authorizes only credential IDs whose credential-type keys appear in a set inferred statically from unresolved node parameters. An authenticated member with edit access to a shared workflow can place another user's known credential ID on an HTTP Request node and make genericAuthType or nodeCredentialType an expression. The pre-execution checker sees the expression text rather than its runtime-resolved credential type, omits the credential ID from the ownership query, and execution later resolves and loads the unauthorized credential, allowing use or exfiltration.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The smallest causal source change is PR #25599 member 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b. It changed mapCredIdsToNodes from checking every referenced credential to skipping credential keys absent from getActiveCredentialTypes, whose static inference did not fail closed for expressions. Public squash 608e3bf214328e679c03da3e4a6e9c22ceaac9ca carried the flaw but is not the smallest BIC. Later bundle 2d9a2ec76e180b54e8091e31b1e0638c909abd99 added the unresolved genericAuthType value to the set, fixing literal generic types but preserving the advisory's expression mismatch and therefore not originating the flaw.

primary_record.bug_semantics: CredentialsPermissionChecker builds the set of credential IDs to authorize by filtering node.credentials against credential-type names inferred statically from unresolved node parameters. For an HTTP Request node, an attacker with edit access to a shared workflow can put another user's known credential ID under its real credential type while setting genericAuthType to an expression. The pre-execution checker sees the expression source string rather than the runtime-resolved type, so the real credential key is omitted from the authorization query; execution later resolves the expression and loads/uses that credential, enabling unauthorized use or exfiltration.

review_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated member who can edit a shared workflow can put a credential ID belonging to another user into an HTTP Request node and make genericAuthType (or the analogous nodeCredentialType) an expression that resolves to the real credential type only at execution time. CredentialsPermissionChecker statically computes active credential types from unresolved node parameters. The expression text is not equal to the credential object's real type key, so mapCredIdsToNodes drops the referenced credential and the project ownership/access query never sees its ID. The HTTP Request runtime later resolves the expression and loads that credential, allowing its use or exfiltration; the attacker must know the victim credential ID.

audit_record.bug_semantics: With channels.msteams.groupPolicy set to allowlist, a configured teams/team/channel route allowlist was incorrectly treated as sufficient authorization when the effective sender groupAllowFrom list was empty. A message from any sender in a matched route therefore passed the route gate and skipped the sender gate, allowing an unauthorized Teams group sender to trigger bot processing and replies.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit c7ea47e88682283f87cb8d6481df67f4def0258f added Teams route allowlisting and changed the empty-sender-allowlist rejection from an unconditional effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length === 0 check to effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length === 0 && !channelGate.allowlistConfigured. review_record.bug_semantics: Budibase automation actions accepted an automation-supplied URL and made a server-side HTTP request without applying the outbound IP blacklist. This allowed an automation author to target loopback, private-network, link-local/cloud-metadata, or other internal services. The related REST datasource check was also opt-in because an unset BLACKLIST_IPS produced an empty list. A first automation patch checked only the initial URL, so node-fetch's automatic redirects could still reach a blacklisted address; the closing patch manually followed redirects and checked every destination.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3 first added the OUTGOING_WEBHOOK automation action and its run function, taking inputs.url and passing it to server-side axios with no address policy. The immediate parent has neither the file nor an outgoing-webhook request path. Commit 3d77163773d0ab37342e9e2be5d6b8797758e4eb merely replaced axios with node-fetch and is not the BIC; later Slack, Zapier, Discord, Make, and n8n actions replicated the already-existing flaw.
review_record.ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3` shows author and committer `mike12345567 <me@michaeldrury.co.uk>` and only the message `Adding an outgoing webhook action, so that we have both incoming and outgoing ability.`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI attribution trailer.
review_record.evidence: In the validated clone, `git log -L '/module.exports.run = async function/,+45':packages/server/src/automations/steps/outgoingWebhook.js 3d771637...` reaches 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3 and shows that commit adding the complete run function with `let { requestMethod, url, requestBody } = inputs` and `await axios(request)`; the next commit 3d771637... only changes that call to `fetch(url, request)`. `git log --follow -S'const response = await axios(request)' -- .../outgoingWebhook.js` likewise returns addition in 3ae82b95... and removal in 3d771637.... `git cat-file -e 3ae82b95^:packages/server/src/automations/steps/outgoingWebhook.js` fails, and `git grep -E 'OUTGOING_WEBHOOK|Outgoing webhook|axios\(request\)|fetch\(url' 3ae82b95^ -- packages/server/src/automations` has no match; `git show -s --format=%P 3ae82b95...` gives f9eeefb4dca55aec17f2e5088ac483cdcd257b95. The BIC is a focused, one-parent feature commit, not a move, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate. For the fix lifecycle, 62f50d9779cbd7673bc5b1d99e167f3d2e175ec1 adds hardcoded private/link-local defaults to the REST blacklist, and 6cfa3bcca357c56e615b93462c5e70fd81b891fc adds throwIfBlacklisted to all six automation request paths. Its direct fetch still follows redirects automatically. e7d47625be8b0e3d030a5ca5d1fd604f25098efe replaces those calls with fetchWithBlacklist, uses redirect:`manual`, and calls throwIfBlacklisted(nextUrl) before every hop, closing the remaining redirect SSRF; both 62f50d9 and 6cfa3bc are ancestors of e7d47625. Tag 3.34.1 resolves to da6b1c1d6f35d78d70a1e8cf21c8b41e92931161 and `git grep` shows all six automation files still calling fetch(url) directly. Tag 3.34.2 resolves to 5533f6c3273abdc31afb28b75594327c9a87af35 and contains e7d47625 plus fetchWithBlacklist calls in all six files; it is the first tag containing e7d47625. Thus repository history places the complete automation fix boundary at 3.34.2 (the REST default component first appears in tag 3.33.4), earlier than the advisory metadata's conservative `< 3.41.3` / first-patched 3.41.3 declaration. Tags 3.41.2 and 3.41.3 both contain e7d47625, and their delta has no blacklist or automation-step fix, confirming 3.41.3 is not the actual first containing tag.
review_record.reasoning: The security invariant is that every server-originated request to an automation-controlled destination, including redirects, must reject internal and configured-blacklist addresses by default. The earliest causal violation is the original outgoing-webhook action in 3ae82b95: its parent cannot make that automation request, while the commit creates the user-controlled server-side request without a guard. The axios-to-node-fetch change and later action implementations preserve or duplicate the vulnerability rather than originate it. The March 2026 patch chain first makes the REST policy safe by default, then applies it to automation actions, then closes the redirect bypass; e7d47625 is the last direct code commit needed for the advisory's described attack path. Because the BIC commit object contains only a normal human author/committer identity and no qualifying AI attribution, the vulnerability is NOT_AI regardless of any AI activity elsewhere in repository history.

audit_record.bug_semantics: A post-authenticated user with Create and Modify permission can write attacker-controlled bytes outside the user's scope when an in-scope symlink points to a not-yet-existing out-of-scope file. EvalSymlinks on the link returns fs.ErrNotExist; the guard then walks the lexical path up to the link's in-scope containing directory and approves that ancestor. The subsequent OpenFile call uses O_CREATE|O_TRUNC, so the OS follows the dangling symlink and creates the target outside the scope.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b introduced files.WithinScope and put it on the HTTP write path as an incomplete fix for an earlier symlink escape. Its new ErrNotExist fallback validated the nearest lexical existing ancestor and its own comment explicitly accepted dangling symlinks as best-effort. Commit 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 later moved the same flawed fallback into ScopedFs.within and centralized OpenFile behind that guard; the refactor preserved rather than originated the flaw.
audit_record.ai_marker: BIC commit object contains the exact trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Its author and committer are both Henrique Dias <mail@hacdias.com>; no bot identity is used. The commit-object co-author trailer is the attribution signal used for this verdict.

The added comment says a dangling symlink is allowed and creation callers should treat the check as best-effort.

`git log -L ':WithinScope:files/file.go' 3406d3d7f98dfc3c16e4ff7ff4a87e3bdfe221dd` traces the function's creation to 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b. `git log -S'dangling symlink whose target does not yet exist' -- files/file.go files/scoped.go` returns the BIC, the later move 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3, and the fix 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81.

Direct parent-tree verification: `git rev-list --parents -n 1 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b` gives sole parent 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d, and `git grep -n -e WithinScope -e EvalSymlinks 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d -- '*.go'` returns no matches. The BIC diff is therefore the first parent-to-child appearance of the flawed guard.

`git show 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 -- files/file.go files/scoped.go http/resource.go users/users.go` shows a refactor deleting WithinScope and creating ScopedFs.within with the same ErrNotExist lexical-parent loop and dangling-symlink best-effort comment; ScopedFs.OpenFile guards and then delegates to BasePathFs.OpenFile.

At vulnerable release commit be23ab3a15bf957928ecfed88de5ab67850c1b9c (tag v2.63.15), http/resource.go resourcePostHandler requires Create, treats the dangling link as an existing entry and requires override=true plus Modify, then writeFile calls `afs.OpenFile(dst, os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC, ...)`. files/scoped.go OpenFile first calls the flawed guard and then delegates to s.base.OpenFile, which follows the link.

`git show 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81 -- files/scoped.go` shows the direct fix: on ErrNotExist it Lstats the current target, detects a symlink, Readlinks and resolves it (including real-directory resolution for relative links), and validates the destination rather than the lexical parent. The same commit adds file-level and HTTP regression tests that reject a dangling escaping symlink and assert no outside file is created.

Version-boundary checks: `git tag --contains 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.63.6 and includes v2.63.15; `git tag --contains 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81 --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.63.16 and excludes v2.63.15. The v2.63.16 first-party release notes at https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/releases/tag/v2.63.16 list 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81.

`git cat-file commit 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b` supplies the BIC-only AI evidence: human author/committer Henrique Dias and exact commit-message trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. The commit is a one-parent direct commit in the public graph; GitHub's commit-to-pulls endpoint returns no associated PR, so there are no reconstructable squash member SHAs to substitute for it.

The BIC added a guard intended to make symlink-backed reads and writes safe, but for a nonexistent target it discarded the unresolved leaf and approved the nearest existing lexical ancestor. A dangling final symlink is exactly the case where this inference is false: its parent is in scope while the eventual O_CREATE destination is outside. The write call was guarded by this new function in the same BIC, establishing causal content linkage. The later 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 commit is excluded as a BIC because it is a refactor that moves the unchanged faulty mechanism into ScopedFs. The advisory fix 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81 directly resolves dangling links before deciding scope and lands in the first patched tag v2.63.16. Because the real BIC commit object explicitly co-authors Claude Opus 4.8 and that same commit first writes the causally flawed fallback and its write-path use, the appropriate closed verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.

primary_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is the incomplete confinement logic itself, not the later placement of that logic. The BIC added a guard intended to make symlink-backed reads and writes safe, but for a nonexistent target it discarded the unresolved leaf and approved the nearest existing lexical ancestor. A dangling final symlink is exactly the case where this inference is false: its parent is in scope while the eventual O_CREATE destination is outside. The write call was guarded by this new function in the same BIC, establishing causal content linkage. The immediate parent contains neither WithinScope nor any EvalSymlinks-based equivalent, while line-history and string-history identify 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b as the first writer. Because the real BIC commit object explicitly co-authors Claude Opus 4.8 and that same commit first writes the causally flawed fallback and its write-path use, the appropriate closed verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.

review_record.bug_semantics: ScopedFs is intended to confine a user to a base directory. For an in-scope symlink whose out-of-scope final target does not yet exist, filepath.EvalSymlinks(target) returns fs.ErrNotExist. The vulnerable within()/WithinScope loop then replaces the link path with its lexical parent, resolves that in-scope directory, and returns true. guard() therefore permits OpenFile, while the subsequent base OpenFile with os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC follows the symlink at the OS layer and creates attacker-controlled content outside the scope. An authenticated HTTP user with Create and Modify can reach this through POST /api/resources/<link>?override=true (and equivalent write paths). Existing out-of-scope targets are rejected; the escape is specific to a dangling target. The advisory declares github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/v2 <=2.63.15 affected and 2.63.16 first patched.
review_record.flaw_origin: Incomplete symlink-confinement remediation in 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b. Its direct parent 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d has neither WithinScope nor that fallback. Commit 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 later moves the same loop into new files/scoped.go as ScopedFs.within and is a carrier/refactor, not the first writer. The BIC first ships in v2.63.6; the residual remains in the predecessor issue's nominally patched v2.63.14 and in v2.63.15. Earlier releases had the broader unguarded symlink behavior, which explains the advisory's inclusive <=2.63.15 range; this BIC identifies the first writer of the residual patch-gap logic audited here.

review_record.reasoning: The security invariant is that a checked pathname and the pathname dereferenced for a write must resolve to the same in-scope destination. The BIC's fallback checks a different object: after EvalSymlinks reports the dangling final link's missing destination, it discards the link component and validates only the lexical parent. audit_record.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.Reset() made a context appear safe to reuse but left its CachedTemplates dictionary intact. After one render cached a request-dependent include, a later render on the reset context found the same path in CachedTemplates and returned the old compiled Template without invoking ITemplateLoader.Load(), so content authorized for an earlier request, user, or tenant could cross the reuse boundary.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af introduced the public Reset() API and explicitly promised safe same-thread reuse, but reset only output, global, culture, and source-file stacks. Scriban's include cache and loader-on-cache-miss path already existed in the immediate parent; omitting CachedTemplates from the newly defined reset boundary is therefore the smallest change that created the advisory's vulnerable lifecycle.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-x6m9-38vm-2xhf identifies src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs Reset/CachedTemplates and the include loader path, demonstrates first=admin-only then second=admin-only after Reset(), lists affected versions <= 6.6.0, and lists 7.0.0 as patched.

`git log -L '/public virtual void Reset/',+40:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs f55280a09575e577fcf7f5629007e0814594e3ac` traces the entire vulnerable Reset body to 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af (`Add TemplateContext.Reset`); `git show` shows that focused one-file commit added the safe-reuse documentation and 58 lines implementing Reset without a cache clear.

At the BIC tree, src/Scriban/Functions/IncludeFunction.cs:156-185 checks CachedTemplates first, calls templateLoader.Load() only on a miss, then adds the parsed template to the dictionary. Thus retained state directly suppresses the request-dependent authorization/loading decision on subsequent renders.

Direct parent-tree check: `git grep -n -e 'void Reset' -e 'TemplateContext.Reset' a2fc52e704e9c929e166d3ab7046081dfa8ab1fa -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` finds only unrelated internal ResetPreviousNewLine and no public TemplateContext.Reset. The same parent does contain CachedTemplates construction/property and IncludeFunction.cs:156/185 cache lookup/add plus TemplateLoader.Load at line 162. The vulnerable Reset lines are therefore absent while all prerequisite cache behavior is present.

Version boundary: `git grep` finds no public Reset in tag 3.8.0 and finds it at src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs:817 in 3.9.0; `git tag --contains 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af` starts at 3.9.0 and includes every release through the advisory's 6.6.0 upper bound.

Fix https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/099cb0491df92fafda95acb8c731c60d765bf41a adds `CachedTemplates.Clear()` to Reset in src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs. `git tag --contains 099cb0491df92fafda95acb8c731c60d765bf41a` starts at 7.0.0; `git grep` finds no clear in 6.6.0 and finds it at TemplateContext.cs:981 in 7.0.0.

BIC object check: 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af has exactly one parent, a2fc52e704e9c929e166d3ab7046081dfa8ab1fa, a human author/committer, and no trailers. Its focused diff directly introduces Reset rather than moving, reverting, backporting, or aggregating earlier member commits, so squash decomposition is not applicable.
audit_record.reasoning: The cache itself predates the vulnerability-specific reuse boundary: before the BIC, includes were cached and loaded only on cache misses, but there was no public TemplateContext.Reset promising safe reuse. The BIC is the smallest causal introducer because it added that API and its complete reset implementation while omitting the already-existing CachedTemplates state. Direct inspection of the immediate parent proves the Reset method and safe-reuse promise were absent, while the cache lookup/load/add prerequisites were already present. The flaw shipped beginning with 3.9.0, remained in 6.6.0, and the direct fix added the missing clear before the patched 7.0.0 release. The single-parent, one-file BIC is not a squash or history-only movement. Its commit object contains only a human author/committer and no AI marker, so under BIC-only attribution the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

review_record.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.Reset() cleared output, global, culture, and source-file state but left the per-context CachedTemplates dictionary intact. IncludeFunction.Invoke() resolves an include through TemplateContext.GetOrCreateTemplate(); a cache hit returns the previously compiled Template without calling ITemplateLoader.Load(). An application that pools or reuses a TemplateContext across requests, users, or tenants can therefore prime an include under one authorization context and, after Reset(), expose that stale include content to a later context.
review_record.flaw_origin: Direct atomic commit 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af added the public safe-reuse boundary TemplateContext.Reset() but omitted CachedTemplates.Clear() even though the cache and cache-hit include path already existed in its immediate parent. The vulnerability begins with this Reset contract, not with the older intentional within-context include cache; the commit is neither a move, refactor, revert, merge, nor squash aggregate.
review_record.ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af` shows human author Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, the same human committer, subject `Add TemplateContext.Reset`, and no trailers, Generated-with text, AI co-author, or bot identity.
review_record.evidence: Advisory identity and mechanism: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-58jr-9c6g-55jq identifies CVE-2026-74791 and points to the repository advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-x6m9-38vm-2xhf; the latter states affected <=6.6.0, patched 7.0.0, and documents the stale admin-only/guest-view include-cache path. In the assigned full-history clone, `git grep -n -e 'GetOrCreateTemplate' -e 'CachedTemplates.TryGetValue' -e 'TemplateLoader.Load' 6.6.0 -- src/Scriban/Functions/IncludeFunction.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` shows IncludeFunction.cs:41 calling GetOrCreateTemplate, TemplateContext.cs:1251 testing CachedTemplates, and Load at 1264 only on a miss. BIC: `git show --format=fuller --patch 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af` shows a one-parent, one-file commit adding Reset and its safe-reuse documentation while clearing only outputs, globals, cultures, and source files. `git log -L 964,993:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs HEAD` follows that method back to exactly 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af; `git log --all --full-history -S'public virtual void Reset()' -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only that commit. Direct parent verification: `git grep -n 'public virtual void Reset' a2fc52e704e9c929e166d3ab7046081dfa8ab1fa 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only the child at line 817, while `git grep -n -e 'CachedTemplates' -e 'GetOrCreateTemplate' a2fc52e704e9c929e166d3ab7046081dfa8ab1fa -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs src/Scriban/Functions/IncludeFunction.cs` proves the parent already had the dictionary and cache-hit include path. Tag boundary: `git grep -n 'public virtual void Reset' 3.8.2 3.9.0 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only 3.9.0, establishing the first vulnerable release after the BIC; `git grep -n 'CachedTemplates.Clear()' 6.6.0 7.0.0 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only 7.0.0. `git rev-parse 3.8.2^{commit} 3.9.0^{commit} 6.6.0^{commit} 7.0.0^{commit}` resolves respectively to 53da5bc08964319be948638f2747f8610b305e3c, 3d7c4e29e4803511cafe3724147276c2d60f7f9a, b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7, and 25d148a104dd4d679a1a1932442616599e003c2f; `git tag --contains 099cb0491df92fafda95acb8c731c60d765bf41a --sort=version:refname` begins at 7.0.0.

audit_record.bug_semantics: TemplateContext caches an IObjectAccessor solely under the target's System.Type. For ordinary .NET objects, the cached TypedObjectAccessor eagerly computes its member dictionary using the context's then-current MemberFilter (and MemberRenamer). If the same TemplateContext is later reused after MemberFilter is tightened, GetMemberAccessor returns the permissive accessor already cached for that Type, so reads or writes of members now denied by policy remain available.
audit_record.flaw_origin: ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d first added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and, in the same commit, passed that mutable per-context policy into TypedObjectAccessor while leaving the pre-existing Type-only _memberAccessors cache unchanged and without invalidation. The later 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af added TemplateContext.Reset with an explicit safe-reuse contract but likewise retained the accessor cache, making the stale-policy flaw directly reachable during pooled/cross-request reuse; that later commit amplified but did not originate the flawed filter/cache composition.

audit_record.evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-5wr9-m6jw-xx44 identifies the vulnerable path as TemplateContext.GetMemberAccessor's Type-keyed _memberAccessors cache, GetMemberAccessorImpl constructing TypedObjectAccessor with MemberFilter/MemberRenamer, TypedObjectAccessor.PrepareMembers precomputing exposed fields/properties, and Reset not clearing the cache; it declares <= 6.6.0 affected and 7.0.0 patched. `git log -S'MemberFilter' --all --reverse -- src/Scriban src/Textamina.Scriban` makes ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d the first MemberFilter commit. `git log -L 940,940:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs 8180fb6c^` traces the decisive constructor call from `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberRenamer)` to `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberFilter, MemberRenamer)` at ace7a0e; its diff also adds the mutable TemplateContext.MemberFilter property and TypedObjectAccessor's _filter field/filter checks. Cache-line `git log -L 858,864:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs 8180fb6c^` shows the Type-only cache predates that commit, so the large 2017 namespace move is not misclassified as the BIC. Direct parent-tree verification against c525ebfc8bfb31853da2e0280d2a24045893badb finds zero `MemberFilter` references in TemplateContext.cs and TypedObjectAccessor.cs; that tree constructs `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberRenamer)`, so the advisory's filter/cache composition is absent. `git cat-file -p ace7a0e` shows one parent, human author/committer Alexandre Mutel, and no trailers, so no squash decomposition or commit-object AI signal applies. The BIC is five commits before tag v0.16.0 (`git describe --contains --tags ace7a0e` => v0.16.0~5), while its parent describes from v0.15.0; `git tag --contains ace7a0e` includes 6.6.0. audit_record.reasoning: The attack requires a context to first encounter a model Type under a permissive filter, causing TypedObjectAccessor to snapshot that Type's allowed members, and then to reuse the context under a stricter filter. Because lookup consults only the Type key, later member-expression access receives the old accessor and bypasses the new sandbox policy. Historical decomposition separates three stages: the Type cache existed from the initial repository history; ace7a0e was the smallest normal commit that made it security-sensitive to MemberFilter by adding the policy and feeding it into the cached accessor; 2e95889 later formalized safe TemplateContext reuse without flushing that cache. The immediate parent lacks MemberFilter and the filter-bearing constructor entirely, while ace7a0e's own diff writes both causal additions, establishing parent absence and the BIC. The direct fix clears the stale accessors during Reset and is released exactly at the declared 7.0.0 patched boundary after 6.6.0. Finally, attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: it is a one-parent human-authored commit with no AI marker. The correct closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI regardless of any signals on later lifecycle commits.

primary_record.bug_semantics: TemplateContext caches an IObjectAccessor solely under the target's System.Type. For ordinary .NET objects, the cached TypedObjectAccessor eagerly computes its member dictionary using the context's then-current MemberFilter (and MemberRenamer). If the same TemplateContext is later reused after MemberFilter is tightened, GetMemberAccessor returns the permissive accessor already cached for that Type, so reads or writes of members now denied by policy remain available.
primary_record.flaw_origin: ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d first added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and, in the same commit, passed that mutable per-context policy into TypedObjectAccessor while leaving the pre-existing Type-only _memberAccessors cache unchanged and without invalidation. The later 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af added TemplateContext.Reset with an explicit safe-reuse contract but likewise retained the accessor cache, making the stale-policy flaw directly reachable during pooled/cross-request reuse; that later commit amplified but did not originate the flawed filter/cache composition.

review_record.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.GetMemberAccessor cached one accessor per runtime Type, while TypedObjectAccessor captured the context's then-current MemberFilter and eagerly precomputed the exposed field/property set. After a permissive render populated that cache, resetting and reusing the same TemplateContext under a tighter MemberFilter returned the stale permissive accessor. ScriptMemberExpression therefore continued to read, and potentially write, members that the later sandbox policy denied, enabling cross-request or cross-tenant policy bypass when contexts were reused.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and threaded it into the precomputed TypedObjectAccessor without changing the existing Dictionary<Type, IObjectAccessor> cache key or invalidation behavior. That commit is the first one in which a Type-only cached accessor can embody a context-specific filter policy.

audit_record.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.LimitToString bounded one ObjectToString conversion rather than cumulative rendered output. Each rendered expression entered a fresh top-level ObjectToString call, which reset _currentToStringLength, and StringBuilderOutput appended every resulting chunk without a render-wide cap. A template could therefore emit a near-1 MiB string in each of 1,000 loop iterations, pass the per-call check each time, and accumulate roughly 1 GiB until the host exhausted memory.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest real BIC: it directly added LimitToString, _currentToStringLength, and the top-level reset that made the safety counter restart for every ObjectToString conversion. Its two-file focused patch is neither a merge, aggregate, import, nor move, and its immediate parent lacks both LimitToString and _currentToStringLength. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append was a necessary sink but did not create the advisory-specific limit-bypass invariant; b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later enabled the already-flawed limit by default. Commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b directly fixed the flaw by adding cumulative output accounting across write chunks.

primary_record.bug_semantics: LimitToString tracked only one ObjectToString conversion: every top-level expression reset _currentToStringLength to zero, while TemplateContext.Write forwarded each converted string to StringBuilderOutput, whose Builder.Append calls imposed no render-wide bound. Commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b fixed the lifecycle by accounting every synchronous and asynchronous output chunk against one render-wide counter and resetting that counter only with TemplateContext.Reset.

review_record.bug_semantics: Scriban's object-to-string rendering recursively formats every ScriptObject member value without tracking object identity. With the default ObjectRecursionLimit of 0 (unlimited), a ScriptObject that directly or indirectly contains itself repeatedly re-enters ObjectToString until the CLR throws an uncatchable StackOverflowException, terminating the host process and enabling denial of service wherever an attacker can influence the rendered object graph.
review_record.flaw_origin: cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e is the smallest real introducer: it added the ScriptObject-specific pretty-print branch to ScriptValueConverter.ToString and the recursive call result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value)). Its parent only handled ScriptObject through the generic IEnumerable path and did not recursively extract a KeyValuePair's Value, so the advisory PoC's self-referential ScriptObject path was absent. Later commits moved/refactored the formatter; a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d added an opt-in recursion guard but explicitly initialized ObjectRecursionLimit to 0, preserving the vulnerable default rather than introducing the already-existing recursion.

audit_record.bug_semantics: POST /api/provider-nodes/validate accepts a caller-controlled baseUrl and apiKey, constructs provider URLs from baseUrl, performs server-side fetches, and forwards apiKey in Authorization headers. The later assertPublicUrl mitigation remains bypassable because it compares hostname strings without resolving DNS or revalidating redirect destinations, and its IPv4-mapped IPv6 regex expects a dotted quad even though WHATWG URL parsing canonicalizes mapped literals to hextets first. Mapped loopback/link-local literals, DNS names resolving internally, and redirects can therefore reach internal services. The custom-embedding branch also returns up to 200 bytes of most non-2xx response bodies, while other validation branches expose status/timing signals. A dashboard session is required by default, but not when requireLogin is disabled.

primary_record.bug_semantics: POST /api/provider-nodes/validate accepts caller-controlled baseUrl and apiKey, makes server-side requests to baseUrl-derived provider endpoints, and forwards the supplied secret in Authorization headers. review_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated remote caller controls baseUrl in POST /api/provider-nodes/validate. audit_record.bug_semantics: A page served from an attacker-controlled DNS name can retain its browser origin while DNS rebinding moves the connection to a victim's loopback Paperclip server. Paperclip's missing Host-header gate in default private local_trusted mode allowed that request to receive the implicit instance-admin board actor, create/configure a process-adapter agent with attacker-controlled command and arguments, and invoke its heartbeat/wakeup path, which passed the stored configuration to child_process.spawn as the Paperclip OS user.

Its immediate parent 8c830eae70a14723749828f0ce5d9ae435270e9c lacks both server/src/middleware/auth.ts and server/src/services/heartbeat.ts, so the API-to-process-execution chain is absent there.

primary_record.bug_semantics: A browser page can retain the attacker-controlled origin name while DNS rebinding moves its TCP connection to Paperclip on loopback. Paperclip accepted the attacker hostname because the API had no Host-header gate, assigned requests without a valid bearer credential the trusted board actor, allowed that actor to create/configure an agent, and exposed a heartbeat invocation path whose process adapter passed the stored command and arguments to node:child_process spawn. Thus visiting an attacker page could turn an unauthenticated cross-origin web request into command execution as the Paperclip OS user.
primary_record.flaw_origin: abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b is the smallest commit that completed the RCE mechanism. In one non-merge commit it added server/src/middleware/auth.ts with a board actor as the default for requests lacking a recognized bearer key, mounted company and expanded agent routes in server/src/app.ts without any Host validation, added agent creation and POST /agents/:id/heartbeat/invoke, and created server/src/services/heartbeat.ts where non-HTTP adapter configuration supplies command, args, cwd, and env to spawn(). Its immediate parent had the basic API shell but neither heartbeat.ts nor this process-execution path, so it could not execute an API-configured local command through the disclosed chain.

review_record.bug_semantics: A browser page on an attacker-controlled DNS name can rebind that same origin to the victim's loopback Paperclip server. Because Paperclip did not reject the attacker's Host header and the default local-trusted behavior treated requests without credentials as an instance-admin board actor, the page could create a company and a process-adapter agent with attacker-controlled command/args, then invoke the agent heartbeat/wakeup route; the server passed that configuration to child_process.spawn as the Paperclip OS user, yielding drive-by command execution.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The runner registration-token API exposed token creation through GET routes.
