audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle begins in the implementation member of PR #1563, not in its squash landing. Decomposing the 13-member branch shows that earlier members culminate at parent 229707951c66c6796a2ed6ca75872545df9a60c4 without operations.ts; cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d then creates the file, the permissive operation-key schemas, and the service path that consumes them. That direct parent-tree absence, plus blame and -S history, makes cf80a02d... the smallest real BIC; 34f8bd5... merely squashes the completed PR onto main. An authenticated client can choose operation.key, the request schema accepts any string, and JSONHeroPath follows dangerous prototype segments before writing, explaining the process-wide cross-tenant effect rather than merely a malformed metadata record. The flaw persists in the demonstrably affected published releases through 4.5.5. Direct fix member 0c2d9ce... adds both input refinement and a defense at applyMetadataOperations; 6997aeb0... lands that member and v4.5.6 ships it. For attribution, only the raw cf80a02d... commit object controls: its author/committer are the human Eric Allam and it has no explicit AI marker. CodeRabbit appears only in the PR body/later member naming and is excluded by the BIC-only rule. The resulting closed verdict is NOT_AI.

review_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated low-privilege environment API-key holder can send PUT /api/v1/runs/:runId/metadata with an operation such as {type:"set",key:"$.__proto__.polluted",value:"PWNED"}. UpdateMetadataRequestBody accepted operation.key as an unrestricted string and applyMetadataOperations passed the path to @jsonhero/path without rejecting __proto__, constructor, or prototype. JSONHeroPath.set therefore writes through __proto__ to Object.prototype in the shared webapp process. Inherited attacker data then contaminates unrelated Prisma and prom-client objects across tenants, breaking worker authentication and allowing a repeatable process-wide denial of service.
review_record.flaw_origin: The public main-line commit 34f8bd588e6f1a3edcf3aac3c773d3a0e35af4bf is a GitHub squash of PR #1563. Its reconstructable PR branch has the same final tree, and the smallest member that first adds the unrestricted operation schemas, the operations endpoint path, and JSONHeroPath(operation.key).set is cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d ("Implement run metadata updates from ancestor tasks").
review_record.ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d` records human author and committer Eric Allam <eallam@icloud.com>, a GitButler change-id header, and only the subject `Implement run metadata updates from ancestor tasks`; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
review_record.evidence: First-party GHSA-p28v-f755-9qrg documents the authenticated PUT attack, `$.__proto__.polluted` proof, cross-tenant Prisma/prom-client effects, advisory range >=3.3.8 through 4.5.5, and patched version 4.5.6. In the validated clone, `git log --all -S'new JSONHeroPath(operation.key)' -- packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts` returns the public squash 34f8bd588e6f1a3edcf3aac3c773d3a0e35af4bf and its branch member cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d. `git log -L 20,27:packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d` attributes the first `new JSONHeroPath(operation.key)` and `path.set(newMetadata, operation.value)` lines to cf80. `git show cf80 -- packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts packages/core/src/v3/schemas/common.ts apps/webapp/app/services/metadata/updateMetadata.server.ts` shows that same commit creates the helper, defines every keyed operation with z.string(), and routes request-body operations into it. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 229707951c66c6796a2ed6ca75872545df9a60c4 -- packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts` prints nothing, while `git show 229707951c66c6796a2ed6ca75872545df9a60c4:packages/core/src/v3/schemas/common.ts` has none of the operation schemas, directly proving parent absence. PR #1563 reports head ad5a3db013086ecb401b36695219d8bd7a835c1e; both it and squash 34f resolve to tree 8dad287dc514d1ec773829ba88e8fb92ef28ab0c, proving the decomposition. `git show cf80:packages/core/package.json` reports package version 3.3.8 and @jsonhero/path ^1.0.21, matching the advisory's lower boundary; repository release tags are slightly different operational evidence: @trigger.dev/core@3.3.8 points to pre-BIC 4243cb2451ebe4c892591f1d0439358c84286988, while the first containing core tag is @trigger.dev/core@3.3.9 at efd61f1374c44eb94b2776dbaaceb2346db9b22c. For closure, `git show 0c2d9ce22a1af5e2ae8d1809cba38051b4acfb1a` shows the focused security-branch change adding isSafeMetadataKey, schema refinements, and a runtime guard that rejects dangerous segments. `git log --reverse cc748422d8188833948035281cc50ef4f7ab77e2..fc392b1fcaa0b929ead6ff8caef2e160f782109e` places 0c2 in PR #4316's security branch; fc392 and public squash 6997 both resolve to tree 73eea7370b72f9e966c5ec0378cec52cf5db89ae. `git tag --contains 6997 --list 'v4.5.*' --sort=version:refname` starts at v4.5.6, and direct `git show v4.5.5:packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts` versus v4.5.6 shows the former unguarded and the latter guarded.
review_record.reasoning: The vulnerability requires both attacker-controlled metadata operation keys and an unsafe path setter; cf80 is the first atomic branch commit that adds that complete causal chain. The later 34f public commit is only a squash representation of cf80 plus unrelated PR members, so treating 34f as the BIC would violate the smallest-real-BIC rule. The immediate cf80 parent lacks both the helper file and operation schemas, and -S/-L independently converge on cf80. The focused fix is 0c2; the advisory-linked 6997 is the public security-release squash that contains it, with v4.5.5/v4.5.6 proving the closing tag boundary. AI attribution is judged only from cf80's raw commit object, which has a human identity and no qualifying AI marker; CodeRabbit activity on the PR and AI-related repository dependencies are outside the BIC commit-object rule and do not change the result.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The Admin Console gadget endpoint passes the request-controlled #{param.gadget} value to gf.getGadgetModule, which accepts a path or complete URL and parses the referenced XML. JSFTemplating then resolves handler input in a context where a resulting #{...} string is evaluated again, while gadget.jsf emits pageSession.gadget.text with escaping disabled. Attacker-controlled gadget XML can therefore inject server-side EL; the unrestricted resolver exposed class/getClass, constructors, static methods, and static fields, making the injection capable of remote code execution.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit ece6ab82e495d2cf87cbf4ec78170727adf2c7f1 is the smallest BIC: it added gadget.jsf and completed the request-reachable path from #{param.gadget} to the pre-existing URL-capable gadget loader and doubly evaluated template content. Commit 16e12748c3def5754a21f3019a1794b899862017 added the loader infrastructure shortly before, but did not expose the gadget.jsf request endpoint. Eclipse root commit 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb is only the later aggregate Initial Contribution carrying the already-vulnerable flow.
audit_record.ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p on the BIC commit object names Ken Paulsen <kenpaulsen@java.net> as author and committer on 2009-07-02; its message contains SVN revision and Former-commit-id provenance but no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.

primary_record.bug_semantics: The Admin Console gadget bootstrap accepts the request-controlled gadget parameter as a URL/path, parses the referenced XML into a GadgetModule, and emits the module text with escaping disabled inside JSFTemplating. review_record.bug_semantics: The Admin Console gadget endpoint embeds the request parameter in gf.getGadgetModule("#{param.gadget}", ...). JSFTemplating Handler.getInputValue resolves that outer expression through ComponentUtil.resolveValue; after param.gadget becomes an attacker string, resolveValue treats a resulting #{...} string as another ValueExpression and evaluates it. Thus a request to the gadget.jsf XML-loader endpoint can make attacker-supplied EL execute server-side before the resulting value is treated as the gadget path/URL. The vulnerable EL resolver allowed class/getClass, static method, constructor, and static-field access, turning the double evaluation into RCE; a cross-site request supplies the UI interaction reflected by CVSS UI:R.

audit_record.bug_semantics: After an administrator authenticates to the GlassFish Administration Console, crafted alertSummary or alertDetail request parameters can enter the shared alertMsg.inc template. The template copies request values into attributes rendered through #{alertSummary} and #{alertDetail}; JSFTemplating then evaluates the expressions with an unrestricted Faces EL resolver chain. Static methods, constructors, getClass()/class traversal, and static fields permit an injected expression to reach java.lang.Runtime and execute operating-system commands as the GlassFish service user. HTML escaping does not prevent the preceding server-side EL evaluation.

review_record.bug_semantics: The authenticated GlassFish Administration Console uses JSFTemplating as its view-description/templating engine. JSFTemplating accepted and evaluated EL from console request processing with the ordinary Faces ELContext and no resolver in front of the standard resolver chain to reject dangerous reflective/static constructs. A crafted authenticated panel request could therefore reach static methods or constructors, getClass()/class traversal, and static fields; an attacker could reach Java process-execution facilities and run operating-system commands as the GlassFish service account. The closing component change installs RestrictedELResolver ahead of PageSessionResolver and rejects ELClass method invocation/constructors, getClass(), the class property, and (in the immediately following hardening commit) static fields.

In eclipse-ee4j/glassfish, root commit 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb is likewise an aggregate 'Initial Contribution' and already pins vulnerable jsftemplating 2.1.3. Neither aggregate is the smallest commit that originally wrote the flaw, and neither has a parent/history from which that commit can be decomposed.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated bot author can store a rich-text link with a javascript: URL. Typebot serializes that author-controlled link and presents it to a visitor as active HTML or, in later viewers, assigns the stored URL directly to an anchor href without validating its protocol. A victim click executes attacker JavaScript in the viewer or embedding host page origin; target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer" do not neutralize a javascript: URL. The assigned advisory snapshot records @typebot.io/js versions below 0.10.1 as vulnerable and 0.10.1 as first patched, and the first-party advisory metadata identifies application versions through 3.15.2 as affected and 3.16.0 as patched.

primary_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated bot author can store a rich-text link whose URL uses the javascript: scheme. primary_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is a stored-XSS lifecycle, not merely the final PlateBlock spelling. Authoring already allowed rich-text links, and the v2 JavaScript viewer first exposed the unsafe stored data in 3487850 by injecting serialized HTML without scheme validation. That exact member commit is smaller and causally prior to the recreated mainline PR carrier. e0a9824 removed redundant html/plainText storage and rewrote rendering to use richText nodes, but its direct href retained the same trust-boundary failure; 765c4b2 later retained it again. Therefore neither refactor is the BIC. Direct inspection of 3487850's parent tree proves the new viewer sink absent, while tree identity with 1a3869 proves how the decomposed member landed. The landed tree precedes the first js-v0.0.1 tag and remains vulnerable through js-v0.10.0. Fix 2c3fc7 applies protocol allowlisting, is exactly js-v0.10.1, and is included in v3.16.0 but not v3.15.2. Finally, attribution is based only on the decomposed BIC commit object: it is authored and committed by Baptiste Arnaud and contains no AI marker. Any AI signal on the later fix cannot attribute the 2022 root cause, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

review_record.bug_semantics: Stored cross-site scripting in Typebot text bubbles: an authenticated bot author can save a rich-text link whose URL uses the javascript: scheme. The stored URL reaches an anchor href without a protocol check; SolidJS leaves that href intact, and a visitor who clicks the link executes attacker JavaScript in the viewer's origin (or the embedding host page's origin), despite target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer". The first-party advisory identifies product versions <=3.15.2 as affected and 3.16.0 as patched; the npm advisory range for @typebot.io/js is <0.10.1 with 0.10.1 first patched.
review_record.flaw_origin: The smallest true first-writer is b7cdc0d14a83891786507f6cdf76339b320461c3 (2021-12-22, Baptiste Arnaud, '🚀 Init preview and typebot cotext in editor'). In one ordinary, single-parent commit it introduced the authoring source (createLinkPlugin plus LinkToolbarButton), serialized editor nodes directly with serializeHtml into content.html, and introduced packages/bot-engine/.../HostMessageBubble.tsx, which rendered that stored HTML with dangerouslySetInnerHTML and no URL-scheme filtering. Later commits changed carriers rather than originating the flaw: 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc introduced the Solid @typebot.io/js viewer with innerHTML={props.content.html}; e0a9824913237cb5340d262770e9e8290fbc4002 replaced stored HTML rendering with an explicit anchor href={props.element.url as string}; cfc5f641a62847ef3b38194d87f89a39daeffabd and 765c4b2f8c1fd4ec610bc81b2547efbda65452ae refactored that unsanitized anchor without closing it.

Carrier checks are reproducible with `git show 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc:packages/js/src/features/blocks/bubbles/textBubble/components/TextBubble.tsx`, `git show e0a9824913237cb5340d262770e9e8290fbc4002 -- packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/bubbles/textBubble`, and `git show 765c4b2f8c1fd4ec610bc81b2547efbda65452ae -- packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/bubbles/textBubble/components/plate/PlateBlock.tsx`. `git show 2c3fc7267a5e1529ba4b1a2ab4f1edb3e3b8990b` creates sanitizeUrl with an http:/https:/mailto:/tel: allowlist, routes text, image, and toast links through it, and bumps @typebot.io/js and @typebot.io/react from 0.10.0 to 0.10.1. review_record.reasoning: The security invariant is protocol validation before a stored author-controlled URL reaches a clickable DOM anchor. b7cdc0d14a83891786507f6cdf76339b320461c3 is earlier than the later Solid and Plate rewrites and is the smallest commit that simultaneously made author-created links storable and rendered their serialized HTML without sanitization; its direct parent has neither that content.html flow nor an __html sink. The intervening commits preserve the same causal source-to-sink failure, so they are carriers/refactors, not BICs. The direct fix closes the invariant at the viewer boundary with a protocol allowlist and is present in both declared patched release lines. Because the verdict must use only the BIC commit object and that object has a human author/committer and no AI attribution, the closed result is NOT_AI; any AI signal on later commits is irrelevant to origin attribution.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The privileged /admin/gateways/test flow performed a security decision on DNS answers obtained while validating the submitted hostname, then gave an httpx-based ResilientHttpClient a URL containing that same hostname. The client therefore performed an independent connection-time resolution. An attacker controlling DNS could return a public address for validation and then rebind the hostname to a private, loopback, link-local, or cloud-metadata address for the actual request, bypassing the SSRF network checks.
audit_record.flaw_origin: PR #3115 member d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934 first inserted SecurityValidator.validate_url(str(request.base_url), ...) into admin_test_gateway while retaining construction of full_url from the validated hostname string and passing that URL to ResilientHttpClient. SecurityValidator._validate_ssrf used socket.getaddrinfo for the check, but the member did not preserve or bind the checked address for the later connection. The repository landed PR #3115 as squash d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f; later allowlist work made the limitation more explicit but did not originate it.

audit_record.evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/security/advisories/GHSA-9hgc-g3w5-67cm describes <1.0.3 as affected and 1.0.3 as first patched, with validation-time socket.getaddrinfo followed by an independent ResilientHttpClient lookup. BIC decomposition: https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/pull/3115.patch exposes seven original members; PATCH 3/7 is d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934, specifically titled 'fix: outbound url validation hardening and behavior consistency'. Its mcpgateway/admin.py hunk at lines 12511-12532 adds SecurityValidator.validate_url and constructs full_url from returned validated_base_url; the same tree at lines 12577-12593 puts full_url in request_kwargs and calls ResilientHttpClient.request. In mcpgateway/common/validators.py, _validate_ssrf resolves the hostname with socket.getaddrinfo and checks the resulting addresses. Immediate-parent verification: git show f1c78d290e2901b4c58ee64e575e049b0f8b2bb3:mcpgateway/admin.py at lines 12508-12535 shows direct construction from request.base_url and no validation-time DNS security decision; git diff f1c78d290e2901b4c58ee64e575e049b0f8b2bb3 d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934 -- mcpgateway/admin.py is the 14-line hunk that first couples the DNS-validating check to the still-hostname-based request. The public squash d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f contains the member's vulnerable flow. Fix verification: git diff ce31d2a84e2c1d0eda5c6c4696e21086bec71fdb fba11a99babd80779fa05510b35fb6a153bbacaf changes validate_gateway_test_url to return validated_url, hostname, and resolved_ip; mcpgateway/admin.py replaces the URL authority with the checked IP, restores the original Host authority, and supplies extensions.sni_hostname, removing the independent hostname lookup from this flow. Commit view: https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/commit/fba11a99babd80779fa05510b35fb6a153bbacaf. Version boundary: git tag --contains d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f includes v1.0.0-RC2, v1.0.0-RC-3, v1.0.0, v1.0.1, and v1.0.2; git merge-base --is-ancestor fba11a99babd80779fa05510b35fb6a153bbacaf v1.0.2 fails, while the same command for v1.0.3 succeeds. git tag --contains fba11a99babd80779fa05510b35fb6a153bbacaf starts at v1.0.3, and v1.0.3:pyproject.toml declares mcp-contextforge-gateway version 1.0.3. Release: https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/releases/tag/v1.0.3.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is not merely that the endpoint could make an outbound request; its defining flaw is the split security transaction introduced when a DNS-resolving SSRF check was added without binding its result to the eventual socket. The decomposed PR history is necessary because public commit d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f aggregates unrelated OAuth, authentication-timing, SSRF, and test work. Original member d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934 is the smallest causal change: it alone adds the gateway-test validation call and then continues to pass the hostname URL to ResilientHttpClient. Its immediate parent f1c78d290e2901b4c58ee64e575e049b0f8b2bb3 has an unrestricted hostname request but not the advisory's check/use DNS race, so the exact vulnerable mechanism is absent there. Later commits 2b5b9e9a145304c466966c560e82d4682849b13a and fb4d9a2616f22dcc64239b250b1c6389b638de4f strengthened allowlisting and documented the known rebinding limitation; they preserved rather than originated the race. Direct fix fba11a99babd80779fa05510b35fb6a153bbacaf carries the checked IP into the actual request while preserving Host and TLS SNI, and its tag ancestry exactly matches the 1.0.3 patched boundary. Finally, the complete d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934 commit object has human identities and no AI authorship marker, so under BIC-only attribution this is a closed NOT_AI result.

review_record.bug_semantics: With the admin API enabled, a database-backed principal holding gateways.read can submit an attacker-controlled hostname to POST /admin/gateways/test. Validation resolves that hostname and rejects private, loopback, link-local, reserved, and metadata addresses, but the accepted URL retains the hostname. ResilientHttpClient/httpx then resolves the hostname again when connecting. An attacker-controlled DNS server can therefore return a public address for the validation lookup and a private or metadata address for the connection lookup, bypassing the SSRF checks and returning internal response content.
review_record.flaw_origin: The exact check/use race first appears in PR #3115 member d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934: it inserted SecurityValidator.validate_url() before the existing gateway-test request, while leaving the outbound request addressed by the validated hostname rather than the checked IP. PR #3115 was squash-landed on the release line as d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f. Later hardening 2b5b9e9a145304c466966c560e82d4682849b13a added an allowlist and an explicit ICACF-15 rebinding TODO, and fb4d9a2616f22dcc64239b250b1c6389b638de4f consolidated validation into validate_gateway_test_url(), but both retained independent connection-time DNS resolution. The race was closed by fba11a99babd80779fa05510b35fb6a153bbacaf, which captures a safe resolved IP, rewrites the dial target to that IP, preserves the original Host authority and TLS SNI, and was released in v1.0.3.

evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/security/advisories/GHSA-9hgc-g3w5-67cm specifies mcp-contextforge-gateway < 1.0.3 as affected and 1.0.3 as first patched, and describes the validation-time socket.getaddrinfo result being discarded before httpx re-resolves the original hostname.

The public PR commit list at https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/pull/3115/commits enumerates seven member commits and identifies d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934 as `fix: outbound url validation hardening and behavior consistency`, with body text `validate admin gateway test base URL before outbound requests`; the squash commit d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f includes that member subject and content.

Run `git diff f1c78d290e2901b4c58ee64e575e049b0f8b2bb3 d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934 -- mcpgateway/admin.py mcpgateway/common/validators.py`: d34f611 adds `validated_base_url = SecurityValidator.validate_url(str(request.base_url), ...)` in admin_test_gateway but leaves the existing ResilientHttpClient request path hostname-based.

Run `git grep -n 'socket.getaddrinfo\|SecurityValidator.validate_url(str(request.base_url)\|request_kwargs = {"method"' d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934 -- mcpgateway/admin.py mcpgateway/common/validators.py`: the check resolves DNS at validators.py:1213, admin.py:12516 invokes it, and admin.py:12579 sends the resulting hostname URL to the client. Those are separate resolution phases.

Direct parent verification: `git grep -n 'SecurityValidator.validate_url(str(request.base_url)' f1c78d290e2901b4c58ee64e575e049b0f8b2bb3 -- mcpgateway/admin.py` has no match, while `git grep -n 'full_url = str(request.base_url)\|request_kwargs = {"method"' f1c78d290e2901b4c58ee64e575e049b0f8b2bb3 -- mcpgateway/admin.py` shows the pre-existing unvalidated request at lines 12514 and 12573. Thus the parent has direct outbound SSRF behavior but not this advisory's DNS validation TOCTOU mechanism; d34f611 is the smallest member that creates the check/use race.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated static-download route passes request.getParameter("version") into BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension without validating it. For a request to the route base (/file/static/noauth in the renamed endpoint, formerly /downloadFile/static/noauth), the path-derived fileName is "noauth", whose full-path component is empty, so the helper replaces it entirely with attacker-controlled version. A value such as ../../etc/passwd is then handed to FileUtils.readFile(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName, ...), which constructs new File(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName) and can escape the intended download directory, exposing arbitrary readable files without authentication.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46 added version as a cache/content-identity filename override during a resources/web-client refactor. The normal producer generated an ID for version, but DownloadFileRequestHandler treated the HTTP parameter as if it were trusted and reused it as a filesystem child path. The already-existing security rule exempted /downloadFile/static/noauth/** from authentication, making this new trust-boundary error remotely reachable immediately.

review_record.bug_semantics: DownloadFileRequestHandler derives fileName from the /file/* path, then accepts the request's version parameter and passes it unchanged to BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension. That helper returns FilenameUtils.getFullPath(fileName) + version, and FileUtils.readFile/createFile ultimately opens new File(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName) without canonical containment checking. On the unauthenticated /file/static/noauth/** route, a request to /file/static/noauth with a version such as ../../... therefore replaces the benign basename with a traversal path and reads a server file outside the download folder.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46 first added both the unsafe replaceFileNameAndExtension helper and the three handler lines that read the untrusted version parameter and replace fileName without validation. Commit 87b7b9e81d8ebdf52b0480cfcad78c5817603883 later exposed /downloadFile/static/noauth/** without authentication, and 256ae9dcb19d8762b1cb43f2d1e688d46592581c renamed that public endpoint to the advisory's /file/static/noauth/**; these later exposure/rename commits did not write the unsafe version-to-path logic and are not the BIC.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The remotely reachable /uploadFile multipart handler parsed an uploaded FileItem and constructed its destination name by concatenating the request-controlled sid, an underscore, and the client-controlled upload filename beneath an intended temporary upload directory. Because sid was not validated and the resulting path was not canonicalized or checked for containment, ../ segments in sid escaped the upload directory; an attacker could select the uploaded bytes and filename (for example a JSP) and place the file in a web-accessible location.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 7436c2f0b67128a558e3ac3a820ef8e0a01f59c0 introduced the /uploadFile servlet mapping and the first upload handler in one feature commit. Its new UploadFileHandler passed request.getParameter("sid") + "_" + item.getName() directly to a java.io.File rooted at WEB-INF/temp and wrote attacker bytes there. Later package moves and the 2022 conversion to FileUtils.writeFile preserved the same unvalidated path composition, so they are not origins of the flaw.

review_record.bug_semantics: The remotely reachable /uploadFile multipart handler used the request-controlled sid and uploaded item name as the child path below its upload directory without validating or canonicalizing either value. A sid containing parent-directory components therefore escaped the intended upload directory; choosing a JSP upload name let an unauthenticated attacker place executable content in a web-accessible location and then request it.

audit_record.bug_semantics: ZPan initialized its process-wide HS512 JWT helper with the public constant "123". A remote attacker who knows that repository-visible secret can sign a z-token whose subject and roles claim an administrator identity; LoginAuthWithRoles accepts the signature and then authorizes protected API routes from the attacker-controlled roles, bypassing password authentication.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 added the new user/token authentication subsystem. Its newly created internal/app/service/token.go made NewToken call jwtutil.Init("123") and used that same global helper to issue and verify RoleClaims; the same commit added the cookie-to-roles authentication middleware and protected-route role checks. The hard-coded signing key, rather than a per-installation secret, is therefore part of the original implementation of this authentication mechanism, not a later move or refactor of pre-existing vulnerable lines.
audit_record.ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object for 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 names human author and committer saltbo <saltbo@foxmail.com>, contains only the subject "refactor: remove the moreu depend && add user supports", and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
audit_record.evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/saltbo/zpan/issues/219 identifies internal/app/service/token.go:16, HS512 key "123", and demonstrates a forged administrator z-token against a protected system-options endpoint; the maintainer links PR #410, commit 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947, and release v1.6.6 as the fix. `git log -L '/func NewToken()/,+5':internal/app/service/token.go 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947^` traces `jwtutil.Init("123")` to 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5. An all-history `git log -S 'jwtutil.Init("123")' --pickaxe-all --find-renames -- '*.go'` finds that addition, the later v2 reset removal, and the v1 security fix, with no earlier writer. Direct diff 3de132e2248fa8257f5e0dc2aa688bff8f94418c..4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 shows internal/app/service/token.go created from /dev/null with NewToken, Create, Verify, and RoleClaims; `git ls-tree` shows that path absent in the immediate parent, while `git grep` of the parent finds neither the exact hard-coded initializer nor an earlier equivalent user-token signing setup. `git tag --contains 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5` begins at v1.5.0 (v1.4.1 predates the BIC) and includes v1.6.5 and v1.7.0-beta2. Tag-tree greps confirm the exact hard-coded initializer in v1.5.0, v1.6.5, and v1.7.0-beta2. The advisory package range is <1.6.6 with first patched version 1.6.6; tag v1.6.6 points exactly to 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947, whose sole parent is the v1.6.5 commit 33eec01e971f206356c76df79c4148e3f8d1752f. Its direct diff replaces `jwtutil.Init("123")` with `jwtutil.Init(JWTSecret())`, generates 32 random bytes, persists `security.jwt_secret` for new and upgraded installations, and uses that configured key for share-token issue/verification as well. `git cat-file -p 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5` supplies the BIC-only authorship/trailer evidence used for attribution.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is exploitable because HS512 is symmetric: knowledge of the constant signing key is enough to mint a structurally valid token with arbitrary administrator roles, and the middleware derives authorization from claims after verifying them with that same constant. History analysis chooses 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 rather than a later release, reset, or fix because it is the first commit to write both the exact weak-key initializer and the new authentication path that consumes attacker-forgeable role claims. Although its subject says refactor and the commit moves many unrelated files, token.go and the user-token authentication mechanism are new additions; exact-string pickaxe and line history expose no earlier vulnerable source to follow, so there is no smaller prior BIC to decompose. The immediate parent tree lacks both token.go and the hard-coded initializer, establishing parent absence. The BIC is included from v1.5.0 onward, the constant remains in the reported v1.6.5 and v1.7.0-beta2 trees, and the v1.6.6 tag is the direct fixing commit on top of v1.6.5, satisfying the affected/patched boundary. Finally, attribution is based only on the raw BIC commit object: it records a human author/committer and no AI marker. Under the protocol, the closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI.

review_record.bug_semantics: ZPan v1's Token constructor globally initialized jwtutil with the literal HMAC signing secret "123". The same utility issued and verified RoleClaims containing attacker-relevant Subject and Roles fields, and LoginAuth trusted a verified z-token cookie for identity and RBAC. Anyone knowing the repository value could therefore sign an HS512 token claiming an arbitrary uid and the admin role and remotely reach administrator-only APIs; issue #219 demonstrates GET /api/system/options/core.email with a forged admin cookie.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 (saltbo, 2021-02-01, 'refactor: remove the moreu depend && add user supports') is the smallest true first-writer. It created internal/app/service/token.go with NewToken calling jwtutil.Init("123"), plus the new user-token and LoginAuth flow that consumed it. This was not a move of the vulnerable line: its sole parent 3de132e2248fa8257f5e0dc2aa688bff8f94418c has no internal/app/service/token.go and no jwtutil.Init call.
review_record.ai_marker: BIC commit-object check only: `git cat-file -p 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5` records author and committer `saltbo <saltbo@foxmail.com>`, one parent, a GPG signature, and only the subject `refactor: remove the moreu depend && add user supports`; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity. The Claude Co-Authored-By trailer on later v2 reset/deletion commit b817cab2c1627d9cadc2239492d9b5c16afc1c59 is not on the BIC and is excluded.
review_record.evidence: In the assigned clone, `git log -L '/func NewToken/',+4:internal/app/service/token.go 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947^` resolves the complete vulnerable constructor to 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 and shows its /dev/null-to-file hunk containing `jwtutil.Init("123")`; `git log --all -S'jwtutil.Init("123")' -- internal/app/service/token.go` independently shows the lifecycle as the 4fae6e2 addition, b817cab2 deletion during the v2 repository reset, and 8662db8 replacement. Direct parent verification is reproducible with `git cat-file -e 3de132e2248fa8257f5e0dc2aa688bff8f94418c:internal/app/service/token.go` (fatal: path does not exist) and `git grep -n -F 'jwtutil.Init' 3de132e2248fa8257f5e0dc2aa688bff8f94418c -- '*.go'` (no match). At v1.6.5, internal/app/service/token.go initializes `123`, service/user.go uses that Token for issue/verify, internal/pkg/authed/authed.go reads cookie `z-token`, internal/pkg/middleware/auth.go verifies it and trusts its Subject/Roles, and auth_rbac.yml restricts `/api/system/options/core.email` to admin. First-party issue https://github.com/saltbo/zpan/issues/219 identifies HS512, supplies a forged admin z-token, and demonstrates that endpoint. Tag checks with `git grep -n -F 'jwtutil.Init("123")' <tag> -- '*.go'` find no match in v1.4.1, but find the line in v1.5.0, v1.6.5, and v1.7.0-beta2; thus the repository's first vulnerable release is v1.5.0, the last v1.6 release before the patch is v1.6.5, and the historical beta2 tag also carries the flaw. `git show 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947 -- internal/app/service/token.go cmd/root.go` directly replaces `jwtutil.Init("123")` with `jwtutil.Init(JWTSecret())`, generates a random 32-byte per-installation `security.jwt_secret`, persists it for installs/upgrades, and rejects missing installed configuration. The fix is a one-parent commit whose parent is exactly v1.6.5 commit 33eec01e971f206356c76df79c4148e3f8d1752f; lightweight tag v1.6.6 resolves exactly to 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947. PR #410 and the v1.6.6 release both identify that commit/release as the direct patch and recommend v2 for the retired v1 line.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An attacker-controlled archive entry name was appended to a temporary extraction-directory path and opened for output without canonical normalization or a containment check. A traversal entry could therefore escape the staging directory, overwrite a server-writable file, and then have that escaped file deleted by cleanup. The advisory PoC exercises ZIP through ZipUtils.unpackFile; the same unchecked construction also existed in the sibling RAR path and was reachable from configured EmailReceiver unpacking and MakeUnzipFileAction.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827 first created an affected lifecycle by adding opt-in archive unpacking to EmailReceiver and writing ZIP and RAR entry names directly beneath an output-directory string. Commit ce3cf594f118e720279abdb78116a597956bbe41 later added the same unsafe mechanism to MakeUnzipFileAction. Commit 4950d66839375b11a4706fe1b5bd5f28ec9abf17 merely centralized the existing implementations in ZipUtils and routed both callers to it, so that move/refactor is not the BIC.
audit_record.ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827` shows human author and committer Vandrouny <filipchyk.andrei@gmail.com>, one parent, and only the subject `[server] Опция распаковки архивов при приёме почты`; it contains no AI/bot identity, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer.
audit_record.evidence: The assigned fix_sha disagreement was primary 547f9c92df24969fb34f6d7009bfeb3d7727c67a versus reviewer 90d058b9007c1e9b0babc0aac50fe2f292fb947d. The reviewer wins. `git show 1aefa1fd67bb644e6d4f5682051fc85b81048322 -- ZipUtils.java` shows the March source patch only wrapping ZIP file entries in `!filePath.contains("../")`; `git show 547f9c92df24969fb34f6d7009bfeb3d7727c67a` records that it is a cherry-pick of 1aefa1fd67bb644e6d4f5682051fc85b81048322, and stable patch-id gives the same 4ba1c5411569c90ccac57099811a1285acbe05db for both. That partial check does not cover backslash traversal on Windows, ZIP directory entries, or the manual RAR output path. `git show 90d058b9007c1e9b0babc0aac50fe2f292fb947d -- ZipUtils.java` replaces the string test with canonical-path `isInsideDirectory` checks on ZIP files, ZIP directories, and RAR entries. `git log --all --reverse -S'isInsideDirectory' -- ZipUtils.java` returns only 90d058b9007c1e9b0babc0aac50fe2f292fb947d; its direct parent bc091770fd0f86050a0056b375d40728166fb423 still has only `contains("../")`. Although 90d058b9 also updates junrar, it is a one-parent directly authored commit, not an import, merge, move, or squash aggregate, and it is the smallest repository commit that introduces the complete containment fix. For the version boundary, `git merge-base --is-ancestor 557102b69a04a7476d244d4ea6f9c24c29e55827 6.1` succeeds; 547f9c92 is absent from 6.1 and present in 6.2, while 90d058b9 is not an ancestor of 6.2 and `git tag --contains 90d058b9` returns no tag. audit_record.bug_semantics: Penpot MCP automatically started an Express ReplServer whose POST /execute route accepted an unauthenticated JSON code string and sent it through PluginBridge as an ExecuteCodePluginTask; the plugin handler evaluated that string with new Function in a context exposing the Penpot API, storage, console, and PenpotUtils. ReplServer called app.listen(this.port) without a host, so Node/Express listened on all interfaces rather than loopback. Consequently, an unauthenticated adjacent-network peer that could reach port 4403 could cause arbitrary JavaScript execution in the connected Penpot plugin context.

review_record.bug_semantics: The MCP ReplServer creates an Express POST /execute route with no authentication. The handler accepts a JSON code string, wraps it in ExecuteCodePluginTask, and sends it through PluginBridge.executePluginTask, so the supplied JavaScript executes in the MCP process. ReplServer.start originally called app.listen(this.port) without a host; Node/Express therefore listened on the unspecified/all-interfaces address rather than loopback. An unauthenticated adjacent-network client able to reach port 4403 could execute arbitrary code with the MCP process's filesystem, environment, command-execution, and availability privileges. Merely securing the main PenpotMcpServer listener did not secure this separate Express listener.
review_record.flaw_origin: The vulnerable behavior originated in the former first-party penpot/penpot-mcp repository at 8552bb4183fc1479c8436c1ccec2868ea221d498 (Add REPL server): that one focused commit first created ReplServer.ts, the unauthenticated /execute route, and app.listen(this.port) without a host. Its parent ad771ee92fbbf36b2d3b515e1a16e551a39cc986 has no ReplServer.ts. Later source commits moved the inline HTML, changed REPL presentation, and changed configuration/logging but retained both security-relevant behaviors. Penpot commit 880b9b61c41f977f4ddf8463ab6ab62194acb077 is a 30,118-line aggregate import whose commit object identifies source repository https://github.com/penpot/penpot-mcp and imported tip fcfa67e908fc54e23a3a3543dee432472dc90c5d; c14ccc18b8c50f21bd581fc662503ac5444df0cf then imported the same vulnerable ReplServer blob into the release line. Those import commits are not the smallest BIC and were decomposed through the referenced source history.

The company email domain text `oraios-ai.de` is not a generation disclosure or bot identity.

The assigned bundle records npm @penpot/mcp vulnerable range < 2.15.0 and first patched version 2.15.0.

In the validated penpot clone, `git cat-file commit 880b9b61c41f977f4ddf8463ab6ab62194acb077` says `Original repository: https://github.com/penpot/penpot-mcp` and `Imported commit: fcfa67e908fc54e23a3a3543dee432472dc90c5d`. `git show --stat 880b9...` shows a 70-file, 30,118-insertion aggregate, including a new ReplServer.ts, so 880b9 is an import boundary rather than the smallest original write.

"localhost"' -- PenpotMcpServer.ts` finds the later localhost-default work, including 4e3dc6532a314f3411b193a4e40b3a8b98adad9b, while ReplServer remained separately exposed, matching the advisory's missed-server account.

audit_record.bug_semantics: A remote ActivityPub Create/Note can supply an Emoji tag whose icon.url and name are attacker-controlled. NodeBB converted a matching shortcode into an img element by interpolating those values into quoted HTML attributes after the original note content had already been sanitized, then stored the generated HTML. Remote-post rendering could bypass markdown/sanitize-html, so an attribute breakout in the generated markup became persistent same-origin JavaScript for viewers.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 introduced incoming ActivityPub emoji expansion in src/posts/create.js before database storage and first wrote the causal unescaped sink, interpolating tag.icon.url directly into img src. Commit 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 added the unescaped title attribute from tag.name one day later. review_record.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated federated ActivityPub server can send a Create/Note whose sanitized content contains an emoji shortcode and whose attacker-controlled Emoji tag supplies icon.url and name. NodeBB replaces the shortcode after the content sanitization pass with an HTML img string containing those values in quoted attributes, then stores that generated HTML. The first exploitable sink interpolated icon.url; commit 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 subsequently added the unescaped title from tag.name.
review_record.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6: it first added the incoming ActivityPub emoji rewrite to src/posts/create.js and directly interpolated tag.icon.url into an img src immediately before post storage. Its parent has no emoji rewrite or tag.icon.url use in that file. Commit 9608cce693d43579b54ef2500133f0630f7a96c3 is only a later refactor that moved the already-vulnerable construction into Helpers.renderEmoji, so it is not the BIC.

audit_record.bug_semantics: deepExtend() enumerated attacker-controlled own keys and used Reflect.has() on the merge receiver. For a JSON-parsed __proto__ key, Reflect.has({}, '__proto__') is true through Object.prototype's inherited accessor; because both resolved values are objects, the recursive branch calls extendObject(Object.prototype, attackerValue), and the attacker's nested keys are then assigned onto Object.prototype. Every subsequently created ordinary object inherits the injected properties, enabling application-dependent integrity, availability, or authorization failures wherever untrusted data reaches deepExtend().
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 changed the receiver test from !o1.hasOwnProperty(key) to !Reflect.has(o1, key) while retaining recursive merging and no forbidden-key filter. That semantic change made inherited __proto__ look like an existing object-valued destination and redirected recursion into Object.prototype. Earlier code could alter the returned object's own prototype via __proto__ assignment, but the advisory's realm-wide Object.prototype write primitive was absent until this commit.

review_record.bug_semantics: @cleverbrush/deep deepExtend recursively copies every enumerable source key into a fresh ordinary object without rejecting __proto__. From ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 onward, the merge loop uses Reflect.has(o1, key). For attacker-controlled JSON containing an own __proto__ object, Reflect.has sees the inherited __proto__ accessor on an ordinary target; o1[key] resolves to Object.prototype, both sides satisfy the object checks, and extendObject recurses into Object.prototype. Attacker-chosen inner properties are then assigned as own properties of Object.prototype and become inherited by every ordinary object in the realm. An application reaches the sink by passing parsed request/config/query data to deepExtend; the resulting realm-wide inherited values can corrupt authorization or configuration logic, cause denial of service, or feed a secondary gadget. The disclosed working route is __proto__; constructor is a function on the ordinary receiver and therefore does not take this recursion branch, although the closing defense rejects __proto__, constructor, and prototype.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated Project Manager or Owner can store a repository git_url beginning with Git's --upload-pack= option. The server-side schedule commit-hash poller passes that value directly after `git ls-remote` without an end-of-options delimiter; Git parses it as an option and invokes the attacker-selected upload-pack command through a shell, yielding command execution in the Semaphore server process.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f changed GetLastRemoteCommitHash from running `git ls-remote origin <branch>` in the already-cloned repository to running `git ls-remote <Repository.GetGitURL()> <branch>` in the temporary directory. review_record.bug_semantics: Authenticated Project Managers or Owners can store an attacker-controlled repository git_url beginning with a Git option such as --upload-pack=... . With the default cmd_git client, the server-side schedule commit-hash poller passes that value to git ls-remote before the repository operand and without --end-of-options. Git interprets it as an option and invokes the supplied upload-pack command through a shell, yielding command execution in the Semaphore server process. Repository validation checked only that GitURL was nonempty while branch validation did not delimit the URL argument.
review_record.flaw_origin: The exploitable schedule-poller data flow was introduced by a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f (fix(be): bug with getting remote commit), which changed GetLastRemoteCommitHash from git ls-remote origin <branch> in a repository directory to git ls-remote <Repository.GetGitURL()> <branch> in the temporary directory. This was the first write that put attacker-controlled GitURL into the ls-remote option-parsing position; later file moves and client refactors only preserved it.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The MCP approval-request entry point accepts caller-controlled categoryName and passes it unchanged to ApprovalStorage.createApproval(). That method formed categoryDir with join(this.approvalsDir, categoryName), recursively created the resulting directory, and wrote the approval JSON beneath it. A categoryName containing parent-directory components and directory separators could therefore normalize outside .spec-workflow/approvals and cause a local caller to create or overwrite an approval JSON outside the intended storage tree.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The repository's root commit introduced the complete vulnerable path in one public commit: request-approval exposed categoryName in the MCP input schema and forwarded args.categoryName to createApproval, while createApproval used the value as a filesystem path component without validation or a containment check before mkdir and writeFile. Later refactors preserved that mechanism; they did not originate it.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An initialized XKB client can first grow xkb->map->num_types to 255 with a SetMap request carrying XkbSetMapResizeTypes, then send firstType=255 and nTypes=10. audit_record.bug_semantics: A remote caller could supply an arbitrary HTTP(S) target in GET /api's url query parameter. PullMD passed that value to its server-side web extractor and returned the fetched content without rejecting loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, or cloud-metadata destinations or revalidating redirect targets, so a request such as /api?url=http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data could disclose cloud instance metadata and reach other internal services.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The root release commit wired req.query.url directly from server.js into extractWebFn(url), while lib/web.js wrapped globalThis.fetch only with a timeout and then called fetchFn(url, { headers }). It added no URL-scheme, hostname, DNS-result, IP-range, or redirect-hop policy between attacker input and the outbound request; that unsafe fetch design, rather than a later refactor or move, is the causal origin.

At BIC 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d, server.js:164-170 creates GET /api and reads req.query.url with only a presence check, server.js:288-290 calls extractWebFn(url), and lib/web.js:164-174 selects globalThis.fetch, adds only timeout handling, and fetches the supplied URL. git log -S'const res = await fetchFn(url, { headers });' --all --reverse -- lib/web.js returns only 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d; git log -L 505,506:lib/web.js and -L 519,519:lib/web.js from vulnerable tag commit 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5 both trace the fetch setup/call to root commit 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d. git rev-list --parents -n 1 on the BIC prints only the BIC SHA, proving it has no parent; git diff-tree --root --name-status shows both server.js and lib/web.js as A against the empty pre-root tree, directly proving the vulnerable path was absent before it. The BIC's package.json is version 1.0.0, git tag --contains the BIC includes v1.0.0 through vulnerable v3.2.0, v3.2.0 resolves to 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5, and v3.3.0 resolves exactly to fix 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e; git tag --contains the fix starts at v3.3.0 and excludes v3.2.0. The fix directly adds lib/ssrf.js, validates the URL before /api cache access, wraps the web fetch with redirect-hop validation, covers MCP/Reddit/Playwright paths, and bumps package.json from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0.
audit_record.reasoning: The disclosed attack path is causal and direct: attacker-controlled req.query.url enters GET /api, survives only a non-empty check, reaches extractWebFn, and becomes the destination of Node's outbound fetch; the response is converted and returned. The v3.2.0 tree still blames the decisive unchecked fetch setup and call to 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d, and both -S and -L history identify that root commit as the first writer rather than any later orchestration, auth, release, move, or refactor commit. review_record.bug_semantics: A caller able to reach GET /api could supply an arbitrary http(s) url. The route passed that value into extractWeb, whose timeout wrapper called the server's fetch implementation directly, with no destination-address validation and ordinary redirect behavior. PullMD could therefore request loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, or cloud-metadata resources from its own network position and return the retrieved content as Markdown; the reported concrete payload targeted Alibaba-style metadata at http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data. The same unguarded extraction primitive was also reachable from MCP read_url and stale-share refresh paths.
review_record.flaw_origin: Public-history root commit 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d, 'Initial public release', created server.js with app.get('/api') forwarding req.query.url to extractWebFn and created lib/web.js with extractWeb wrapping globalThis.fetch and executing await fetchFn(url, { headers }) without any scheme, DNS, address-range, or redirect-hop guard. It also created the MCP read_url caller. This is the first and smallest Git commit object that writes the vulnerable route/sink in the available repository: git -L and -S both terminate at that root, and the root has no parent object to contain the lines. It is not a later move, refactor, revert, release carrier, or identifiable squash carrier; there are no member commits in the available history to decompose.

evidence: First-party report https://github.com/AeternaLabsHQ/pullmd/issues/41 gives the exact request `/api?url=http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data`, says PullMD fetched and returned metadata User-Data, and records the maintainer's closure in v3.3.0/#42. First-party PR https://github.com/AeternaLabsHQ/pullmd/pull/42 states that GET /api and MCP read_url accepted user URLs without address validation and identifies private/metadata access and redirect hopping as the repaired mechanism.

In the read-only clone, `git show 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d:server.js` shows the new `app.get('/api', ...)`, `const { url, ... } = req.query`, and non-Reddit `await extractWebFn(url, { comments: false })`. `git show 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d:lib/web.js` shows `const rawFetchFn = options.fetch || globalThis.fetch`, `const fetchFn = withTimeout(rawFetchFn)`, and `const res = await fetchFn(url, { headers })`, with no SSRF validation. The same root's lib/mcp.js registers read_url and calls extractWeb(url, ...).

Origin cross-check: `git log -L 519,519:lib/web.js 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5 --format='commit %H%nparents %P%nsubject %s'` attributes the fetch statement's addition from /dev/null solely to 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d. Independently, `git log --all -S'await fetchFn(url, { headers })' --format='%H %P %s' -- lib/web.js` returns only that root commit. `git log --all -S'const fetchFn = withTimeout(rawFetchFn)' ... -- lib/web.js` returns the root addition and the eventual removal in the fix.

Direct parent verification: `git rev-list --parents -n 1 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d` prints only the commit SHA, and raw `git cat-file -p` contains no `parent` header. Thus introducer_parent is null and introducer_parent_absent is true because the verified BIC is the repository root; there is no parent tree in which the vulnerable lines could exist.

Fix reversal: `git show 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e -- lib/web.js server.js lib/mcp.js lib/playwright-client.js lib/reddit.js lib/ssrf.js` shows direct security changes: new assertUrlAllowed/safeFetch guards, safeFetch wrapping the main web fetch and manually validating every redirect hop, a pre-cache 403 guard on /api, MCP error handling, and guards before Reddit short-link and Playwright sidecar dispatch. The commit has sole parent 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are the same direct patch commit.

Version boundary: `git show 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d:package.json` reports version 1.0.0. `git show-ref --tags v1.0.0 v3.2.0 v3.3.0` resolves those tags to 0d6912e562def8d03e9a085b9c5079423366678f, 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5, and 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e respectively. `git tag --contains 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d --sort=version:refname` includes every release from v1.0.0 onward, while `git tag --contains 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e --sort=version:refname` starts at v3.3.0. Together with the -S transition, this proves the vulnerable implementation persisted through v3.2.0 and the guard first shipped in v3.3.0.

BIC-only AI check: raw `git cat-file -p 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d` is exactly a tree header, human author/committer lines for syswave-dev, a blank separator, and `Initial public release`; it has no AI trailer or bot identity. No PR-body, branch-name, later-refactor, or fix-only AI disclosure is used for the verdict.
review_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is the trust-boundary failure at the original server-side URL fetch: an attacker-controlled URL was fetched from the deployment's network context without resolving and rejecting internal destinations or rechecking redirects. Both first-party disclosure and the direct patch identify that same mechanism. Provenance checks do not stop at the advisory's v3.2.0 snapshot: -L and -S trace the unsafe fetch to the repository's parentless root, whose package version was already 1.0.0, and the code remains unsafe until 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e replaces the raw wrapper with safeFetch and adds entry-point guards. The fix is tagged v3.3.0 and its parent is exactly tagged v3.2.0. Because the verified BIC commit object has a human identity and no AI marker, the only protocol-compliant closed judgment is NOT_AI; AI information outside the BIC commit object is intentionally excluded.

audit_record.bug_semantics: When AUTH_ENABLED=true, an external request from outside INTERNAL_SERVICE_IPS that omits X-Internal-Service receives None from request.headers.get(), while an unset INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET also yields None from os.getenv(). is_internal_request() compared those values directly, so None == None returned true; verify_api_key() then created an unauthenticated internal principal with scopes ["all"], satisfying require_scope("admin") and exposing admin key creation, listing, and revocation. The bypass does not by itself pass the generate-master-key handler's additional is_master_key check.

GitHub squash commit 658eb3d171df7a038a1b93c799c77dd430ac4671 integrated that member unchanged; 58363aac03acf347bbb74861d0ce1108f345faf4 only simplified the if/return form, and c2bc36b15f818babca5a7c1e787ce86d60341fb0 later performed a 100% rename into src/memos/api/middleware/auth.py, so neither is the introducer.

review_record.bug_semantics: When AUTH_ENABLED=true, is_internal_request() checks an external request's optional X-Internal-Service header against the defaultless INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET with direct equality. If the environment variable is unset and the attacker omits the header, both lookups return None, so None == None is true. verify_api_key() then returns the trusted internal principal with scopes ["all"] before requiring an API key; that scope satisfies require_scope("admin") and permits unauthenticated creation (including admin-scoped keys), enumeration, and revocation of API keys. The /admin/generate-master-key route is not itself reachable through this bypass because it additionally requires is_master_key=true, contrary to that part of the issue/advisory impact wording.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated proxy client can put an arbitrary HTTP(S) origin in x-headroom-base-url. Headroom uses that origin as the upstream without establishing that its resolved addresses are public, forwards the incoming request headers and body to it, and returns the upstream response. A caller can therefore reach loopback, link-local/cloud-metadata, RFC 1918, and other internal services through the proxy and read their responses; the incoming Authorization header also follows the caller-selected destination. The reference compose deployment amplified reachability by publishing the proxy on 0.0.0.0 without requiring HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f introduced the trust-boundary violation in headroom/proxy/server.py: the catch-all route read x-headroom-base-url and immediately passed custom_base.rstrip('/') to the pre-existing handle_passthrough method. That method copied all request headers except Host into the outbound request and relayed the response content/status/headers. The commit added no scheme, hostname, address-class, DNS, or operator-allowlist validation. Later commits moved the same catch-all mechanism and expanded it to dedicated OpenAI handlers; they did not originate the already exploitable SSRF.

At the same tree, headroom/proxy/server.py:4294-4353 shows handle_passthrough constructing url = f'{base_url}{path}', copying dict(request.headers.items()), removing only Host, calling http_client.request(... headers=headers ...), then returning response.content/status/headers. audit_record.reasoning: The causal root is the first client-controlled destination selection, not the current file attribution. Commit 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f made a request header authoritative over the outbound origin while reusing a passthrough routine that forwards headers and discloses the response. Direct inspection of its immediate parent proves the header mechanism was absent. Later extraction/restoration and line-ending commits merely carried that behavior into provider routes; c19347c31046bf25baf9b1a816c9bede5d3ee807 broadened it to dedicated OpenAI routes. In particular, the Copilot-attributed 49a8f80e9b7c14c8e913e6160851f6f8fa8e0b3d is excluded because its relevant change is normalization of already-existing route code. The release graph is coherent: the origin lies between v0.3.0 and v0.3.7, is an ancestor of the assessed v0.29.0, and the complete fix lands only in v0.36.4 after the partial v0.36.1 guard missed one sink. BIC-only commit-object review finds a human author/committer and no AI marker on 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f. AI disclosure in fix PR bodies, the Claude trailer on the complete fix, and the later Copilot normalization cannot attribute the root cause. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

review_record.bug_semantics: CWE-918 SSRF: an unauthenticated proxy caller could supply x-headroom-base-url and make Headroom issue the request to a caller-selected http(s) destination. The original catch-all route passed that value directly to handle_passthrough, which appended the inbound path, copied all inbound headers except Host (including Authorization), sent the request with httpx, and returned the upstream response. Later OpenAI and Azure/passthrough resolution paths preserved the same trust error. Without rejecting loopback, link-local, RFC1918, metadata, or other non-public addresses, a remotely exposed proxy could disclose internal-service responses and forward caller credentials to the chosen host.
review_record.flaw_origin: 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f is the smallest first-writer. It added the x-headroom-base-url catch-all override in headroom/proxy/server.py and immediately passed custom_base.rstrip('/') to handle_passthrough without destination validation. The later b17c6d81cc39676f322779dc2e5695cba28b8e65 extraction into headroom/providers/proxy_routes.py, 7d747306066de6ed9f2635b58860f7d85fdf6362 compatibility work, and c19347c31046bf25baf9b1a816c9bede5d3ee807 OpenAI resolver are lifecycle moves/extensions, not the BIC.

audit_record.bug_semantics: On a glamor-backed X server, glamor_font_get() sized a CPU-side font-atlas heap buffer and each glyph slot from the font's declared maxbounds, but copied each bitmap using that glyph's unchecked GLYPHWIDTHBYTES and GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS metrics. libXfont2's PCF parser did not recompute maxbounds from the per-glyph records, so an authenticated X client could supply a PCF whose individual metrics exceeded (or were negative relative to) maxbounds; drawing text then made the row memcpy write attacker-controlled bytes beyond the allocated atlas, with negative values also permitting unsigned/size_t wrap.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f changed glamor_font_get() from issuing one glTexSubImage2D call per glyph to building one CPU heap staging atlas. review_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated X client can use SetFontPath to expose a crafted PCF font, OpenFont to load it, and text drawing on a glamor-backed drawable to reach glamor_font_get(). The function sizes each heap-atlas slot from the PCF-declared font maxbounds but, before the fix, copied each glyph using the untrusted per-glyph GLYPHWIDTHBYTES and GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS values without checking that they fit the slot. Because libXfont2's PCF parser does not recompute maxbounds from the glyph metrics, an oversized glyph writes attacker-controlled bytes beyond the heap allocation; negative width or height can also wrap the memcpy size or unsigned loop bound. Only glamor-backed Xorg/Xwayland servers are on this path.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f replaced one glTexSubImage2D upload per glyph with a CPU-side atlas: it allocated bits using overall_width * overall_height derived from maxbounds, then introduced a row loop whose memcpy length and iteration count came directly from each glyph. That newly combined mismatched allocation/copy geometry is the smallest source change that created the reported heap overflow.
review_record.ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f` shows human author Michel Dänzer, human committer Keith Packard, Reviewed-by and Signed-off-by trailers only; it has no Co-Authored-By, Assisted-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI disclosure.
evidence: First-party X.Org security announcement https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/07/08/2 names CVE-2026-55999, describes the maxbounds/per-glyph mismatch and SetFontPath -> OpenFont -> glamor drawing attack path, identifies glamor-backed Xorg and Xwayland as affected, names fbf7bac22e2c6bd627fb042742a23318263edae1 as the fix, and states fixed releases xorg-server-21.1.24 and xwayland-24.1.13.

In the assigned clone, `git show --format=fuller --no-renames fbf7bac22e2c6bd627fb042742a23318263edae1 -- glamor/glamor_font.c` shows the direct repair: reject non-positive maxbounds dimensions; compute gw/gh once; reject negative per-glyph dimensions or gw > glyph_width_bytes / gh > glyph_height; otherwise use the checked values in the loop and memcpy. The commit message independently explains that PCF maxbounds are trusted and that malformed per-glyph dimensions overflow or wrap.

`git log -L ':glamor_font_get:glamor/glamor_font.c' fbf7bac22e2c6bd627fb042742a23318263edae1^` traces the vulnerable atlas allocation/copy back to 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f. `git log --all -S'memcpy(dst, src, GLYPHWIDTHBYTES(glyph))' -- glamor/glamor_font.c` independently identifies that commit on main history (alongside equivalent objects on other refs) as the addition of the exact unchecked memcpy and the 2026 fixes as its removal.

`git show --format=fuller --no-renames 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f` shows the BIC adding `bits = malloc(overall_width * overall_height)` and replacing the parent's glTexSubImage2D call with `for (y = 0; y < GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS(glyph); y++) memcpy(dst, src, GLYPHWIDTHBYTES(glyph))`, while the atlas dimensions remain derived from maxbounds. The commit is a focused performance change, not a move, revert, backport, merge, or squash aggregate.

audit_record.bug_semantics: When the optional webhook server is enabled, it listens on all interfaces and accepts POST requests containing an attacker-controlled exec string. Authentication is fail-open: WebhookServer.authenticate returns true whenever the configured token is empty, a state the configuration comments explicitly describe as 'empty = no auth'. The handler then dispatches req.Exec to a shell with -c/-Command. Thus an attacker who supplies a nonempty, reconstructable session_key (and a project when multiple projects are configured) can execute an arbitrary shell program as the cc-connect process without a credential. The shell interpretation of exec is an intentional feature; the security failure is exposing that full shell capability across a network endpoint while treating an omitted token as authorization.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The complete vulnerable mechanism originated in the single-parent feature commit 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38: it created core/webhook.go, added the network listener and /hook handler, defined the JSON exec field, made an empty token authenticate successfully, passed exec to sh -c, wired the server into main, and documented an empty token as disabling authentication. This is the smallest repository-visible BIC, not the later shell-helper refactor.
audit_record.ai_marker: BIC commit object has human author and committer 'chenhg5 <chenhonggui@wps.cn>' and contains the exact message lines 'generated by llmgit' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'. The latter is an explicit AI co-authorship trailer on the BIC itself.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/issues/1488 identifies core/webhook.go's empty-token authentication bypass, exec dispatch, all-interface listener, and shell sink; maintainer @chenhg5 replied on 2026-07-03 that the report was confirmed valid and described the same two-part chain. Source review adds an important reachability qualification: handleHook requires a nonempty session_key, resolveEngine must succeed, and executeShell must reconstruct the named platform context. Consequently, the issue's displayed curl body, which omits session_key, would be rejected at the required-field check, but adding a valid/reconstructable session key reaches the confirmed unauthenticated shell path.

`git show 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go config/config.go config.example.toml cmd/cc-connect/main.go` shows one cohesive +503-line webhook feature. In core/webhook.go it creates WebhookRequest.Exec, starts http.Server at fmt.Sprintf(":%d", ws.port), routes POST /hook through authenticate, returns true for ws.token == "", dispatches req.Exec, and runs exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", req.Exec). config/config.go and config.example.toml state that an empty token means no authentication, while main.go starts the listener whenever webhook.enabled is true.

The BIC's newly added core/webhook_test.go makes the insecure policy explicit: TestWebhookServer_NoTokenRequired creates a server with an empty token and asserts authenticate succeeds. The same test file validates that exec is accepted as one of the two request action types, corroborating that no-token access and network-triggered exec were deliberately shipped together rather than accidentally joined by later history.

History searches `git log --all -S 'if ws.token == ""' -- core/webhook.go` and `git log --all -S 'req.Exec' -- core/webhook.go` each identify 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 as the first writer. The complete path log contains only the introducer, a later broad error-handling commit b9af7ea7ba641eb9278d45c9a19f361692acef44, and shell-configuration refactor 6feaf90f2f8cccec2203169b4d0edc3edd538837. The latter only replaces direct sh -c construction with shellExecCommand while continuing to pass req.Exec, so it preserves rather than introduces the vulnerable trust boundary.

Immediate-parent verification is direct: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2 -- core/webhook.go` returns no path, and `git diff-tree --name-status 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go` reports `A core/webhook.go`. Therefore the parent tree lacks the endpoint, empty-token bypass, request exec field, and webhook shell sink. The BIC is a one-parent public-DAG feature commit; no smaller reachable member commits exist to decompose.

Release-boundary check: v1.2.2-beta.1 resolves to ecea1ef36d86bb70dd633fb342f655d108ea52cb (2026-03-12) and lacks core/webhook.go, while the 2026-03-14 BIC is contained by v1.2.2-beta.2, which resolves to 9223201696e3f91b2f9fb456bba7dcef0a76bcd3 (2026-03-16). `git tag --contains 6ae088a...` starts at v1.2.2-beta.2 and includes v1.4.1. Direct `git grep` confirms both `if ws.token == ""` and the req.Exec shell sink in v1.2.2-beta.2 and v1.4.1; v1.2.2-beta.1 has neither. This places the introduction before the affected upper-bound release named by the advisory.

No fix is present in the validated public history. `git log --all -- core/webhook.go` has no post-6feaf90 remediation, `git log --all -S 'if ws.token == ""'` has no removal, and direct tag-tree checks show the bypass plus req.Exec-to-shell path still present in stable v1.5.0 (17c61062c2f9ce9bcdd45a2082e491f9743a2770, 2026-08-16) and HEAD/v1.5.1-beta.1 (80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4, 2026-08-28). Issue #1488 was auto-closed for inactivity rather than by a patch. fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are therefore null; the advisory summary's 'up to 1.4.1' wording is not a demonstrated patched boundary and the source remains vulnerable in later tags.

BIC-only attribution comes from `git cat-file -p 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38`: the object names parent 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2, human author/committer chenhg5, exact standalone marker `generated by llmgit`, and exact trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Because this same object first writes every causal component, the explicit AI co-authorship is attached to the root-cause introduction, satisfying AI_ROOT_CAUSE without relying on issue/PR prose, branch names, or later commits.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is a composed trust-boundary failure, not merely the existence of a shell API. With webhook.enabled true, the BIC binds the webhook listener to every interface; an omitted token causes authenticate to approve every caller; handleHook accepts a caller-provided exec action; and executeShell supplies that string as the shell program. A usable request also needs a session key whose platform context can be reconstructed, and possibly a project selector, but neither substitutes for authentication. The 6ae088a commit introduced all of these pieces at once and even added a test requiring empty-token authentication to pass. Its immediate parent has no core/webhook.go or equivalent webhook-exec route, so absence is tree-proven. Pickaxe history finds no earlier writer, while the only later sink change is a behavior-preserving helper refactor. Tag membership brackets introduction between v1.2.2-beta.1 and v1.2.2-beta.2 and confirms persistence through the advisory's v1.4.1 boundary. There is no remediation commit: both the latest stable tag and audited HEAD retain the bypass and shell dispatch, so null fix fields are justified and unpatched status is recorded. Finally, the smallest BIC's own commit object explicitly says `generated by llmgit` and credits Claude as co-author. Since that AI-marked object is the first writer of the flawed authentication-plus-exec design, the causal verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.

A future remediation commit and patched release boundary are the only outstanding lifecycle facts.
