primary_record.ai_marker: BIC commit object has human author and committer 'chenhg5 <chenhonggui@wps.cn>' and contains the exact message lines 'generated by llmgit' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'. The latter is an explicit AI co-authorship trailer on the BIC itself.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/issues/1488 identifies core/webhook.go's empty-token authentication bypass, exec dispatch, all-interface listener, and shell sink; maintainer @chenhg5 replied on 2026-07-03 that the report was confirmed valid and described the same two-part chain. Source review adds an important reachability qualification: handleHook requires a nonempty session_key, resolveEngine must succeed, and executeShell must reconstruct the named platform context. Consequently, the issue's displayed curl body, which omits session_key, would be rejected at the required-field check, but adding a valid/reconstructable session key reaches the confirmed unauthenticated shell path.

`git show 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go config/config.go config.example.toml cmd/cc-connect/main.go` shows one cohesive +503-line webhook feature. In core/webhook.go it creates WebhookRequest.Exec, starts http.Server at fmt.Sprintf(":%d", ws.port), routes POST /hook through authenticate, returns true for ws.token == "", dispatches req.Exec, and runs exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", req.Exec). config/config.go and config.example.toml state that an empty token means no authentication, while main.go starts the listener whenever webhook.enabled is true.

The BIC's newly added core/webhook_test.go makes the insecure policy explicit: TestWebhookServer_NoTokenRequired creates a server with an empty token and asserts authenticate succeeds. The same test file validates that exec is accepted as one of the two request action types, corroborating that no-token access and network-triggered exec were deliberately shipped together rather than accidentally joined by later history.

History searches `git log --all -S 'if ws.token == ""' -- core/webhook.go` and `git log --all -S 'req.Exec' -- core/webhook.go` each identify 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 as the first writer. The complete path log contains only the introducer, a later broad error-handling commit b9af7ea7ba641eb9278d45c9a19f361692acef44, and shell-configuration refactor 6feaf90f2f8cccec2203169b4d0edc3edd538837. The latter only replaces direct sh -c construction with shellExecCommand while continuing to pass req.Exec, so it preserves rather than introduces the vulnerable trust boundary.

Immediate-parent verification is direct: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2 -- core/webhook.go` returns no path, and `git diff-tree --name-status 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go` reports `A core/webhook.go`. Therefore the parent tree lacks the endpoint, empty-token bypass, request exec field, and webhook shell sink. The BIC is a one-parent public-DAG feature commit; no smaller reachable member commits exist to decompose.

Release-boundary check: v1.2.2-beta.1 resolves to ecea1ef36d86bb70dd633fb342f655d108ea52cb (2026-03-12) and lacks core/webhook.go, while the 2026-03-14 BIC is contained by v1.2.2-beta.2, which resolves to 9223201696e3f91b2f9fb456bba7dcef0a76bcd3 (2026-03-16). `git tag --contains 6ae088a...` starts at v1.2.2-beta.2 and includes v1.4.1. Direct `git grep` confirms both `if ws.token == ""` and the req.Exec shell sink in v1.2.2-beta.2 and v1.4.1; v1.2.2-beta.1 has neither. This places the introduction before the affected upper-bound release named by the advisory.

No fix is present in the validated public history. `git log --all -- core/webhook.go` has no post-6feaf90 remediation, `git log --all -S 'if ws.token == ""'` has no removal, and direct tag-tree checks show the bypass plus req.Exec-to-shell path still present in stable v1.5.0 (17c61062c2f9ce9bcdd45a2082e491f9743a2770, 2026-08-16) and HEAD/v1.5.1-beta.1 (80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4, 2026-08-28). Issue #1488 was auto-closed for inactivity rather than by a patch. fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are therefore null; the advisory summary's 'up to 1.4.1' wording is not a demonstrated patched boundary and the source remains vulnerable in later tags.

BIC-only attribution comes from `git cat-file -p 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38`: the object names parent 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2, human author/committer chenhg5, exact standalone marker `generated by llmgit`, and exact trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Because this same object first writes every causal component, the explicit AI co-authorship is attached to the root-cause introduction, satisfying AI_ROOT_CAUSE without relying on issue/PR prose, branch names, or later commits.
primary_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is a composed trust-boundary failure, not merely the existence of a shell API. With webhook.enabled true, the BIC binds the webhook listener to every interface; an omitted token causes authenticate to approve every caller; handleHook accepts a caller-provided exec action; and executeShell supplies that string as the shell program. A usable request also needs a session key whose platform context can be reconstructed, and possibly a project selector, but neither substitutes for authentication. The 6ae088a commit introduced all of these pieces at once and even added a test requiring empty-token authentication to pass. Its immediate parent has no core/webhook.go or equivalent webhook-exec route, so absence is tree-proven. Pickaxe history finds no earlier writer, while the only later sink change is a behavior-preserving helper refactor. Tag membership brackets introduction between v1.2.2-beta.1 and v1.2.2-beta.2 and confirms persistence through the advisory's v1.4.1 boundary. There is no remediation commit: both the latest stable tag and audited HEAD retain the bypass and shell dispatch, so null fix fields are justified and unpatched status is recorded. Finally, the smallest BIC's own commit object explicitly says `generated by llmgit` and credits Claude as co-author. Since that AI-marked object is the first writer of the flawed authentication-plus-exec design, the causal verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
primary_record.remaining_gap: The vulnerability remains unpatched in every fetched ref of the validated clone through HEAD 80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4 and v1.5.1-beta.1; therefore no fix SHA or direct-fix SHA exists to audit. A future remediation commit and patched release boundary are the only outstanding lifecycle facts.

review_record.bug_semantics: When the optional webhook server is enabled, it listens on all interfaces and treats an empty configured token as authenticated. An unauthenticated remote POST to the configured hook path can therefore supply a JSON exec value; handleHook dispatches that value to executeShell, which passes it as the command string to the configured shell. Thus an enabled deployment with the documented empty-token setting exposes arbitrary command execution in the cc-connect process context.
review_record.flaw_origin: Single-parent feature commit 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 introduced the entire vulnerable surface in one coherent change: WebhookConfig documented token empty = no auth, an externally bound HTTP server, WebhookRequest.Exec, authenticate's empty-token allow branch, handleHook's Exec dispatch, and exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", req.Exec). This is the first writer, not a move, refactor, release/backport, revert, or merge carrier. Later commit 6feaf90f2f8cccec2203169b4d0edc3edd538837 only generalized the shell helper and preserved the attacker-controlled command sink.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated DatoCMS user could supply an absolute or protocol-relative external URL in the visual inspector's path query parameter. ContentLinkContext copied that value unchanged into iframeState.path, and UI then placed it unchanged in the redirect parameter of the configured enableDraftModeUrl. When the draft-mode endpoint followed redirect, the inspector iframe could be navigated to an attacker-chosen origin, bypassing the configured frontend-origin restriction.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The Visual Editing feature was introduced with both ends of the unsafe data flow in one commit: web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/ContentLinkContext/index.tsx accepted ctx.location.search path without origin validation, while web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/UI/index.tsx forwarded iframeState.path to the draft-mode redirect parameter without validating it at the iframe sink.

audit_record.evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x8p2-g6vv-f5mr identifies authenticated iframe injection, Web Previews <1.0.31, and commit 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e. At the BIC, ContentLinkContext/index.tsx:79-85 initialized iframeState.path from new URLSearchParams(ctx.location.search).get('path') with no validation, and UI/index.tsx:35-39 set that value as url.searchParams.redirect before passing the resulting URL to IframeContainer. git log -L on both ranges and git log --all -S for the exact source and sink expressions identify 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 as their first appearance; the only later -S removal of the sink is the advisory fix. Direct parent-tree verification with git ls-tree -r d42b0fc4e54d2e9731030812d2b98098cc6d1a95 -- web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/UI/index.tsx returned no entry, because the vulnerable Inspector UI did not exist in the parent. The BIC tree's package.json declared 1.0.27; descendant a933ee45d41b02d0d6643d8ebc1aa60f6929a993 bumped 1.0.27 to 1.0.29, and 3d697a3b3ebd280f36ae2a411199d2d715ca8b31 bumped it to the last vulnerable release 1.0.30. The fix's immediate parent a20d935b50daa9bdde4c88776ace6de5cb65a05d still declared 1.0.30. Fix 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e added normalizePathForVisualEditing, rejects parsed origins unequal to the configured draft-mode origin, emits only pathname/search/hash, and applies this at sources and again at the redirect sink. Its immediate child a40b1e48bea2c352bb5c4838dbd536ee3c0457f0 bumped 1.0.30 to patched 1.0.31, proving the fix/version boundary. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit with no squash/member identifiers, and all-ref -S history exposes no smaller predecessor to decompose.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is the complete unvalidated path-to-redirect flow, not a later refactor: an authenticated user-controlled inspector path reached the draft-mode redirect and therefore the iframe destination without a same-origin check. Commit 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 is the smallest history object that first wrote both causally necessary lines; later 04aa5d9ad0506751b305cf86d18a8ca07358a906 only changed visualEditing naming around them. The immediate parent lacks the Inspector UI path entirely, directly establishing parent absence. The vulnerable feature precedes the 1.0.29 and 1.0.30 release bumps, while the sanitizer lands on top of 1.0.30 and immediately precedes the 1.0.31 bump, matching the advisory's <1.0.31 boundary. The direct fix validates all path entry points and revalidates the iframe redirect sink against the configured origin. Because attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object and that object has only a human author/committer with no AI marker or trailer, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

review_record.bug_semantics: Authenticated iframe injection in the Web Previews visual inspector. An authenticated user can supply an absolute or scheme-relative external URL in the inspector's `path` query parameter. ContentLinkContext copied that untrusted value directly into `iframeState.path`; UI then put it unchanged into the configured draft-mode endpoint's `redirect` parameter and used that endpoint URL as the iframe `src`. When the draft-mode endpoint follows `redirect`, the iframe leaves the configured frontend and loads the attacker-selected external origin, bypassing the frontend-origin restriction. The advisory states Web Previews <1.0.31 is affected; repository and npm history narrow the actually present visual-editing path to published 1.0.29 and 1.0.30, with 1.0.31 the first fixed release.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 (`Visual Editing`) is the smallest first-writer. It created `web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/ContentLinkContext/index.tsx` with `new URLSearchParams(ctx.location.search).get('path')` flowing unsanitized into `iframeState.path`, and created `web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/UI/index.tsx` with `url.searchParams.set('redirect', iframeState.path)` followed by the resulting URL as the iframe source. Later commit 04aa5d9ad0506751b305cf86d18a8ca07358a906 only selected among visual-editing frontends and renamed the URL source to `currentVisualEditing`; it did not originate the untrusted redirect sink. The BIC is a preserved single-parent feature-branch commit, not the later normal merge a20d935b50daa9bdde4c88776ace6de5cb65a05d and not a squash aggregate.

In the validated clone, `git log --all --reverse -S "url.searchParams.set('redirect', iframeState.path)" -- web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/UI/index.tsx` returns exactly introducer 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 and remover/fix 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e. `git log -L 51,56:web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/UI/index.tsx 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e^` traces the redirect sink to 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 and shows 04aa5d9ad0506751b305cf86d18a8ca07358a906 changed only `visualEditing.enableDraftModeUrl` to `currentVisualEditing.enableDraftModeUrl`; `git blame -L '/new URLSearchParams(ctx.location.search)/',+4 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e^ -- web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/ContentLinkContext/index.tsx` attributes the attacker-controlled `path` read to 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672. `git diff --name-status d42b0fc4e54d2e9731030812d2b98098cc6d1a95 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 --` for the two Inspector files reports both as `A`, directly proving the immediate parent has neither vulnerable source nor sink. `git show 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e` adds `normalizePathForVisualEditing`: it resolves the candidate against `new URL(draftModeUrl).origin`, rejects a parsed origin that differs, emits only pathname/search/hash, applies safe fallbacks, and revalidates initialization, content-link state, navigation, frontend changes, and the final iframe redirect sink. Finally, `git cat-file -p 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672` supplies the BIC-only marker check quoted in `ai_marker`.
review_record.reasoning: The security invariant is that iframe navigation must remain on the configured draft-mode frontend origin. The BIC simultaneously introduced the attacker-controlled inspector query input and the redirect-based iframe sink without validating that invariant. Its direct parent lacks both newly added Inspector files, while line history rejects the later frontend-selection edit and normal merge as origins. The advisory-linked fix closes the complete path by canonicalizing every path source and, critically, checking again at the redirect sink that `parsed.origin` equals the configured draft-mode origin; 1.0.31 is the immediate release bump containing that fix. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC commit object. That object names a human author/committer and contains no AI/bot marker or trailer, so the correct closed verdict is NOT_AI regardless of any later commits or fix authorship.

audit_record.bug_semantics: For a window drawable, do_get_buffers allocated only count + 1 DRI2BufferPtr slots, filled count client-requested slots, and then used arithmetic attachment counters to decide whether to append implicit front buffers. With at least two DRI2BufferBackLeft requests and one DRI2BufferFrontLeft request, need_real_front remained positive even though FrontLeft was already present, so a redundant real-front pointer was appended at buffers[count]. The FrontLeft request also made need_fake_front positive, so the fake-front pointer was then written at buffers[count + 1], one pointer beyond the heap allocation. The DRI2GetBuffers and DRI2GetBuffersWithFormat request paths both called this helper, allowing a local X client to crash the server or potentially escalate privileges when it ran as root.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 replaced the parent's bulk CreateBuffers path with per-attachment allocation and introduced need_real_front++/-- alongside the existing fake-front accounting, while retaining an allocation sized for only one implicit attachment. The parent could append at most one fake front and therefore respected its count + 1 capacity; the new combination could append both a redundant real front and a fake front. Treating attachment presence as signed counts rather than boolean presence broke the allocation invariant.

primary_record.bug_semantics: For a window drawable, do_get_buffers allocated only count + 1 DRI2BufferPtr slots, filled count client-requested slots, and then used arithmetic attachment counters to decide whether to append implicit front buffers. With at least two DRI2BufferBackLeft requests and one DRI2BufferFrontLeft request, need_real_front remained positive even though FrontLeft was already present, so a redundant real-front pointer was appended at buffers[count]. The FrontLeft request also made need_fake_front positive, so the fake-front pointer was then written at buffers[count + 1], one pointer beyond the heap allocation. The DRI2GetBuffers and DRI2GetBuffersWithFormat request paths both called this helper, allowing a local X client to crash the server or potentially escalate privileges when it ran as root.
primary_record.flaw_origin: Commit ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 replaced the parent's bulk CreateBuffers path with per-attachment allocation and introduced need_real_front++/-- alongside the existing fake-front accounting, while retaining an allocation sized for only one implicit attachment. The parent could append at most one fake front and therefore respected its count + 1 capacity; the new combination could append both a redundant real front and a fake front. Treating attachment presence as signed counts rather than boolean presence broke the allocation invariant.

review_record.bug_semantics: In the Xorg DRI2 request path, a client controls the attachment list passed by ProcDRI2GetBuffers or ProcDRI2GetBuffersWithFormat to do_get_buffers. The vulnerable code allocates count + 1 DRI2BufferPtr slots but treats requested attachment multiplicity as arithmetic: every DRI2BufferBackLeft increments need_real_front, while one DRI2BufferFrontLeft decrements it only once and also increments need_fake_front for a window. With at least two BackLeft entries and one FrontLeft, both counters remain positive after the count input entries are stored, so the function appends both an implicit real-front and an implicit fake-front buffer. The fake-front pointer is written at buffers[count + 1], one element beyond the count + 1 allocation, causing a client-triggerable heap out-of-bounds write and permitting server crash or privilege escalation when the X server is privileged.
review_record.flaw_origin: ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 replaced the earlier bulk CreateBuffers path with the new per-attachment do_get_buffers implementation for DRI2GetBuffersWithFormat. audit_record.bug_semantics: An X client can send XkbSetMap with a non-canonical key type whose one-byte numLevels is as large as 255. CheckKeyTypes accepted every positive value and stored it even though downstream code assumes at most XkbMaxShiftLevel (63). A later core ChangeKeyboardMapping reaches XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore and XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols, where the tainted level count becomes groupsWidth and XKB_OFFSET(g,l) indexes a 252-entry XkbMaxSymsPerKey stack buffer; at width 255 the maximum index is 1019. The same oversized key geometry can also make XkbChangeTypesOfKey copy excessive symbols and actions into its fixed oldSyms and oldActs stack arrays, yielding three client-triggerable stack overflows and possible crash or privilege escalation when the server is privileged.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The causal mechanism is the combination of CheckKeyTypes validating only numLevels >= 1 and the XKB conversion/resizing paths using fixed XkbMaxShiftLevel * XkbNumKbdGroups stack arrays without independently bounding stored non-canonical type widths. All of those lines already appear in the repository's 2003 R6.6 vendor baseline import, whose immediate parent contains no xkb tree. That 609-file baseline aggregate imported pre-existing X11/XFree86 code rather than authoring the mechanism, so the smallest original change and its parent are beyond this Git history. The 2025 CVE-2025-26597 fix changed only the nGroups == 0 action-resize path and did not introduce this excessive-numLevels path.

review_record.bug_semantics: An XKB-capable local client can use XkbSetMap to replace a non-canonical key type with wire numLevels=255. CheckKeyTypes accepted every positive CARD8 width and stored it without enforcing XkbMaxShiftLevel=63. A later core ChangeKeyboardMapping reaches XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore; XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols derives groupsWidth from the attacker-controlled num_levels and uses XKB_OFFSET(g,l)=(g*groupsWidth)+l against a stack KeySym tsyms[XkbMaxSymsPerKey] buffer of 252 entries. With four groups and width 255, indices reach 1019, 767 entries beyond the buffer; the related fixed-size symbol/action temporaries make this a set of stack-overflow paths capable of server crash and, for a root X server, privilege escalation.
review_record.flaw_origin: The missing upper-bound validation, the fixed-size XKB temporaries, and their consumer path already coexist in the repository's 2003 R6.6 whole-tree baseline import ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1. audit_record.bug_semantics: With federation enabled, NodeBB authenticated the HTTP-signature key against the ActivityPub activity actor and required object.id to have that actor's origin, but did not bind object.attributedTo to the authenticated actor. A remote actor could therefore send a signed Create whose object.id was on the attacker's origin but whose attributedTo was a bare local numeric uid such as 1. The inbound mock copied attributedTo into the post/message uid; actors.assert filtered numeric identifiers out and its false result was ignored, after which topic or chat persistence treated the attacker-chosen local uid as the author.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 first made the unsafe attribution mapping remotely exploitable: it added inbox.create, took only req.body.object for authorship, passed the untrusted object through activitypub.mocks.post, and persisted the resulting postData without comparing attributedTo to the authenticated req.body.actor. The unsafe mocks.post assignment had been prepared in f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458 and moved by 06e1583461f034d68c8c3c6d69547b06ad6ab3b5, but f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 is the smallest commit that connected it to the inbound Create attack surface and made the remote post-forgery path real.
audit_record.ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file commit f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7` shows human author and committer Julian Lam <julian@nodebb.org>, the message `feat: handle Create(note)`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other trailer.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8m27-grg5-27vj and its referenced vulnerable tree https://github.com/NodeBB/NodeBB/blob/v4.13.2/src/activitypub/mocks.js describe the unsigned-author binding failure and the bare numeric attributedTo local-uid exploit.

`git show f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 -- src/activitypub/inbox.js` adds inbox.create: it reads object from req.body, calls activitypub.mocks.post(object), and sends postData to activitypub.notes.assert without reading or comparing the authenticated actor. The commit has one parent, so it is neither a merge nor a squash aggregate.

Direct parent-tree verification with `git grep -n 'inbox.create = async' 756548520401e1f920d358ad61ec1f28451173d5 -- src/activitypub/inbox.js` returned no match. The parent already contained the generic mock, but no inbound Create handler connected a remote signed activity to that mock-and-persist path; the f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 diff is the minimal enabling change.

At v4.13.2, src/middleware/activitypub.js verifies the HTTP signature, derives req.uid from keyId, checks key ownership against req.body.actor, and checks actor hostname against object.id hostname, but never checks object.attributedTo. src/activitypub/inbox.js create passes object to notes.assert; src/activitypub/mocks.js maps attributedTo to uid, calls actors.assert(uid) without checking its return, and returns uid in the persistence payload; src/activitypub/actors.js explicitly filters numeric ids; src/activitypub/notes.js ultimately calls topics.post with authorId or messaging.sendMessage with payload.uid.

History cross-checks show the precursor assignment `attributedTo: uid` originated in f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458, was only moved by refactor 06e1583461f034d68c8c3c6d69547b06ad6ab3b5, and became remotely reachable in f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7. Later d948334713dc0857c28ec680f935e16e293bb73a added the ignored actors.assert(uid) call, and 4ec7552cfbbdf23c6f51b905e2e1536777695b70 added normalization/private-message mocking, expanding but not originating the flaw.

`git tag --contains f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7` includes v4.0.0-alpha, every stable v4 release through the vulnerable v4.13.2, and later descendants; `git merge-base --is-ancestor f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 v3.12.9` exits 1. Thus the boundary is the v4 ActivityPub line, with v3.12.9 outside this BIC's ancestry.

Direct fix dc45bd7f98168e8c5726e36a8f84a519cc2dbc35 adds `if (!activitypub.helpers.isUri(attributedTo)) throw` in src/activitypub/mocks.js and states that the guard prevents a number from enabling unchecked impersonation of local users. Its parent b799d51d9b513a121fa9ba7204a0e7b764dea284 lacks that guard. `git tag --contains dc45bd7f98168e8c5726e36a8f84a519cc2dbc35` starts at v4.14.0, whereas v4.13.2 predates it; this establishes the vulnerable/patched release boundary for the advisory's local-uid vector. Follow-up f93507a6404ce0e32e6e7befb47ef3a1f56bbac1 additionally enforces attributedTo origin matching in Create/Update handlers.

BIC-only AI attribution comes from the raw f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 commit object: Julian Lam is both author and committer and there are no trailers or bot markers. No later fix or refactor signal is used for the verdict.
audit_record.reasoning: The causal split matters. f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458 created a generic remote-note mock that trusted attributedTo, but its existence alone did not provide the advisory's unauthenticated remote inbox attack. f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 is the first complete vulnerable state: it added the signed inbound Create handler and connected the untrusted object to that mock and persistence while omitting the authenticated actor from the author decision. Its immediate parent has no inbox.create handler, so the remote path is directly absent there. Subsequent commits moved and broadened the implementation, including a numeric-id filter whose failure was ignored and a private-message path, but those are not smaller origins. The BIC precedes v4.0.0-alpha and is present in v4.13.2; dc45bd7f98168e8c5726e36a8f84a519cc2dbc35 blocks the exact bare-number local-user impersonation vector and first ships in v4.14.0. Because the only admissible AI evidence is the BIC commit object and that object is a trailer-free human commit, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

review_record.bug_semantics: With ActivityPub enabled, a remote sender can submit a signed inbound Create whose object.id is on the sender's origin but whose object.attributedTo is an attacker-chosen bare number such as 1. The inbound path does not bind attributedTo to the authenticated activity actor. Mocks.post/_normalize carries attributedTo into the internal uid, while Actors.qualify later filters numeric IDs out as already-local rather than rejecting or re-deriving the author. Public note assertion therefore creates a post under that local uid. The non-public path added later likewise turns attributedTo into the message payload uid and uses it to create/send a chat message, allowing forged posts or DMs attributed to a local user, including the administrator.
review_record.flaw_origin: f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 is the smallest functional BIC. Earlier f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458 only stubbed the post mock and 06e1583461f034d68c8c3c6d69547b06ad6ab3b5 only moved it; neither exposed inbound Create. f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 simultaneously added the controller's Create dispatch and inbox.create, which fed the untrusted object through Mocks.post and into note creation without comparing object.attributedTo to req.body.actor. b82e20dfc79659c741155a866bdb48ae1b423f13 later extended the same trust flaw to non-public notes/chat, but the public-post vulnerability already existed, so it is not the BIC.
review_record.ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7` shows author and committer `Julian Lam <julian@nodebb.org>` and the sole message `feat: handle Create(note)`; there are no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot, or other AI trailers/identities.
evidence: Advisory reproduction: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8m27-grg5-27vj describes the authenticated-actor/attributedTo mismatch, the numeric attributedTo=1 path, Actors.assert filtering numeric identifiers, and forged posts/private messages; it references the vulnerable v4.13.2 mocks.js.

BIC and parent: `git show --format=fuller --stat --patch f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7` shows a 19-line, two-file change adding both `case 'Create': await activitypub.inbox.create(req)` in src/controllers/activitypub/index.js and inbox.create in src/activitypub/inbox.js. That handler calls `activitypub.mocks.post(object)`, then `activitypub.notes.assert(1, [postData])` and `assertTopic`. `git show 756548520401e1f920d358ad61ec1f28451173d5:src/activitypub/inbox.js` has follow/accept/undo only, and its controller switch has no Create case, directly proving parent absence.

Lineage cross-checks: `git log v4.13.2 -L '/^inbox\.create = async/,/^};/':src/activitypub/inbox.js` terminates at f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 with the handler addition; `git log --all -S"case 'Create':" -- src/controllers/activitypub/index.js` also reaches f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7. `git log --all -S'attributedTo: uid' -- src/activitypub.js src/activitypub/*.js` shows the earlier stub f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458 and move 06e1583461f034d68c8c3c6d69547b06ad6ab3b5; they lacked inbound dispatch and are rejected as BICs.

Vulnerable release mechanics: `git show v4.13.2:src/activitypub/mocks.js` shows _normalize returning attacker-controlled attributedTo, Mocks.post destructuring it as uid and calling `activitypub.actors.assert(uid)`, and Mocks.message returning `uid: object.attributedTo`. `git show v4.13.2:src/activitypub/actors.js` shows Actors.qualify's `ids = ids.filter(id => !utils.isNumber(id))`; an all-numeric input consequently returns without rejecting the claimed local author. `git show v4.13.2:src/activitypub/notes.js` lines 420-529 shows the private path creating the room and sending the message as payload.uid.

review_record.bug_semantics: A client able to change the X server font path can create a directory whose fonts.alias maps an alias to a 257-1023-byte target, add that directory with SetFontPath, and request the alias with ListFonts or ListFontsWithInfo. libXfont2 accepts and returns names/alias targets up to its 1024-byte MAXFONTNAMELEN, while the server historically used XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN=256 for the stack-local tmp_pattern and the LFWIstateRec current.pattern arrays. doListFontsAndAliases copied resolvedlen bytes into tmp_pattern and then current.pattern without checking resolvedlen; doListFontsWithInfo likewise copied namelen bytes into current.pattern without checking namelen. The oversized library-produced target therefore writes beyond stack buffers, permitting a server crash and potentially privilege escalation when the X server runs as root.
review_record.flaw_origin: The vulnerable 256-byte server buffers and all three relevant unchecked alias-resolution copies are already present in ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1, the 2003-11-14 whole-tree snapshot whose message is 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line'. That changeset creates dix/dixfonts.c and include/closestr.h wholesale on top of a parent containing neither path, so it is an aggregate import boundary rather than the smallest source commit and is rejected as the BIC. Later 05a793f5b3c40747d5a92a076def7f4fb673c7e7 merely migrated the pre-existing code from libXfont to libXfont2, and 5cc24dbb4c151023dc0d18e16001e27f87ae8391 merely changed non-overlapping memmove calls to memcpy; neither first introduced the unchecked length-versus-buffer mismatch. The true originating source change predates the fine-grained history available for these paths in this repository.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated /cgi-bin/api.values.get handler in the Grandstream GXP1600 firmware's 32-bit ARM /app/bin/gs_web binary parses the attacker-controlled request parameter as colon-delimited identifiers and copies each non-colon byte into a 64-byte stack buffer without checking the identifier length. An identifier longer than 63 bytes writes beyond that buffer, and repeated colon-delimited identifiers let an attacker place multiple terminating NUL bytes, overwrite saved registers including PC, build a ROP chain, and invoke system() as root.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The flawed bounds-free identifier-copy loop belongs to Grandstream's proprietary GXP1600 firmware, not rapid7/metasploit-framework. Its source and version-control history are not public, so the exact introducing source commit is beyond the public-history boundary. Metasploit commit 08efa9cd16f254bfc8f2f4cee0550f3a851e0aa5 merely added an exploit for the already-existing device flaw after fixed firmware 1.0.7.81 had been released; it did not write the vulnerable /app/bin/gs_web code.
audit_record.ai_marker: unavailable: there is no public BIC commit object for Grandstream's proprietary /app/bin/gs_web source, so BIC author, committer, bot identity, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, and other trailer checks cannot be performed; no AI conclusion is drawn from the later Metasploit exploit commit
evidence: Rapid7's first-party disclosure (https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ve-cve-2026-2329-critical-unauthenticated-stack-buffer-overflow-in-grandstream-gxp1600-voip-phones-fixed) identifies the vulnerable component as the native 32-bit ARM /app/bin/gs_web firmware binary and decompiles its api.values.get handler: attacker-controlled request_buffer bytes are appended to small_buffer[64] while part_length is incremented without a bound check. It documents PC control and the repeated-colon/NUL technique used to construct a ROP chain and execute commands as root.

The disclosure tested vulnerable firmware 1.0.7.79 and says users must upgrade to 1.0.7.81 or above. Its timeline records that Grandstream made 1.0.7.81 available, reaffirmed the issue resolved in that release, and that Rapid7 independently verified remediation by reverse engineering the public firmware. This is binary verification, not a public source commit.

Grandstream's release notes (https://firmware.grandstream.com/Release_Note_GXP16xx_1.0.7.81.pdf) list 1.0.7.81 for all six affected models, date it 2026-01-30, and include 'Fixed some security vulnerabilities.' The preceding 1.0.7.80 is dated 2025-12-31. The Metasploit module's description at modules/exploits/linux/http/grandstream_gxp1600_unauth_rce.rb:19-23 states that every firmware version below 1.0.7.81 is affected, and its check at lines 105-117 classifies version < 1.0.7.81 as vulnerable and 1.0.7.81 or later as safe.

review_record.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated POST parameter request at /cgi-bin/api.values.get is parsed character by character by the Grandstream firmware's 32-bit ARM /app/bin/gs_web service. Non-colon bytes are copied into a 64-byte stack buffer and a terminator is appended without checking that the current colon-delimited component is at most 63 bytes. An overlong component therefore overwrites the stack; repeated colon-delimited components permit multiple strategically placed NUL writes, enabling a ROP chain and unauthenticated command execution as root.

audit_record.bug_semantics: A remote Bluetooth device can supply an EIR name element whose field_len is 254, making eir_parse pass data_len 253 to name2utf8. On the non-UTF-8 conversion path, name2utf8 used strncpy with that attacker-controlled length to copy into utf8_name[HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 2]. HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248, so the 250-byte stack array is overrun by three bytes; the missing terminator can also make the subsequent stripping and duplication read beyond the array. Discovery therefore permits a radio-adjacent unauthenticated peer to crash bluetoothd and potentially corrupt control data.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 first added src/eir.c:name2utf8 and coupled the fixed 250-byte utf8_name array to strncpy(..., len), where len is derived from the untrusted EIR element length and can be 253. Although the subject calls the change a move, the removed src/event.c code copied at the fixed MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH bound, while the newly added EIR helper introduced the attacker-length copy; it is therefore the smallest causal introducer rather than a pure move. Later commit 218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99 changed character conversion but retained the already-vulnerable array and copy.
audit_record.ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 names Johan Hedberg <johan.hedberg@intel.com> as both author and committer and contains only the subject 'core: Move UTF-8 validation of device names into eir.c'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: The first-party BlueZ advisory https://github.com/bluez/bluez/security/advisories/GHSA-68h6-5qgp-3975 identifies src/eir.c:name2utf8, affected release 5.86, and patched commit 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2. It explains that field_len 254 yields data_len 253 and a three-byte overflow of the 250-byte array.

git show --format=fuller --patch 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2 shows the direct fix adding 'len = MIN(len, HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH);' immediately before memset/strncpy in src/eir.c. The commit message also records the remote EIR/advertising attack path and the possible unterminated follow-on reads.

At fix parent c73fa2f9ae2d366cb8a4f101fa9a5ccd9f33a4ea, git blame -L 136,150 -- src/eir.c assigns the function, utf8_name declaration, memset, strncpy(..., len), g_strstrip, and g_strdup to 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22; only the character-conversion call is later (218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99).

git log --all --reverse -S 'strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)' -- src/eir.c returns 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 as the first addition and 8c81ab108b09154b884b1b0549dc9c23ffe3ec6f as its later removal, confirming the smallest source-level origin.

git show 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 shows the new helper and the EIR_NAME_SHORT/EIR_NAME_COMPLETE call name2utf8(data, data_len). In the same parser, a first field_len of 254 with eir_len 255 passes the bounds check and computes data_len = field_len - 1 = 253. git grep at that commit confirms HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248 in lib/hci.h, so the destination is 250 bytes.

Immediate-parent tree verification used git grep at 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e: there is no name2utf8 and no src/eir.c attacker-length strncpy; the only matching src/event.c copy is strncpy(utf8_name, name, MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH), a fixed bound into MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 1. Thus the vulnerable mechanism is absent from the direct parent.

Version checks show the BIC is not an ancestor of tag 4.101 but is an ancestor of tag 5.0 and of the advisory's affected tag 5.86 (74770b1fd2be612f9c2cf807db81fcdcc35e6560). Tag 5.86 contains the vulnerable strncpy and no clamp. The fix is not in tag 5.86, while 5.86 is an ancestor of 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2, placing the fix after the affected boundary.

git cat-file commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 provides the BIC-only attribution evidence: human author and committer Johan Hedberg, one parent 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e, and no trailers or AI marker. The later fix's 'Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5' is deliberately excluded from BIC attribution.
audit_record.reasoning: The lifecycle begins in 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22: EIR parsing already derived an 8-bit data_len from the remote element, and this commit newly routed remote name elements into a helper that could copy that length into a smaller fixed stack array. The immediate parent had only a separately located fixed-bound remote-name copy, so the title's 'Move' does not disqualify this commit: the unsafe attacker-controlled bound was new. The risky copy survives the later conversion refactor 218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99 and is present in release 5.86. Commit 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2 directly closes the root cause by clamping len to 248 before the copy, and it descends from the affected tag. Finally, the only permissible AI evidence is the raw 2012 BIC commit object, which has a human author/committer and no AI marker. The AI-assisted 2026 fix cannot attribute the introducer, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

At 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^, `git grep -n HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH -- lib/bluetooth/hci.h src/eir.c` shows HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248 and name2utf8 declares `char utf8_name[HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 2]`; `git blame -L 136,150 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -- src/eir.c` attributes the buffer, memset, attacker-sized `strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)`, strip, and duplicate lines to 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22.

`git blame -L 250,306 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -- src/eir.c` reproduces the length path: uint8_t field_len, `len += field_len + 1`, only an aggregate `len > eir_len` rejection, `data_len = field_len - 1`, and name fields passed as `name2utf8(data, data_len)`. `git grep -n -C 25 'btd_adapter_device_found(adapter, &ev->addr.bdaddr' 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -- src/adapter.c` shows the remote MGMT Device Found event supplies its eir/eir_len to the discovery path, and the callee's data_len is uint8_t, permitting 255.

`git log 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -L ':name2utf8:src/eir.c'` and `git log master --reverse -S 'strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)' -- src/eir.c` both reach 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 as the first writer of the vulnerable EIR sink; the later 218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99 only removes the valid-UTF-8 fast path and changes conversion, while the unsafe buffer and variable-length copy remain attributed to 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22.

`git show --find-renames --find-copies 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` shows the newly added name2utf8 and the name-case call replacing the parent's validation/g_strndup path. `git rev-parse 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22^` returns 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e; `git grep -n -e name2utf8 -e 'strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)' 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e -- src/eir.c` has no match, while `git grep -n -C 6 g_utf8_validate 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e -- src/eir.c` shows malformed names were rejected and accepted names used g_strndup.

Release ancestry establishes the source boundary: `git describe --contains --match='5.*' 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` returns `5.0~2624`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` succeeds for introducer versus 5.0^{} and fails versus 4.101^{}, so the unsafe source first shipped in 5.0. This is broader than the advisory UI's explicit affected-version entry of 5.86. The fix was committed after both 5.86 and 5.87: ancestry fails for 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2 versus 5.87^{}, and `git tag --contains 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2` is empty in the validated clone, so no observed release tag contains the fix yet.

`git show --format=fuller 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2` is the direct repair: it adds `len = MIN(len, HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH);` immediately before memset/strncpy and changes no other file. Thus the advisory fix and the smallest direct fix are the same commit.

`git cat-file commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` provides the BIC-only provenance check: tree 2650a41bd430d9a9acb38ece9975d5bb5630df6e, parent 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e, human author/committer Johan Hedberg, and no AI/bot marker or trailer. Any AI assistance recorded on the 2026 fix is outside the protocol's BIC-only judgment.
review_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is the unbounded copy in the EIR name conversion sink, not the 2025 conversion refactor and not the 2026 fix. Line history and pickaxe agree that 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 first wrote the fixed stack array plus variable-length copy and first routed EIR names through it. Its direct parent has neither the sink nor the vulnerable route, instead rejecting invalid UTF-8 and using a bounded allocation, so parent absence is directly proven. The commit is a normal 2012 human-authored commit object with no AI disclosure or bot identity. Under the required BIC-only rule the closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI.

audit_record.bug_semantics: AuthorizationServerHandler parses the raw JSON body rather than the endpoint DTO and copies every recognized identifier, including an undeclared attacker-added workspaceId and a victim connectionId/sourceId/destinationId, into X-Airbyte-* headers. AuthenticationHeaderResolver.resolveWorkspace then trusts X-Airbyte-Workspace-Id before any resource-derived header, so the role check is performed against the attacker's workspace while the endpoint handler operates on the victim resource; no later ownership comparison reconnects the authorization decision to the resource.
audit_record.flaw_origin: afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d introduced AuthenticationHeaderResolver and wired request headers into Keycloak role lookup. Its initial resolveWorkspace if/else puts WORKSPACE_ID_HEADER ahead of CONNECTION_ID_HEADER, destination, job, source, operation, and config lookups, without checking that simultaneous identifiers resolve to the same workspace. The raw-body header extractor already existed in the parent, so this commit is the smallest repository commit that completed the vulnerable per-workspace authorization mechanism.

audit_record.reasoning: The lifecycle is: the raw request-body extractor and AuthenticationId.WORKSPACE_ID already existed; afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d then created the resolver, made caller-derived workspaceId the first workspace choice, and used that choice to fetch the caller's RBAC role. This completed the confused-deputy path: a valid role in workspace A authorizes an operation whose resource ID belongs to workspace B. review_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated member of workspace A can send a request body containing a resource identifier owned by workspace B (for example connectionId, sourceId, or destinationId) plus an otherwise undeclared workspaceId for workspace A. AuthorizationServerHandler parses the raw JSON before endpoint-schema binding and copies both values into X-Airbyte-* headers. AuthenticationHeaderResolver.resolveWorkspace gives X-Airbyte-Workspace-Id priority over all resource-derived headers, so RBAC checks the caller's permission in A while the endpoint later acts on the B resource identifier. Because no later ownership comparison binds that resource to the authorized workspace, the caller can read configuration, trigger or cancel syncs, or delete cross-workspace resources at the privilege level held in A.
review_record.flaw_origin: The exploitable authorization mismatch first became real in afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d. That commit added AuthenticationHeaderResolver with WORKSPACE_ID_HEADER as the first resolveWorkspace branch, ahead of connection/source/destination lookup, and changed KeycloakTokenValidator from unconditional ADMIN to request-scoped permission lookup using that resolver. It composed unsafely with the already-present raw-body-to-header extractor introduced by ec53cc9f8267b9fda31219ecc10827f6965c6f3f. The immediate parent had the extractor and workspaceId enumeration but no AuthenticationHeaderResolver and no request-header-derived workspace RBAC decision, so it lacked the specific split between authorized workspace and acted-on resource.

The direct parent was checked and lacks both the resolver file and request-derived RBAC path. audit_record.bug_semantics: When the opt-in Management API is enabled with its token left empty, its authentication middleware treats the empty secret as successful authentication. The server listens on all interfaces at port 9820, and an unauthenticated remote POST to /api/v1/cron can copy attacker-controlled JSON exec text into a persisted CronJob. The cron scheduler identifies a nonempty Exec as a shell job and ultimately runs that text through the configured shell, so the attacker obtains command execution when the job fires; later code also added an immediate /api/v1/cron/{id}/exec trigger, but that was not necessary for the original scheduled-execution path.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The vulnerable trust-boundary crossing was created in one change: c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 added the network-facing Management API, deliberately made authenticate return true for an empty token, registered the cron endpoints behind that fail-open middleware, and assigned untrusted req.Exec directly to CronJob.Exec. The shell-capable CronJob and its sh -c execution sink already existed in the parent; c2681402 is the smallest commit that made that sink reachable from an unauthenticated remote management request.
audit_record.ai_marker: BIC commit object c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 has author and committer chenhg5 <chenhonggui@wps.cn> and contains the exact message markers 'generated by llmgit' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'.
audit_record.evidence: Advisory GHSA-v2jj-5g64-rxp4 / CVE-2026-76761 names core/engine.go shellExecCommand and Management API command injection through exec; first-party report https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/issues/1489 documents the complete POST /api/v1/cron -> CronJob.Exec -> scheduler -> shellExecCommand chain and maintainer confirmation. At BIC c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380, core/management.go:55-85 starts an HTTP server on :<port>, lines 69-71 register /api/v1/cron, lines 96-124 wrap requests but return true when m.token is empty, and lines 922-973 decode CronAddRequest and assign Exec: req.Exec before AddJob. The same commit adds cmd/cc-connect/main.go startup wiring and config/config.go ManagementConfig; enabled is opt-in/default false, but token is an unchecked string and the example calls it required without enforcing that requirement. In immediate parent 968cd9142dd7a9f7f1ea09a45cb7329761c44abb, git grep shows core/cron.go already defines CronJob.Exec and core/engine.go:613 runs job.Exec with exec.CommandContext(ctx, 'sh', '-c', job.Exec), but git ls-tree for core/management.go is empty. Direct tree comparison reports 'A core/management.go', proving the remote fail-open path and req.Exec assignment are absent from the immediate parent. git log -L 325,327:core/management.go HEAD attributes the empty-token true return only to c2681402; git log -L 1572,1575 attributes Exec: req.Exec only to c2681402; git log -S 'if m.token == ""' --all likewise returns only c2681402. The BIC is a one-parent public commit, not a merge; no smaller public member commit is present or referenced, so squash decomposition is not applicable. Version boundary: v1.2.2-beta.1 (ecea1ef36d86bb70dd633fb342f655d108ea52cb) predates the file, while the v1.2.2-beta.1..v1.2.2-beta.2 diff adds core/management.go and git tag --contains c2681402 starts at v1.2.2-beta.2; c2681402 is also contained in advisory-named v1.4.1. No fix was found: git grep at v1.4.1, v1.5.0, and audited HEAD 80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4 still finds both 'if m.token == ""' and 'Exec: req.Exec' in core/management.go. Thus the textual 'up to 1.4.1' boundary reflects the latest version considered by the advisory, not a patched 1.4.2 boundary; v1.5.0 and HEAD remain vulnerable. BIC-only AI evidence comes from git cat-file commit c2681402 and the public commit object at https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/commit/c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380, which carry the llmgit and Claude co-author markers.
audit_record.reasoning: The preexisting cron shell facility is not by itself the reported Management API vulnerability: before c2681402 there was no core/management.go and therefore no network management route accepting attacker-controlled cron JSON. Commit c2681402 completes the vulnerable lifecycle in the smallest recorded unit by exposing the API on all interfaces, authorizing every request whenever the configured token is empty, accepting exec, and storing it in the already shell-executable CronJob. Its direct parent lacks the entire file, while both origin-tracing methods identify c2681402 as the first writer of the decisive fail-open check and remote-to-shell assignment. The first vulnerable tagged boundary is v1.2.2-beta.2 and the mechanism persists through v1.4.1, v1.5.0, and the audited HEAD, so there is no fix SHA to record. AI attribution is closed from the BIC commit object alone: the same causal first-writer commit explicitly says it was generated by llmgit and co-authored by Claude. That satisfies AI_ROOT_CAUSE rather than AI_CODE_FLAWED because the AI-marked BIC itself created the flawed authentication and dataflow, not merely a later refactor or fix.
audit_record.remaining_gap: Unpatched as of audited HEAD 80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4 (2026-08-28): no fix_sha or direct_fix_sha exists, and the advisory's 'up to 1.4.1' wording does not identify a patched release even though v1.5.0 and HEAD retain the vulnerable lines.

A remote caller can POST an arbitrary exec string to /api/v1/cron; that string is persisted as CronJob.Exec and executed by the cron scheduler through shellExecCommand with the shell command flag (-c on Unix). audit_record.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /_instatic/hole/<nodeId> handler treats the attacker-controlled u parameter as the originating page URL and uses its path, slug, and query to render a shared hole, but its process-wide cache key contains only nodeId, publish version, and u's normalized inner query. Because u's pathname is content-varying but absent from the key, an attacker can render route-dependent HTML for a chosen pathname into the slot later used by a legitimate request with the same nodeId, version, and query.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit f066a8838e49ba211250c56c2955a25689e5e7ca first forwarded location.pathname + location.search as u, parsed u into pageUrl, exposed pageUrl-derived route.path and route.slug to rendering and request-dependent loop sources, and simultaneously keyed shared-hole responses as v=<version>&normalizeQuery(pageUrl.searchParams), omitting the content-varying pageUrl pathname. The older hole cache existed, but its parent did not accept u or render from an attacker-selected page URL, so it did not contain this poisoning mechanism.

Vulnerable flow: at current main a0b1e4e522b2b5813fa07655d34335309f520c53, server/handlers/cms/hole.ts:217 reads url.searchParams.get('u'), lines 220-226 turn it into pageUrl and route, lines 229 and 252-257 pass its query/path/slug into rendering, while lines 258-262 key getOrRender by nodeId plus v and normalizeQuery(pageUrl.searchParams), not pageUrl.pathname. server/publish/holeRuntime.ts:38-39 sends location.pathname + location.search as u. audit_record.reasoning: The original Layer C hole feature cached fragments, but before f066a8838e49ba211250c56c2955a25689e5e7ca the endpoint had no attacker-controlled originating-page URL and did not derive route-sensitive output from u. The BIC made u influence the rendered route path/slug and source request while varying the shared key only by u's query. Two requests whose u values have different pathnames but the same inner query therefore collide; the first unauthenticated request populates the process-wide entry and subsequent legitimate visitors receive its route-dependent body until invalidation or eviction. Both the tainted render input and the incomplete cache key first appear together in this single non-merge commit, so no squash decomposition is needed, and the immediate parent directly proves the mechanism absent. The BIC predates and belongs to every tagged release, satisfying the lower affected boundary, but public history disproves a patch at 0.0.15: later tags and main retain the vulnerable lines, so no real fix SHA can be supplied. Under the BIC-only attribution rule, the human author/committer and complete absence of AI trailers or bot identity require NOT_AI.
audit_record.remaining_gap: The vulnerability remains unpatched in the available public history through main a0b1e4e522b2b5813fa07655d34335309f520c53 (2026-08-21): there is no fix or direct-fix SHA, and the advisory supplies no patched version or fix reference. Its claim 'through 0.0.14' is inconsistent with unchanged vulnerable code in public v0.0.15 and v0.0.16.

An attacker can therefore prime a shared hole entry with a chosen pathname/slug; a later victim request for the same node, version, and query but a different legitimate pathname receives the attacker's cached rendering.

The later 78bb498666f07a532da8ed985ebce8e7b73619f4 project rename only changed /_pb to /_instatic and did not create the key/dependency mismatch.

audit_record.bug_semantics: When persistent proxy memory is enabled, the proxy used the client-controlled x-headroom-user-id header as the memory partition key without authenticating or binding that identifier to the caller. A reachable client could select another user's partition, disclose stored memory through search/context injection, and create, update, or delete records in that partition. The shipped compose deployment made the data plane network-reachable by binding 0.0.0.0 and publishing port 8787 without requiring a proxy token.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192 is the smallest public-history BIC. It introduced proxy memory, read memory_user_id from x-headroom-user-id in headroom/proxy/server.py, and passed that untrusted value to memory search and tool-call read/write operations implemented by the newly added headroom/proxy/memory_handler.py. Its sole parent 8c22a72715a328f1f7c3d4ba4a44516910192e80 contains neither the header selector nor proxy memory handler. Later handler splits and OpenAI, Gemini, Responses, and WebSocket additions moved or copied the already-vulnerable identity selection and are not introducers.

primary_record.bug_semantics: When proxy memory is enabled, the proxy treats the caller-controlled x-headroom-user-id header as the authoritative memory partition key without authenticating or otherwise binding that value to the caller. A remote client can select a victim identifier, causing memory search results to be injected into the attacker's LLM context and memory tool operations to read, create, update, or delete records in the victim's partition; this is a CWE-639 confidentiality and integrity failure.
primary_record.flaw_origin: Commit da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192 first integrated persistent memory into the network proxy and wrote memory_user_id = headers.get("x-headroom-user-id") in headroom/proxy/server.py, then passed that untrusted value directly to search_and_format_context and handle_memory_tool_calls. The pre-existing reference docker-compose configuration already bound the proxy to 0.0.0.0 and published port 8787, and the BIC added no caller authentication or identity binding, so the new partition selector was remotely attacker-controlled in the shipped deployment model.

review_record.bug_semantics: When persistent proxy memory is enabled, the proxy used the client-controlled x-headroom-user-id header verbatim as the memory partition key. That value flowed into search_memories and save/update/delete operations and into context/tool handling, without authentication or any binding between the selected partition and the caller. A client able to reach a data-plane route could therefore choose another user's identifier, retrieve that user's stored LLM memory through context/search, and write or alter memory in that partition. The flaw began on the original Anthropic memory-enabled proxy path, was later copied to OpenAI Chat Completions, Gemini, OpenAI Responses, and OpenAI websocket paths, and was practically network-reachable in the reference compose deployment because it bound the proxy to 0.0.0.0 and published port 8787 without requiring HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN. Fix 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 centralizes identity selection in resolve_memory_identity: the header is honored only for a loopback peer (or by a deployment-supplied authenticated resolver); a remote peer instead gets the configured proxy-token fingerprint or OS-user fallback. The same fix requires a proxy token in the shipped compose file.

audit_record.bug_semantics: In SPIP 4.4.20, analyse_resultat_skel() examined the inner text of each PHP block with an anchored header() regular expression that mistakenly retained PCRE's multiline modifier. Because ^ and $ therefore matched individual lines rather than the whole PHP block, an unauthenticated attacker could inject a newline-delimited header("X-Spip-Filtre: intval|_request|system") line into generated template code. SPIP extracted that attacker-selected filter chain, intval reduced the body to the key 0, _request read attacker-controlled POST parameter 0, and system executed it, yielding pre-authentication remote code execution.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The vulnerable product code is in the upstream spip/ecrire repository, not in the bundled rapid7/metasploit-framework reference. Commit d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d rewrote public/composer.php to collect individual PHP blocks and first added the vulnerable /^...$/ims match over each block's innerHtml. Its immediate parent used a materially different whole-page preg_match_all implementation and did not contain this vulnerable collector-plus-multiline-anchors mechanism. Rapid7 commit b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c only added an exploit module and documentation after the SPIP flaw existed; it neither introduced nor fixed SPIP.

review_record.bug_semantics: SPIP 4.4.20's analyse_resultat_skel() parsed each PHP block and applied an anchored header() regular expression with the PCRE m modifier. Because m makes ^ and $ match individual lines, an attacker-controlled newline followed by header("X-Spip-Filtre: intval|_request|system") inside a larger compiled PHP block was accepted as if the whole block were an intended SPIP header emission. X-Spip-Filtre was then interpreted as a pipe-delimited callable filter chain: intval produced key 0, _request read attacker-controlled POST parameter 0, and system executed that value, yielding unauthenticated remote command execution.
review_record.flaw_origin: The vulnerable product code is in upstream SPIP's spip/ecrire repository, not rapid7/metasploit-framework. This was the 4.4.20 remediation for the preceding all-version RCE, but carrying m into the newly anchored matcher created the CVE-2026-77806 bypass. The Rapid7 commit referenced by the advisory, b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c, only adds a Metasploit exploit module and documentation and is neither the BIC nor the fix.

audit_record.bug_semantics: With OAuth enabled behind a reverse proxy that terminates browser-facing HTTPS and forwards the callback to Temporal UI Server over HTTP, authentication cookies used c.Request().TLS != nil to choose Secure. That request describes only the proxy-to-server hop, so the server could emit user* access/ID-token cookies and, later, refresh-token cookies without Secure even though the browser authenticated over HTTPS. Exploitation additionally requires steering the UI hostname to attacker-served HTTP, preventing HTTPS, and receiving a later same-site plaintext request while the credential is live; malicious content alone or passive observation of the successful TLS session is insufficient.

primary_record.bug_semantics: With OAuth enabled behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy, Temporal UI Server created browser authentication cookies with Secure set from c.Request().TLS, which describes only the proxy-to-server hop. When that hop was HTTP, the access-token user cookies (and later refresh-token cookies when an IdP issued one) lacked Secure even though the browser used HTTPS. An attacker who could additionally steer the UI hostname, defeat HTTPS, serve it over HTTP, and observe a later same-site plaintext request could recover and replay the live credential.
primary_record.flaw_origin: The original ui-server commit replaced always-Secure server-side session cookies with browser-resident user0/userN cookies containing the OAuth access token and set each cookie's Secure field to c.Request().TLS != nil. That made a deployment-internal transport property control a browser-facing cookie security boundary. The monorepo later imported this already-flawed code, and later refresh/session work reused the same derivation; neither the import nor those extensions are the first root-cause commit.

review_record.bug_semantics: When LiquidJS renders attacker-controlled template source with memoryLimit enabled, evalRangeToken meters a range as high - low + 1. A reverse range such as (100000000..1) therefore passes a large negative count to Limiter.use(); the vulnerable limiter accepts it and subtracts it from its cumulative base. Later positive allocations then satisfy base + count <= limit despite exceeding the configured budget. Repeated append operations can build a 134217728-character V8 cons-string, and replace forces flattening into a contiguous buffer, producing an uncatchable V8 fatal error and process-wide denial of service.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0 attempted to fix unmetered ranges in for tags by adding exactly ctx.memoryLimit.use(high - low + 1) to evalRangeToken, but assumed low <= high. Its direct parent already had the generic Limiter, whose signed accumulator did not reject negative counts, but did not meter ranges and therefore lacked this reverse-range counter-poisoning path. The BIC is the smallest commit in which the advisory's signed range charge and permissive limiter coexist; it is a direct one-parent change, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate.

audit_record.bug_semantics: LiquidJS promised to bound each render with renderLimit, but Render.renderTemplates checked elapsed time only inside its loop over template nodes. An empty for or tablerow body parses to an empty templates array, so every attacker-controlled collection iteration calls renderTemplates([]), executes no check, and consumes CPU linearly up to the separate memoryLimit while bypassing the configured wall-clock budget.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 introduced the renderLimit feature and its first enforcement point as ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now()) inside for (const tpl of templates). The existing for and tablerow tags could pass an empty body array once per collection element, so placing the new security check exclusively inside the zero-trip inner loop created the bypass at the moment the guard was introduced.

review_record.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-44645 / GHSA-8xx9-69p8-7jp3 is a CPU/event-loop denial of service in LiquidJS's renderLimit control. The for and tablerow parsers store their bodies as Template[] arrays. An empty body therefore makes each collection iteration call Render.renderTemplates([], ctx, emitter). In vulnerable releases, the only ctx.renderLimit.check(...) was inside `for (const tpl of templates)`, so an empty array executed no check while the outer for/tag or tablerow/tag loop still traversed the entire attacker-selected collection; tablerow additionally emitted table markup. A low-privileged author of an untrusted Liquid template could use an empty `{% for i in (1..N) %}{% endfor %}` or empty tablerow to consume CPU far beyond the configured time budget, bounded only by other resource controls such as memoryLimit.
review_record.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 (`feat: DoS prevention, #250`). That commit introduced the renderLimit option, its Limiter state, the documented security guarantee, and the sole enforcement call in src/render/render.ts inside the per-template loop. The pre-existing Render.renderTemplates loop naturally did nothing for an empty Template[]; e443068 made that placement security-relevant by promising a per-render time limit but checking only when a body node existed. `git log e443068... -L 14,23:src/render/render.ts` attributes that exact check insertion to e443068, and `git log e443068... -S'ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now())' -- src/render/render.ts` plus `-S'renderLimit?: number' -- src/liquid-options.ts` independently return e443068. audit_record.bug_semantics: The default-registered strip_html filter applied one global regular expression containing unbounded lazy script, style, comment, and generic-tag alternatives directly to attacker-controlled template data. On many opener tokens without a matching closer, V8 retries an alternative at each '<' and scans the remaining suffix looking for the absent terminator, producing quadratic work on the single Node.js event-loop thread. memoryLimit did not bound that CPU work because it charged only the input string length before String.replace ran.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 replaced the prior simple tag regex in filters.js with the Ruby-Liquid-compatible /<script.*?<\/script>|<!--.*?-->|<style.*?<\/style>|<.*?>/g expression. That functional-parity change first introduced the unbounded lazy alternatives and therefore the vulnerable repeated-suffix search; later moves and expansions preserved or broadened the same mechanism rather than originating it.

review_record.bug_semantics: The default-registered strip_html filter runs a lazy-alternation regular expression directly over caller-controlled template data. For inputs containing many '<script', '<style', '<!--', or generic '<' openers without their required terminator, V8 retries a tail-spanning lazy match at each opener, producing O(N^2) work and blocking Node's single event loop. At the last vulnerable revision, src/filters/html.ts charges only str.length to memoryLimit (whose default is Infinity), so that accounting neither caps nor interrupts regex CPU consumption.
review_record.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887. It changed filters.js strip_html from /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g to /<script.*?<\/script>|<!--.*?-->|<style.*?<\/style>|<.*?>/g, first introducing the repeated tail scans responsible for this ReDoS. Later commits only transported or modified the already-vulnerable expression: 677e8511e60a7cc789dd33a4f295a46beeaf1137 copied it into src/builtin/filters/html.ts during the TypeScript refactor, 42d25902e855d3c06d5ead071bf55604f495c205 broadened three alternatives to [\s\S], and 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045 broadened the generic tag alternative. None is the first causal writer.
review_record.ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887` shows author Paul Robert Lloyd <me+git@paulrobertlloyd.com>, committer Jun Yang <harttle@harttle.com>, and only the message 'Ensure strip_html filter uses same regex as Ruby Liquid'; it contains no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker.

audit_record.bug_semantics: LiquidJS accepted a lexically resolved template pathname as proof that the file opened was inside a configured root, partials, or layouts directory. Node then followed symlinks at the file operation, so a symlink placed under an allowed template directory could point to an arbitrary readable file outside that directory and include, render, or layout would parse and render the external target. The assigned advisory records liquidjs <= 10.25.2 as vulnerable and 10.25.3 as the first patched version.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 8fbbec089fa4e3db4bec47462b1c08dd65c36648 is the smallest real BIC. Although the commit also moved existing modules, its newly added index.js handleCache() resolved an include name with path.resolve(this.options.root, filepath) and passed that non-canonical pathname to fs.readFileSync(), while the newly added tags/include.js evaluated the include name and called handleCache(). The immediate parent had neither handleCache/renderFile nor tags/include.js, so the causal filesystem-template load path was absent; later loader extractions, path checks, and file moves merely preserved or re-expressed this same symlink-following flaw.

review_record.bug_semantics: LiquidJS formed include/render/layout candidate names beneath configured root, partials, or layouts directories and then opened those names without canonicalizing them. An attacker who can place a symlink under an allowed template directory can point it at any readable file outside the directory: the lexical pathname passes the root check, Node follows the symlink during stat/read, and the external target is parsed and rendered. This affects async and sync loading and can disclose arbitrary readable content; the advisory records liquidjs <=10.25.2 as vulnerable and 10.25.3 as the first patched release.
review_record.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is 8fbbec089fa4e3db4bec47462b1c08dd65c36648 (tag:include). audit_record.bug_semantics: LiquidJS strip_html returned attacker-controlled HTML tags containing CR or LF instead of tag-stripped text. primary_record.bug_semantics: LiquidJS strip_html treated its output as tag-stripped text, but the generic-tag alternative <.*?> used JavaScript dot without dotAll, so it could not consume CR or LF inside angle brackets. Browsers accept those line terminators as whitespace between a tag name and attributes; consequently an attacker-controlled value such as <img\nsrc=x\nonerror=alert(1)> survived strip_html and became executable HTML/XSS when rendered without a separate escaping step.
primary_record.flaw_origin: Commit 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 replaced the older tag-name-only strip_html regex in filters.js with a Ruby-Liquid-style alternation whose new generic branch was <.*?>. That one-line change first wrote the exact vulnerable construct: JavaScript '.' stops at CR/LF while browsers continue parsing the tag. Later moves and refactors preserved it. Commit 42d25902e855d3c06d5ead071bf55604f495c205 made script, style, and comment alternatives multiline-safe with [\s\S] but retained <.*?>; it sharpened the inconsistency described by the advisory but is not the BIC because the flawed generic branch already existed in its parent.

audit_record.bug_semantics: Preact distinguishes genuine VNodes by giving them an own constructor value of undefined. In the affected client renderer, the gate became `if (newVNode.constructor != UNDEFINED) return NULL`; JavaScript loose equality treats null and undefined as equal, so a JSON-parsed attacker object shaped as a VNode and carrying `constructor: null` passes the gate. If an application passes that unsanitized object into the render tree, Preact consumes its attacker-controlled type and props as a VNode and can inject HTML, with script execution possible where CSP or other defenses do not stop it. The companion loose `childVNode.constructor == UNDEFINED` check also admits null as the VNode sentinel in child processing. The server-side preact-render-to-string path was not affected.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The smallest first-writer is PR #4723 member 017ac5e370c9198b12b61818279eb84f221d7747, a byte-golfing refactor that changed the JSON-injection guard in src/diff/index.js from strict `!== UNDEFINED` to loose `!= UNDEFINED` and the VNode child check in src/diff/children.js from strict `=== UNDEFINED` to loose `== UNDEFINED`. Its second member 7ed5aeb0246305e3b42e314c1a59bcaa405e6a8c restored three unrelated strict comparisons but retained both vulnerable changes; GitHub then squash-merged the resulting tree as a69aada2799626d3afbfc1eb6550611ca2444a4d. An older loose isValidElement check alone was not sufficient because the strict renderer gate still rejected forged JSON objects; 017ac5e370c9198b12b61818279eb84f221d7747 is the first commit that softened the enforcement point and made the advisory's render path exploitable.

primary_record.bug_semantics: Preact distinguishes genuine VNodes by giving them an own constructor value of undefined. In the affected client renderer, the gate became `if (newVNode.constructor != UNDEFINED) return NULL`; JavaScript loose equality treats null and undefined as equal, so a JSON-parsed attacker object shaped as a VNode and carrying `constructor: null` passes the gate. If an application passes that unsanitized object into the render tree, Preact consumes its attacker-controlled type and props as a VNode and can inject HTML, with script execution possible where CSP or other defenses do not stop it. The companion loose `childVNode.constructor == UNDEFINED` check also admits null as the VNode sentinel in child processing. The server-side preact-render-to-string path was not affected.

review_record.bug_semantics: Preact's client renderer accepts only genuine VNodes, whose createVNode path gives them an own constructor value of exactly undefined. The regression changed the JSON-injection gate in src/diff/index.js from newVNode.constructor !== UNDEFINED to the coercive newVNode.constructor != UNDEFINED (and similarly softened related VNode checks). An attacker-controlled JSON object can therefore supply constructor:null: because null == undefined, the loose inequality is false and the gate does not reject the object. If unvalidated JSON-derived data is passed as a child/render value, an object such as {type:'span',props:{children:'Malicious'},__v:1,constructor:null} is treated as a VNode and can inject HTML, potentially script-capable markup absent CSP. The server-side preact-render-to-string path was not affected.
