review_record.flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructed first-writer is PR #4795 member 3b0152f33b2c03ddd2b86c6ec8541661e01b039a: it added EngineUIProxyServlet.scala, parsed host and port from the request path, formed http://<host>:<port>/..., registered the /engine-ui servlet, and attached it to KyuubiRestFrontendService without any destination policy. The main-branch squash 4cd00a8777043fca4348d2c2f3a2b0b6e358e028 is only the aggregate landing commit, not the smallest BIC.
review_record.ai_marker: Absent on BIC 3b0152f33b2c03ddd2b86c6ec8541661e01b039a. Its commit object names human author zwangsheng <2213335496@qq.com>, human committer Cheng Pan <chengpan@apache.org>, and has the one-line message '[KYUUBI #3420][UI] Proxy Engnie UI' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI attribution trailer. AI disclosure on the 2026 fix is excluded because only the BIC commit object is admissible.
review_record.evidence: Apache's first-party advisory at https://lists.apache.org/thread/ps79fcfx49ox9kwgztc5t5bw0tyhck9m states the request-path host/port SSRF/open-proxy mechanism, affected range 1.8.0 before 1.12.0, and upgrade/configuration remedy. In the validated clone, `git log --follow -- kyuubi-server/src/main/scala/org/apache/kyuubi/server/api/EngineUIProxyServlet.scala` starts at squash 4cd00a8777043fca4348d2c2f3a2b0b6e358e028; `git log -L 31,49:kyuubi-server/src/main/scala/org/apache/kyuubi/server/api/EngineUIProxyServlet.scala aa58942b57eb21a67ce97a4b6404b2d9c0cce878` attributes the unrestricted rewrite to 4cd00a8777043fca4348d2c2f3a2b0b6e358e028, while `git log --all -S'new URL("http", host, port' -- .../EngineUIProxyServlet.scala` returns 4cd00a8777043fca4348d2c2f3a2b0b6e358e028 as the addition and 7067644e1bf469a761b0516ce73b432a2ebf9f9d as its removal. `git show 4cd00a8777043fca4348d2c2f3a2b0b6e358e028` identifies all eight squashed PR members. https://api.github.com/repos/apache/kyuubi/pulls/4795/commits resolves those members; https://api.github.com/repos/apache/kyuubi/commits/3b0152f33b2c03ddd2b86c6ec8541661e01b039a shows the first member added EngineUIProxyServlet.scala with request-derived host/port and parent cb689b66b1ed745a5e38dea37a2b0f1d9e7f1aca. Direct parent verification with `git grep -n -e EngineUIProxyServlet -e engine-ui cb689b66b1ed745a5e38dea37a2b0f1d9e7f1aca -- kyuubi-server/src/main kyuubi-server/web-ui/src` returns no match, whereas the BIC API diff marks the servlet file added and shows registration of the handler. `git show 7067644e1bf469a761b0516ce73b432a2ebf9f9d` shows the closing change: proxy disabled by default, explicit allowed-host patterns when enabled, strict URI parsing, and null/403 for disallowed targets; its direct parent aa58942b57eb21a67ce97a4b6404b2d9c0cce878 still contains `new URL("http", host, port, ...)` and lacks FRONTEND_REST_ENGINE_UI_PROXY_ENABLED. `git tag --contains 4cd00a8777043fca4348d2c2f3a2b0b6e358e028 --list 'v1.7*' 'v1.8.0'` returns only v1.8.0; `git grep` shows the unrestricted constructor in v1.8.0 and v1.11.1; `git tag --contains 7067644e1bf469a761b0516ce73b432a2ebf9f9d --list 'v1.11*' 'v1.12*'` returns v1.12.0/v1.12.0-rc0 only, and v1.12.0 contains allowedTarget plus the proxy-enabled configuration default false. The BIC API's signed commit payload reproduces the human identities and trailer-free one-line message used for the AI check.
review_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is the destination-trust decision, not the later query-string enhancement: the very first proxy implementation already let the requester select the outbound host and port. Main history exposes that implementation as squash 4cd00a8777043fca4348d2c2f3a2b0b6e358e028, but the retained PR chain proves that 3b0152f33b2c03ddd2b86c6ec8541661e01b039a is the smaller original writer and that its immediate parent lacks both the servlet and route. The Apache advisory, ancestry/tag checks, vulnerable tagged blobs, and fixed tagged policy agree on 1.8.0 <= version < 1.12.0 and on 7067644e1bf469a761b0516ce73b432a2ebf9f9d as the closing mainline fix. Because the only admissible object for attribution is the decomposed BIC and that object contains only human identities with no AI marker, the closed verdict is NOT_AI; the fix commit's Assisted-by: OpenCode (GPT-5.5) disclosure cannot causally attribute the 2023 flaw.

audit_record.bug_semantics: AIT CSV Import/Export through 3.0.3 exposed admin/upload-handler.php as a directly reachable unauthenticated multipart upload endpoint. It neither restricted the uploaded file to safe CSV content/types nor prevented a PHP filename from being placed in WordPress's web-executable wp-content/uploads directory. Parsing could subsequently fail, but the file had already been retained; requesting that uploaded PHP file therefore produced unauthenticated remote code execution, even when the plugin was installed but inactive.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The causal code belonged to AIT Themes' proprietary ait-csv-import-export WordPress plugin, specifically admin/upload-handler.php: the handler accepted attacker-controlled multipart file content without an authentication gate or dangerous-type validation and persisted it into the public uploads tree before CSV parsing established that it was valid. rapid7/metasploit-framework contains only a later exploit client and documentation, not this vulnerable server-side handler or the vendor's source history.
audit_record.ai_marker: not assessable: there is no BIC commit object for the vulnerable AIT Themes handler in the assigned repository or in an identified public vendor repository; per the BIC-only rule, the later Metasploit exploit commit was not used for AI attribution
audit_record.evidence: Advisory lifecycle: NVD's CVE-2025-34083 record is REJECTED as a duplicate of CVE-2020-36849; the canonical CVE-2020-36849 record identifies missing file-type validation in /wp-content/plugins/ait-csv-import-export/admin/upload-handler.php through 3.0.3 and labels the Rapid7 files as Exploit references, not product source. WPScan (WPVDB 36e699a4-91f2-426d-ba14-26036fbfeaea) reports a honeypot request to that handler on 2020-11-12, successful reproduction against then-current 3.0.3, a multipart curl PoC, and unsuccessful vendor contact before its 2020-11-13 disclosure. Version boundary: the archived first-party vendor page at web.archive.org/web/20201114060042id_/https://www.ait-themes.club/wordpress-plugins/csv-import-export/ lists current v3.0.3 (2020-08-06); the archived 2021-01-30 page lists v3.0.4 released 2020-12-17 with changelog entry 'Fix: CSV file upload'. Rapid7 independently encodes the boundary as target '<3.0.4' and checks against 3.0.4. Repository boundary: `git log --follow -- modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb` begins at d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135 (parent a4a7efddb756c887a08780562e37f77fe199f34d) on 2021-01-01, after disclosure and after the vendor's 3.0.4 release. `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status -r d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135` shows only two additions: documentation/modules/exploit/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.md and modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb. `git show` confirms those files describe/test 3.0.3 and send a PHP payload to the external plugin endpoint, then request it from wp-content/uploads; they do not implement the vulnerable handler. Finally, `git log --all --full-history -- ':(glob)**/upload-handler.php'` returns no commits. Thus d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135 is demonstrably an exploit-module addition, not a vulnerability introducer or fix, and no immediate-parent absence claim for the real vulnerable lines can be made.
audit_record.reasoning: The attack path and release boundary are reconstructable: an unauthenticated POST reaches the plugin's standalone upload handler, attacker-chosen PHP is persisted under the executable uploads URL before the attempted CSV parse rejects it, and a follow-up GET executes it. Public exploitation was observed while 3.0.3 was current; the vendor later published 3.0.4 with an upload fix. The smallest BIC, however, must be the vendor commit that first wrote the unsafe authentication/validation/persistence sequence. The assigned Rapid7 history starts only when an exploit for the already disclosed and already patched third-party product was added; its parent lacks the exploit module, but that fact says nothing about absence of the vulnerable vendor lines and cannot satisfy BIC parent verification. A move/refactor/squash decomposition is therefore inapplicable. The AIT plugin was paid/proprietary, GitHub's advisory says 'No known source code', the current vendor site treats it as a legacy product, and neither a public vendor VCS history nor commit objects for 3.0.3/3.0.4 were identified. Consequently introducer/fix SHAs, immediate-parent absence, tag membership, and BIC-only AI metadata cannot be established. This is a genuine public-history boundary, so BLOCKED is more accurate than EVIDENCE_GAP and the non-causal Metasploit commit must not be labeled as the BIC merely because the advisory links to it.
audit_record.remaining_gap: The missing evidence is the vendor's commit-addressable source history for AIT CSV Import/Export admin/upload-handler.php: specifically the commit that first added the unauthenticated/unrestricted persistence path, its immediate parent tree and affected-release tags, and the commit/source diff shipped as 3.0.4 on 2020-12-17. Those objects are not in rapid7/metasploit-framework and no public AIT Themes repository or archived source package exposing them was available, so BIC/fix SHAs and BIC commit-object AI signals are inaccessible.

review_record.bug_semantics: The vulnerable product is the proprietary AIT CSV Import / Export WordPress plugin, not Metasploit. In plugin versions through 3.0.3, the directly web-reachable admin/upload-handler.php accepts an unauthenticated multipart file field without restricting the uploaded type. An attacker can submit a .php file; although the handler may report a CSV parse error, the file remains in wp-content/uploads and is web-executable, yielding unauthenticated remote code execution even when the plugin is installed but inactive. WPScan also reports possible deletion through the same handler.
review_record.flaw_origin: External proprietary AIT Themes plugin source at ait-csv-import-export/admin/upload-handler.php. The assigned rapid7/metasploit-framework repository contains only a downstream exploit module that demonstrates the flaw; it does not contain the vulnerable plugin implementation or its release history.
review_record.ai_marker: Unavailable: the true BIC commit object for the proprietary AIT plugin is not present in the assigned repository or in known public source history, so no BIC-only author, committer, bot identity, or AI trailer can be inspected. The downstream Metasploit exploit-module commit object was deliberately not substituted for the BIC.
evidence: Alias resolution: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-34083 reports that CVE-2025-34083 was rejected as a duplicate of CVE-2020-36849. The canonical record at https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-36849 identifies missing file-type validation in /wp-content/plugins/ait-csv-import-export/admin/upload-handler.php through version 3.0.3 and cites the Rapid7 file only as an exploit.

Attack path and disclosure: https://wpscan.com/vulnerability/36e699a4-91f2-426d-ba14-26036fbfeaea records an observed GET to the handler on 2020-11-12, a working exploit against then-current 3.0.3, public disclosure on 2020-11-13, and the reproducer `curl -F 'file=@plugin.php' http://HOST/wp-content/plugins/ait-csv-import-export/admin/upload-handler.php`; it explains that the malicious file remains uploaded despite CSV parsing.

Version boundary: https://www.wordfence.com/threat-intel/vulnerabilities/wordpress-plugins/ait-csv-import-export/ait-csv-importexport-303-arbitrary-file-upload lists affected versions `* <= 3.0.3`, patched version `* 3.0.4`, and remediation to update to 3.0.4 or newer. This is corroborated by the assigned clone's module target `AIT CSV Import Export <3.0.4` and its check against 3.0.4 in modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb.

Repository mismatch: in /home/hanqing/agents/ai-slop/.ai-slop/state/repos/rapid7_metasploit-framework, `git log --all --follow --format='%H %P %ad %an %s' -- modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb` begins at d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135 (parent a4a7efddb756c887a08780562e37f77fe199f34d), dated 2021-01-01 with subject `ait csv improter exploit`, after the 2020 disclosure. `git show d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135 -- modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb` shows a new 90-line Metasploit Ruby client that uploads a generated PHP payload to the plugin endpoint and then requests it from wp-content/uploads; it is exploit evidence, not the vulnerable PHP handler.

Downstream ancestry cross-check: `git log -S'upload-handler.php' -- modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb` and `git log -L 76,90:modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb --format='%H %P %s' --no-patch` both identify only d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135 for the exploit request lines. `git ls-tree -r --name-only a4a7efddb756c887a08780562e37f77fe199f34d -- modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb` is empty, directly confirming only that the downstream exploit module was absent from its parent; it cannot establish parent absence for the external plugin flaw.

Commit-object check on the downstream-only candidate: `git cat-file commit d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135` shows author and committer `h00die <michaeltcyr@gmail.com>`, parent a4a7efddb756c887a08780562e37f77fe199f34d, and only the subject `ait csv improter exploit`, with no AI/bot trailer. Because this object did not introduce the vulnerable handler, protocol forbids using its marker absence for an AI verdict.

Public-history boundary: both https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q6q7-289w-x495 and the canonical duplicate advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p27j-qf57-7cm7 state `Source code: No known source code`; the assigned clone has no plugin source or plugin release commits. Consequently there is no public commit graph in which to run meaningful -S/-L attribution on upload-handler.php, verify its immediate parent, identify the 3.0.4 fixing commit, or inspect the true BIC commit object.
review_record.reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle is externally well established: exploitation was observed on 2020-11-12, WPScan reproduced it against 3.0.3 and disclosed it on 2020-11-13, and later records place the closing version boundary at 3.0.4. CVE-2025-34083 is only a rejected duplicate of CVE-2020-36849. The Rapid7 repository entered the record because it added a working exploit module on 2021-01-01; that commit neither shipped nor fixed the vulnerable WordPress handler. Treating that module addition as the BIC would invert causality and violate the smallest-real-BIC rule. The actual proprietary plugin history is not publicly available, so the introducer, its direct parent absence, the direct fix commit, and BIC-only AI signal cannot be reconstructed. This is a genuine source-history boundary, making BLOCKED more accurate than NOT_AI or EVIDENCE_GAP.
review_record.remaining_gap: A first-party version-controlled history (or authenticated commit/export provenance) for the AIT CSV Import / Export plugin spanning the introduction of admin/upload-handler.php through releases 3.0.3 and 3.0.4 is required to identify the smallest BIC, verify its immediate parent, locate the direct fix commit, and inspect the BIC commit object for AI markers. Public release-version claims alone cannot supply commit SHAs or commit-object provenance.

audit_record.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO treated email-verification state and token contents as client authority. The profile table's existing own-row UPDATE policy allowed an authenticated user to set the newly added is_email_verified column directly through PostgREST. Independently, the emailed verification value was only Base64-encoded JSON containing a client-selected profileId and orgSiteName; /api/verify decoded it without a signature, expiry, one-time-use check, authenticated-user binding, or ownership check and used profileId in a privileged profile update. An attacker could therefore self-verify through the profile API or forge data for the verification endpoint to mark a chosen profile verified without controlling its mailbox.
audit_record.flaw_origin: PR #215's first member commit, 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf, created the verification-email route, the /api/verify route, and the profile verification columns. It first wrote both the unsigned btoa(JSON.stringify({ profileId, orgSiteName })) token construction and the unvalidated profile update, while the pre-existing policy "Users can update own profile." permitted an authenticated owner to update all profile columns. Member 947cfc06ca3a858972e8faafd096c7f662ef6086 later changed /api/verify to getServerSupabase, completing the arbitrary-profile service-role attack path, but it retained rather than originated the client-authoritative token and update mechanism. GitHub squash bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc landed the reconstructed member series on main.
audit_record.ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object identifies author and committer as emmanuel <chifez1@gmail.com>, has the message "worked on the email verification", and has no trailers at all: no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot marker.
evidence: The first-party release https://github.com/classroomio/classroomio/releases/tag/v0.2.6 describes the two repaired mechanisms as client-side verification-status manipulation and Base64 token forgery; the disclosure at https://gist.github.com/prashunbaral/70c4f6f9d9ff8b82295623073eb41f3a documents /rest/v1/profile, /api/email/verify_email, and /api/verify?data=... and identifies versions before v0.2.6.

git log --follow on apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/verify/+server.js reaches mainline squash bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc (PR #215). The surviving origin/email-verification ref is dd71b639355ad09aa02b225e2e126975261962fa; git log from merge base 62a32a62046302c6247b863f9f39cd610125c083 reconstructs the eight listed member commits. Stable patch-id for 62a32a62046302c6247b863f9f39cd610125c083..dd71b639355ad09aa02b225e2e126975261962fa and 5a566cbb4fce2da442779386f8181c734b53caaf..bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc is identical: 31d5be347fff141758a91c5ba2cef7c805d3ea41.

git show of 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf creates apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/email/verify_email/+server.js with verificationData = JSON.stringify({ profileId, orgSiteName }) and btoa(verificationData), creates apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/verify/+server.js with atob/JSON.parse followed by profile.update({ is_email_verified: true, ... }).eq('id', profileId), and creates supabase/migrations/20240320081809_email_verification.sql adding is_email_verified and verified_at. git log --all -S'btoa(verificationData)' confirms 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf as the earliest object containing that construction; bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc is its squash landing.

Direct immediate-parent verification used git ls-tree -r 62a32a62046302c6247b863f9f39cd610125c083 for apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/email/verify_email/+server.js, apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/verify/+server.js, and supabase/migrations/20240320081809_email_verification.sql; it returned no entries. The BIC diff creates all three paths, so the vulnerable lines and columns are absent from the BIC's immediate parent tree.

At the BIC, supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql contains CREATE POLICY "Users can update own profile." ON public.profile FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = id), with no column restriction. Adding is_email_verified to that row therefore immediately exposed the direct authenticated self-verification path. PR member 947cfc06ca3a858972e8faafd096c7f662ef6086 replaces the /api/verify anon client with getServerSupabase; by v0.2.5 that helper uses PRIVATE_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE, while /api/verify has no authentication or integrity check and updates the decoded profileId.

Version-tree checks show v0.1.1 (commit a33594ab1aa7026ee39e7f44bc35d5dfe604e766) has neither verification route, while v0.1.2 (commit b1307a8f7d31ae0e9b144058dc4f6955fcadc02d) has both; git tag --contains bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc includes v0.1.2 through v0.2.5. At v0.2.5 (commit 900f5ec12979f512ae8f333312aee78973a054f5), git grep finds searchParams.get('data'), atob, and the is_email_verified update in /api/verify. Thus the repository's first tagged vulnerable boundary is v0.1.2, and the last vulnerable release is v0.2.5; the advisory's broad wording is versions before v0.2.6.

Release tag v0.2.6 dereferences exactly to 25d1a8d710fed1a4de98f02f1bcfdf215c149be5. Its direct diff replaces the Base64 JSON link with a cryptographically random stored token, checks profile/email at creation, validates existence/expiry/one-time use/current email during verification, and adds prevent_email_verification_manipulation plus a trigger blocking direct verification-flag updates outside the secure function. git grep at v0.2.6 finds searchParams.get('token'), verify_email_with_token, and the protection trigger, establishing the patched boundary and that the release commit itself is the direct fix.

git cat-file commit 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf shows tree 57edbb4866cecd53997518b23b6824c7f750a22c, sole parent 62a32a62046302c6247b863f9f39cd610125c083, author/committer emmanuel <chifez1@gmail.com>, and only the one-line message. No BIC commit-object AI attribution signal exists.
audit_record.reasoning: The advisory combines two manifestations of one broken trust boundary: verification state was directly mutable by the profile owner, and the mail-link endpoint accepted an unauthenticated, attacker-generated identity payload. primary_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated student who knows an enrolled course ID can request tutor/admin course routes directly. The application treats client-side navigation hiding and Svelte RoleBasedSecurity rendering/redirects as authorization, while route scripts and data services still execute course-ID-keyed reads without enforcing a tutor/admin role at the data boundary. As a result, all-course member profiles, attendance, submissions and answers, marks, and analytics can be returned before the client hides the slot or redirects, producing the advisory's transient sensitive-data disclosure.
primary_record.flaw_origin: 07eba6b4e0838c8d7d44a133898f8aa4256cdd7b first established the flawed shared authorization mechanism: it added src/components/RoleBasedSecurity/index.svelte, derived the current role from client stores, and rendered its slot only when allowedRoles.includes(userRole); it also hid the Submissions navigation item for role 3 and wrapped admin UI in attendance, people, and submissions routes, but added no server/data-layer role check. Existing route scripts and Supabase services remained reachable and executed independently of that render-only gate, so a crafted course URL bypassed the intended role boundary.

evidence: The assigned GitHub advisory and https://github.com/Rivek619/CVE-2025-65670 identify ClassroomIO 0.1.13 and the direct-URL course routes /analytics, /attendance, /submissions, /people, and /marks; the disclosure says a student sees privileged data momentarily before normal restrictions resume.

It creates src/components/RoleBasedSecurity/index.svelte with only a client-store role lookup and {#if allowedRoles.includes(userRole)} slot rendering; it adds role-3 navigation hiding and wraps submissions/admin controls without adding any request-time authorization.

At the BIC, src/utils/services/submissions/index.js fetchSubmissions(course_id) selects submission IDs, question answers, exercise questions/options, status, course, and submitter profile, constrained only by .match({ course_id }); the route's script can invoke this independently of whether RoleBasedSecurity renders its slot. The same commit's attendance and people changes disable or hide controls client-side while their course data remains loaded.

The repair is a three-commit linear sequence after v0.2.7: ac4fdf1dd35772a20899e36f5bf55decb1e0ebda migrates client Supabase course, people, submissions, marks, and related reads behind authenticated server endpoints and adds checkUserCoursePermissions; 97d9e490b00f8de355756bd6716d0b607b71712c updates the exercises endpoint and marks page; ac1a05f0068b638e18ed5473fd427506f64a7a1e moves course analytics to /api/courses/analytics and adds an authenticated permission check. git log --reverse v0.2.7..0.2.10 shows exactly that sequence.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated Lucee Web Administrator can configure a scheduled task with an attacker-controlled URL, publish enabled, and an attacker-chosen output path in the served webroot. The scheduler fetches the response and writes it directly to that Resource without constraining the destination or executable extension; choosing a .cfm destination turns the fetched bytes into CFML that Lucee executes with the service account's privileges.

The blind audits trace those halves farther back to consecutive 2009 Railo source imports 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63 and 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb, but those are bulk initial imports rather than the original authoring commits. primary_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated Lucee Web Administrator can create an HTTP scheduled task, then edit it with publish enabled and an attacker-chosen output file in the webroot. The scheduler fetches the remote response and copies it directly to that Resource without constraining the path or executable extension; naming the response .cfm turns attacker-controlled bytes into a server-executed CFML page running with the Lucee service account's privileges.
primary_record.flaw_origin: The vulnerable composition predates the recoverable commit history. The first public Railo Git snapshot split it across two import commits: 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63 added the administrator form that forwards url, publish, and arbitrary file values, and 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb added ExecutionThread's unrestricted HTTP-response-to-file write. The latter completes the visible mechanism, but it is a 2,414-file, 1,335,091-line source import rather than the real commit that authored the vulnerable code. Lucee later inherited the already-existing mechanism in its own root import 4e9afd8e48a71d89e7f34678edb7370c5d4b0b6c.
primary_record.ai_marker: unavailable: the smallest real BIC is behind the pre-2009 public-history boundary, so there is no BIC commit object whose author, committer, message, or trailers can be inspected; the visible import commit objects are not valid substitutes for BIC-only AI attribution

The referenced Metasploit module (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/master/modules/exploits/multi/http/lucee_scheduled_job.rb) authenticates, creates a scheduled job, edits it with publish=true and file=<webroot>/<random>.cfm, executes the job, and requests that .cfm. Its metadata dates disclosure to 2023-02-10 and explicitly characterizes the behavior as inherent platform functionality.

In current Lucee, core/src/main/cfml/context/admin/services.schedule.edit.cfm passes publish=formBool('publish') and file=nullIfEmpty(form.file) to cfadmin; core/src/main/java/lucee/runtime/schedule/ScheduleTaskImpl.java only checks that the output is a file and its parent exists; core/src/main/java/lucee/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java obtains task.getResource() and calls IOUtil.write or IOUtil.copy on the fetched response when publish is true.

In getrailo/railo public history, `git log --all --reverse -S'publish="#formBool' -- railo-cfml/railo-admin/admin/services.schedule.edit.cfm` and the analogous -S search for file=nullIfEmpty(form.file) both first return 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63 (2009-06-23, 'Initial version'). Its parent is 6b20542b4eeeec39064a4d38ea9fb88fa1d3fafe, and `git ls-tree` plus `git diff-tree --name-status` show the whole editor file absent in that parent and added by the commit.

`git log --all --reverse -S'IOUtil.copy' -- railo-java/railo-core/src/railo/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java` first returns 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb, whose parent is 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63. Direct parent-tree verification shows ExecutionThread.java absent in the parent and added in 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb. The imported file performs an HTTP GET, takes task.getResource(), and copies the response stream to that resource whenever task.isPublish(), with no path or .cfm execution guard.

That aggregate import proves a public-history boundary, not a smallest real BIC. The preceding 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63 is likewise a 300-file, 20,455-line admin import. review_record.bug_semantics: After authenticating to /lucee/admin/web.cfm, an administrator can create and edit a scheduled task whose URL is attacker-controlled, whose publish flag is true, and whose file value is an arbitrary path such as the deployed webroot plus a .cfm filename. services.schedule.edit.cfm passes those values to cfadmin action="schedule" without constraining the destination. ExecutionThread fetches the URL and, when publish is enabled, writes the response directly to the task Resource with IOUtil.write or IOUtil.copy. Requesting the newly written .cfm makes Lucee compile and execute attacker-supplied CFML as the Lucee service account. There is no destination-path restriction, payload integrity check, or control preventing a fetched response from becoming executable server-side code.
review_record.flaw_origin: The design predates the Lucee Git repository and is inherited from Railo. audit_record.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO v0.1.13 exposed its browser-reachable Supabase/PostgREST course resource without a server-side authorization rule that limited an authenticated student to the relations and fields appropriate for that role. A student could issue GET /rest/v1/course with a relational select expanding course to group, groupmember, profile, lesson, and teacher profile data; the effective course policy admitted course members while group/groupmember/profile reads exposed other people and metadata. The browser's normal query and UI role checks were not a security boundary because the student controlled the HTTP method and select expression.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Neither disputed SHA is a valid smallest real BIC. Primary candidate 60f06d6ab1468dd276ba4b95fe9478d4f95ce3e7 is a 77-file 'Sync with Server' aggregate that first adds the release-line browser projection, but that projection merely exercises the server authorization boundary and does not create the ability to send an arbitrary PostgREST GET. Reviewer candidate a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab is the first public repository representation of the causal grants/policies, but it adds a 1,290-line file explicitly named 20231115082347_remote_schema.sql containing a dump of an already-existing remote database. Its parent proves only repository absence, not absence in the deployed database. Later RLS commits preserve the exposure rather than originate it. Because imports, synchronization aggregates, moves, squashes, and reverts cannot substitute for the original smallest writer, the true BIC and its parent are outside the available public history.
audit_record.ai_marker: not_assessable: no smallest real BIC was verified, so there is no eligible BIC commit object from which to attribute AI involvement. The complete commit objects for both rejected candidates contain human author/committer identities and plain subjects with no AI trailer, but protocol forbids promoting that evidence from a rejected aggregate or imported snapshot into case attribution.

This makes missing server-side relation/field authorization the vulnerability; the normal UI request is only one way to exercise it.

Introducer disagreement resolved against both prior claims. `git diff e8c74de9cefbbffb61c674b5fb2ac5ba96775a2b 60f06d6ab1468dd276ba4b95fe9478d4f95ce3e7 -- src/utils/services/courses/index.js` shows primary's SHA adding fetchCourse with group(*,members:groupmember(*,profile(*))) and teacher profiles. `git show --stat --oneline 60f06d...` shows that it simultaneously changes 77 files (2,990 insertions and 7,611 deletions) under the generic subject 'Sync with Server'. It is an aggregate client synchronization, and client query text is not the server-side access-control origin.

The filename, full-schema SQL prologue, and wholesale addition establish an import of pre-existing remote state, so it cannot identify the original production writer.

primary_record.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO loaded a course directly from the browser through Supabase/PostgREST and requested the course's entire group, every groupmember row, and every related profile. An authenticated student could therefore send or alter a request to GET /rest/v1/course with the same bearer token and nested select projection and receive other students' and staff profiles plus course/group metadata; UI role checks did not constitute server-side authorization.
primary_record.flaw_origin: Commit 60f06d6ab1468dd276ba4b95fe9478d4f95ce3e7 first added src/utils/services/courses/index.js and its browser-side fetchCourse query: .from('course').select(...) included group(*, members:groupmember(*, profile(*))). Its immediate parent has neither that file nor any .from('course') query under src. Later moves and query expansion preserved the same mechanism, while permissive RLS imported in 2023 and course-member RLS added in 2025 failed to distinguish a student from staff when exposing nested course relations.

review_record.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO v0.1.13 exposed its Supabase/PostgREST public.course resource to low-privilege authenticated clients. A student could replace the application's scoped POST with GET /rest/v1/course and supply an arbitrary relational select. The effective course SELECT policy admitted every published course as well as courses whose group contained the caller, while group, groupmember, and profile rows were globally readable. PostgREST followed the course->group->groupmember->profile and course->lesson->profile foreign keys, so the response disclosed course metadata, membership records, other students, and tutor profiles without an authorization decision tied to the requested relation set or HTTP method.
review_record.flaw_origin: The first public-history writer is a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab (#19: Implement supabase local setup), which imported the remote schema and in one ordinary commit added the course/group/groupmember/profile tables and foreign keys, GRANT ALL on those tables to anon and authenticated, a course SELECT USING (true) policy, and a profile SELECT USING (true) policy. The commit is a schema import of an already existing remote database, so the production database may have predated the repository representation, but no earlier public commit contains the causal schema. Later RLS work preserved rather than originated the read exposure: 20240717053936_rls.sql enabled RLS yet created SELECT USING (true) policies for group and groupmember, and 20250808030821_rls_secure_courses.sql only narrowed course rows to is_published OR course-group/admin membership.

Subsequent RLS migrations did not cure that causal error: course visibility remained public-or-member and the nested membership/profile relations remained globally readable. The BIC commit object is plainly human-authored and has no AI marker, so NOT_AI is supported independently of later history. No fix SHA is assigned: the March 2026 rewrite removed Supabase/PostgREST but its landed replacement exposes essentially the same sensitive relation graph from an unauthenticated slug route, and that code remains at current main. An endpoint rename/architectural refactor is not a root-cause remediation. This is therefore a closed attribution verdict for an explicitly unpatched vulnerability lifecycle, not an EVIDENCE_GAP about AI provenance.

audit_record.bug_semantics: A locally supplied truncated pcap (wire length greater than captured length) processed by tcprewrite --fixlen pad reaches untrunc_packet, which reallocates the packet buffer and may free its old address. tcpedit_packet has already cached packet and IP-header aliases into that old allocation and does not rebase them after untrunc_packet returns; its later DLT merge path calls dlt_en10mb_l2len/get_l2len/get_l2len_protocol through the stale packet address, producing the reported heap use-after-free read (and other post-padding paths could likewise use stale header aliases).
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 changed untrunc_packet from padding the caller-provided buffer in place to safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len), and changed the API/caller to pass u_char **pktdata, but tcpedit_packet continued retaining its pre-call local packet, ip_hdr, and ip6_hdr aliases. In that original commit untrunc_packet did not even assign the new packet back through *pktdata; b58b23a52ffd23c3b1a2e2fe8b868aff0239560d later added *pktdata = packet but still did not rebase tcpedit_packet's cached aliases, so it did not cure the causal stale-pointer mechanism. The smallest first-writer is therefore 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14, not the later headroom adjustment 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860.
audit_record.ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 shows author and committer Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>, one parent, and only the message 'remalloc packets before padding to ensure not overwriting memory - closes #80'; there are no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI trailers/identities in the BIC commit object.
audit_record.evidence: First-party advisory issue https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/973 supplies the ASan chain: tcprewrite rewrite_packets -> tcpedit_packet -> untrunc_packet realloc -> tcpedit_dlt_merge_l3data -> dlt_en10mb_l2len -> get_l2len -> get_l2len_protocol, with the read at src/common/get.c:360 and the free at src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:562 in 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a. The related maintainer-tracked instance https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/970 identifies the same untrunc_packet realloc root in the checksum path; maintainer fix 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da is titled 'Bug #970 tcprewrite: --fixlen: do not use realloc' and its changelog explicitly says '--fixlen use-after-free (#970)'. git log -L 575,575:src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da^ and git log -S show that 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 first replaced in-place memset with packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len); 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 only added PACKET_HEADROOM. Direct parent diff/tree verification against 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e shows untrunc_packet still accepted u_char *pktdata and performed only memset(pktdata + caplen, ...), with no realloc/free, so the UAF mechanism is absent at the immediate parent. Release ancestry checks show v4.0.4 (9ab0e75ca894ad48402265d524207e4e1e8734bb) excludes the BIC; v4.0.5 (4d25e6f59b0cdef57cbd3e910652babe362ea4eb), v4.5.1 (0ba7d17fcb9ddedf61168f99c249b30731310d4e), and v4.5.2-beta2 (a1778a25a2f8dc4de879782567abab6b923e9694) contain the BIC but not the fix. Direct fix 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da removes safe_realloc, adds a pkthdr.len > MAX_SNAPLEN guard before copying into the already-MAXPACKET tcprewrite buffer, and changes configure.ac from 4.5.2-beta2 to 4.5.2-beta3; tagged v4.5.2 (98169912173986cc48a4ad325997dcc20c38af28) contains the fix. This matches the advisory boundary of affected through 4.5.1 and sufficient upgrade to 4.5.2-beta3.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability requires the realloc transition, not get_l2len_protocol itself: that parser is merely the observed stale-pointer consumer. History proves 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 is the atomic commit that first introduced realloc into the --fixlen pad branch while tcpedit_packet retained aliases established before the call. Its immediate parent cannot free or move pktdata on this path, establishing parent absence. Later commits changed pointer propagation and allocation headroom without removing the stale-alias hazard, and the flaw remained in every checked release from v4.0.5 through v4.5.1/v4.5.2-beta2. Commit 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da fixes the root by eliminating the realloc and bounding wire length to the preallocated capacity, with its own version metadata marking 4.5.2-beta3 and the v4.5.2 tag containing it. The BIC is a normal single-parent commit, not a merge/squash/backport, so no decomposition is applicable. Finally, the BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker; under the required BIC-only attribution rule, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

review_record.bug_semantics: A local attacker who can make tcprewrite process a crafted truncated pcap with `--fixlen pad` can reach `untrunc_packet()`. That function reallocates the packet buffer when the pcap header's wire length exceeds its captured length. If realloc moves the allocation, the pre-realloc base pointer and the IPv4/IPv6 header pointers derived from it in `tcpedit_packet()` become dangling. Processing nevertheless continues through DLT layer-3 merging; the Ethernet L2-length path calls `get_l2len()` and then `get_l2len_protocol()`, which reads protocol data through the freed allocation. The issue #973 ASan trace reports that exact read-after-free and abort path. The defect is the realloc in a control flow that retains aliases into the old allocation, not a bounds error authored in `get_l2len_protocol()` itself.
review_record.flaw_origin: Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 is the smallest true BIC. To repair an overwrite reported as issue #80, it changed `untrunc_packet()` to accept `u_char **pktdata`, copied `*pktdata` into local `packet`, and added `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len)` before padding, but it did not make all caller-held aliases safe after a move (and at that point did not even assign the new pointer back to `*pktdata`). Its immediate parent 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e has neither realloc nor safe_realloc in `src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c`, so it cannot free the packet on this path. Commit b58b23a52ffd23c3b1a2e2fe8b868aff0239560d later added `*pktdata = packet`, but did not refresh `tcpedit_packet()`'s local `packet`, `ip_hdr`, or `ip6_hdr` aliases, so the same realloc-caused UAF lifecycle continued rather than being newly introduced there. Commit 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 only enlarged the realloc request with `PACKET_HEADROOM`; it is not the BIC.
review_record.ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file -p 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14` shows author and committer `Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>` at timestamp 1406047482 -0700 and the complete message `remalloc packets before padding to ensure not overwriting memory - closes #80`; the commit object has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-assistance, or other trailer and no bot identity.
review_record.evidence: Advisory/report: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-722m-c232-cwqp identifies CVE-2025-9386, the `get_l2len_protocol` UAF, affected tcpreplay through 4.5.1, and 4.5.2-beta3 as sufficient; https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/973 gives `tcprewrite --fixlen pad -i POC_tcprewrite_protocol_length_use_after_free_360 -o /dev/null` and an ASan stack in which `untrunc_packet`/`safe_realloc` frees the allocation before `tcpedit_dlt_merge_l3data` -> `dlt_en10mb_l2len` -> `get_l2len` -> `get_l2len_protocol` reads it. Fix proof: `git show 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da` removes `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len + PACKET_HEADROOM)` from `src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c`, adds `pkthdr.len > MAX_SNAPLEN` rejection in `src/tcprewrite.c`, and bumps `configure.ac` from 4.5.2-beta2 to 4.5.2-beta3; `git grep` on its parent a1778a25a2f8dc4de879782567abab6b923e9694 still finds the realloc at line 575. The direct fix landed via merge a93ae465b966e6f675b25564ce292fb5cfe762ad (PR #975). Ancestry/version checks: BIC is contained by v4.0.5beta1 and v4.0.5, but not v4.0.4; direct fix is not contained by tag v4.5.2-beta2 (which points at its parent a1778a25...), is contained by v4.5.2, and `git tag --contains 73008f...` starts at v4.5.2. This clone has no `v4.5.2-beta3` tag, but the fix commit itself declares source version 4.5.2-beta3, matching the advisory. Marker proof is the exact `git cat-file -p 69831b...` commit object quoted in `ai_marker`.
review_record.reasoning: The advisory's named reader is only the observed sink. The causal operation is the conditional realloc in `untrunc_packet`: it may free the old buffer after `tcpedit_packet` has cached the base and header pointers, and subsequent protocol/L2 processing dereferences those stale aliases. History search places the first such realloc in 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14. The direct parent was inspected and has no allocation-moving call on this path, so parent absence is proven despite the parent's separate risk of padding beyond available capacity. The 2017 writeback is an incomplete mitigation, not a fresh origin, because caller-local and derived aliases remain stale; the 2020 headroom edit changes only allocation size. The 2025 direct fix 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da closes the root cause by enforcing the preallocated maximum-size invariant and deleting realloc, with vulnerable beta2 as its parent and fixed source version beta3. audit_record.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated client first requests /login.php to obtain an ICTBroadcast session cookie, then replaces the cookie value (observed as BROADCAST, although the applicable cookie name can vary) with shell metacharacters such as a backtick command substitution. ICTBroadcast passes the attacker-controlled session identifier into a shell-backed session-log command of the form sh -c echo "... Session read requested with id: <cookie> ..." >> gui.log. Because the cookie is not shell-neutralized, the shell evaluates the embedded backticks; a payload that base64-decodes and pipes a command to sh therefore executes arbitrary commands as the web-service account before authentication.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The causal flaw is in ICTBroadcast's product-side session read/logging implementation: it interpolates the untrusted cookie/session identifier into a shell command merely to append a diagnostic log line. The assigned rapid7/metasploit-framework repository does not contain that product implementation; it contains only a later exploit module and its documentation. ICTBroadcast's corresponding proprietary source repository and revision history are not publicly identified, so the commit that first introduced the shell interpolation cannot be reconstructed from this clone.
audit_record.ai_marker: not inspectable: no vulnerability-introducing ICTBroadcast commit object is available. Per the BIC-only rule, no AI attribution was inferred from rapid7/metasploit-framework PR #20446, its branch commits, its merge commit, the PR body, or later material because those objects add exploit tooling and do not introduce the product flaw.
evidence: The bundle's GitHub advisory (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3h67-687r-7fpc) says ICTBroadcast passes session-cookie data to shell processing, lists affected/patched versions as unknown, and explicitly reports 'Source code: No known source code.' NVD (https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-2611) and VulnCheck (https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/ictbroadcast-unauthenticated-session-cookie-rce) bound the known affected range to ICTBroadcast <= 7.4; neither supplies a product source commit or fix commit.

First-party disclosure context in rapid7/metasploit-framework PR #20446 (https://github.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/pull/20446) records discovery on 2025-03-19, repeated unanswered vendor contact, and the researcher's statement on 2025-08-02: 'As of today, I have no idea whether it's been patched.' A later PR comment demonstrates the sink as sh -c echo "... Session read requested with id: `id` " >> /usr/ictbroadcast/logs/gui.log, directly explaining why backticks in the session identifier execute.

In the validated clone, `git log --all --grep='CVE-2025-2611\|ICTBroadcast\|20446' -i` finds the Metasploit submission chain beginning at 50ef5edd90273b4147673d033ed2919640861e7a (parent c2971d53075e3c70a4d5c8df97fe82788215b16e) and the two-parent landing merge c99702c8bfffaf5fc84a98842c9685cfe2c1e01a (parents 26bf49a0248e73afdf97f0e8afebace7f0019fc5 and 6ff04da954e69fe4f02c800a707d20fef0a490d9). `git show --stat` proves these commits create documentation/modules/exploit/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.md and modules/exploits/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.rb; they do not modify ICTBroadcast product code and therefore are disclosure/exploit commits, not BICs or fixes.

At landing commit c99702c8bfffaf5fc84a98842c9685cfe2c1e01a, modules/exploits/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.rb:get_valid_cookies sends an unauthenticated GET to login.php and collects the issued cookies; inject_command then sets each cookie value to a backtick payload, `echo${IFS}<base64>|base64${IFS}-d|sh`, and sends another GET to login.php. The module's documented timing check and reverse-shell scenario establish the reachable attack path without claiming that the module is vulnerable product source.

A worktree path search for **/login.php in the validated rapid7/metasploit-framework clone returned no files. A scoped source search located ICTBroadcast references only in modules/exploits/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.rb and documentation/modules/exploit/linux/http/ictbroadcast_unauth_cookie.md. Thus the assigned clone cannot support git log -L/-S or immediate-parent tree verification for the product-side logging statement.

The version boundary is externally corroborated only as known-vulnerable <= 7.4. There is no published patched-version boundary to map to an ICTBroadcast tag, and Metasploit tags cannot answer product-version membership. Consequently introducer parent absence, BIC-before-affected-release membership, and fix-at/after-patched-boundary checks are not performable rather than failed.

The October 2025 VulnCheck exploitation report (https://www.vulncheck.com/blog/ictbroadcast-kev) independently records live exploitation through a BROADCAST cookie containing the same backtick/base64/sh construction. It corroborates the vulnerability mechanism and continued vulnerable deployments, but it publishes neither ICTBroadcast source history nor a vendor fix commit. Patch status therefore remains unknown, and both fix SHA fields are null rather than treating the Metasploit exploit landing as a fix.
audit_record.reasoning: The lifecycle starts in ICTBroadcast itself, not in Metasploit: by at least the known affected <=7.4 line, an unauthenticated login request causes a client-supplied session identifier to reach a shell-built logging command. Shell command substitution turns a crafted cookie into RCE. The researcher discovered this on 2025-03-19, received no vendor response, publicly submitted a working Metasploit module on 2025-08-02, and Rapid7 landed that module on 2025-08-05; later in-the-wild observations confirm the same route. Commit 50ef5edd90273b4147673d033ed2919640861e7a is the smallest Metasploit commit adding the exploit, but it only describes and exercises an already-existing external product flaw, so designating it as the BIC would invert causality. The merge c99702c8bfffaf5fc84a98842c9685cfe2c1e01a is likewise only a landing aggregate. Because no known ICTBroadcast product source repository, product commit history, immediate parent tree, or vendor fix is available, the smallest real BIC cannot be found, its immediate-parent absence cannot be verified, and its commit-object AI signals cannot be inspected. The <=7.4 affected boundary is supported, but patch status is unknown/unpublished and there is no patched tag or fix SHA to cross-check. This is a genuine inaccessible public-history boundary, so BLOCKED is more accurate than EVIDENCE_GAP and no AI verdict is made.
audit_record.remaining_gap: The missing evidence is the non-public ICTBroadcast product history: the source revision that first constructed the shell-backed session log from an untrusted cookie, that revision's immediate parent, release/tag membership for <=7.4, and any vendor remediation revision and patched release. Patch status remains unknown rather than proven unpatched. Resolving the case requires vendor-authenticated source/VCS history (or a public source mirror with preserved provenance) and a vendor fix/release record; the public Metasploit exploit repository cannot supply those facts.

review_record.bug_semantics: ICTBroadcast's unauthenticated /login.php session startup accepts the attacker-controlled session ID from the site cookie (normally BROADCAST) and passes it to the custom Session::read handler. The vulnerable handler logs `Session read requested with id: $id` before rejecting malformed IDs. The logging path invokes a shell command equivalent to `sh -c echo "[...] Session read requested with id: `id` " >> /usr/ictbroadcast/logs/gui.log`; therefore shell metacharacters/backticks embedded in the cookie are evaluated as command substitution. An attacker first GETs /login.php to obtain the configured cookie, then returns a value such as `` `echo${IFS}<base64>|base64${IFS}-d|sh` ``. No authentication is needed, and the injected command executes during session handling. The later-looking valid_sid check in the publicly downloadable 7.1.12 package is too late for the logged read path because fileLog is called on the raw ID first.
review_record.flaw_origin: The flaw is in ICT Innovations' separately distributed ICTBroadcast product, not in rapid7/metasploit-framework. Rapid7's repository contains only the post-discovery exploit module and its documentation. Public vendor RPMs expose snapshots but not the ICTBroadcast Git history: build 6.0.26 (short build ID 67c41c6c) has an older procedural session_read with the logging calls commented out, while build 7.1.12 (short build ID e966e3ef) has the class-based Session::read and the unsafe pre-validation fileLog call. Those eight-hex build IDs are not full public commit objects, the package has no .git metadata, the bootstrap/logger implementation is ionCube-protected, and the vendor organization has no public ICTBroadcast product repository. Consequently the smallest commit that first wrote the unsafe logging flow, its direct parent, and any direct fixing commit are outside public history.
review_record.ai_marker: Not assessable under the BIC-only rule: the true ICTBroadcast BIC commit object is not public, so its author/committer, bot identity, and Co-authored-by/Generated-with trailers cannot be inspected. The available Rapid7 commit 50ef5edd90273b4147673d033ed2919640861e7a has author/committer Chocapikk and no AI trailer, but it creates the exploit and documentation after vulnerability discovery; it is explicitly not the BIC and is not used as AI evidence.

(2) https://github.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/pull/20446 records discovery/vendor disclosure on 2025-03-19, repeated vendor non-response, the author's statement on 2025-08-02 that patch status was unknown, and the exact mechanism: /login.php issues the cookie and server-side handling evaluates cookie data through backticks. The 2025-10-27 maintainer comment gives the observed sink command: `sh -c echo "[Mon, 27 Oct 2025 17:05:46 +0000] [debug] Session read requested with id: `id` " >> /usr/ictbroadcast/logs/gui.log`. (3) https://www.vulncheck.com/blog/ictbroadcast-kev records exploitation observed on 2025-10-11, including `Cookie: BROADCAST=`echo${IFS}c2xlZXAgMw==|base64${IFS}-d|sh`` (decoding to `sleep 3`) followed by reverse-shell payloads. review_record.bug_semantics: tcpprep accepts include/exclude selector strings that are expected to contain a one-byte mode, a separator, and a payload. A malformed one-byte selector is heap-duplicated by the --load-opts doOptInclude path and passed to parse_xX_str. That function examines str[0] but, without checking the string length, advances the pointer by two bytes. For CIDR modes B, D, E, or S it then passes this one-past-allocation pointer to parse_cidr; mask_cidr6 immediately evaluates **cidrin and therefore reads beyond the two-byte allocation (the selector plus NUL), producing the reported heap-buffer-overflow/out-of-bounds read and crash. The closing fix rejects any nonempty one-byte selector before the switch and pointer advance.
review_record.flaw_origin: The unsafe parsing rule originated in 3941c24fbcdf2a9822df5d2a84ac0c3f5612e408, which introduced -x/-X parsing in tcpreplay.c and, for P/S/D/B/E, unconditionally executed str = str + 2 before parsing the payload. Its parent had no -x/-X parser. Commit 90c47b79caa0b7685e6d0d737e01b786ac4ac475 later copied/moved that parser into xX.c and is therefore not the origin; a9a5ec78124ea11c0ab9e1a8a0d74ce6616c4790 then exposed the shared parser through tcpprep. Commit f7d2fb9b5b8696bcc9a7a7b8bc0b5bb8b48273d5 later added mask_cidr6 and the exact reported dereference sink, but the invalid one-past pointer already reached strtok in parse_cidr at the origin, so the IPv6 change is not the root BIC.

See manpage for details.'; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity in the BIC commit object.

audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated user could bypass the profile image input's client-side accept hint and submit an SVG File. The profile flow uploaded the supplied bytes unchanged to the public Supabase avatars bucket, merely naming the object with a .webp suffix, then persisted its public URL. Directly viewing that stored object from the trusted storage origin caused JavaScript embedded in the SVG to execute, yielding stored XSS.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 05ed2b74ee25aaeddefc62121202ee97ed8637f0 introduced the profile-avatar upload end to end: a new UploadImage component accepted a File without validating its MIME type, extension, or contents, and src/routes/profile/[id].svelte uploaded that untrusted File directly to the public avatars bucket and stored its URL. The accept=".jpg, .jpeg, .png" attribute was only a browser file-picker hint, while forcing a .webp object name did not decode or transcode the uploaded bytes.
audit_record.ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names human author and committer rotimi-best <best@classroomio.com>, has the subject "Upload avatar", and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, trailer, or other AI marker.
evidence: The reporter disclosure at https://github.com/Rivek619/CVE-2025-65675 identifies ClassroomIO 0.1.13 and reproduces the issue by logging in, uploading a crafted SVG as the profile picture, saving it, and opening the stored image in a new tab; the embedded script then executes.

Direct parent-tree checks found no src/components/UploadImage/index.svelte at all (git cat-file -e exited 128), and the parent's profile page had no File selection, avatars-bucket upload, generated public URL, or attacker-controlled profile-picture persistence path.

05ed2b74ee25aaeddefc62121202ee97ed8637f0 is a single-parent commit, not a merge or release aggregate, and is an ancestor of v0.1.13 and every listed v0.1.x tag. Same-message commits on unrelated histories were not ancestors of v0.1.13 and therefore are not the BIC for this release lineage.

The direct fix commit 900f5ec12979f512ae8f333312aee78973a054f5 adds validateImageUpload calls before UploadImage and UploadWidget accept a file, central JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP MIME and extension allowlists, explicit SVG rejection, and SVG/data-URL sanitization. Its message expressly says it fixes stored XSS through malicious SVG profile uploads.

The version boundary is direct: v0.2.4 peels to 4ac242d918988855db54aff3578aa73a6d408d2e, does not contain 900f5ec12979f512ae8f333312aee78973a054f5, and has no validateImageUpload reference in the profile UploadImage component. Annotated security tag v0.2.5 peels directly to 900f5ec12979f512ae8f333312aee78973a054f5 and contains those checks. Thus the advisory-named v0.1.13 is demonstrably vulnerable and the repository's first tagged patched boundary is v0.2.5.

git cat-file commit 05ed2b74ee25aaeddefc62121202ee97ed8637f0 is the sole AI-attribution source inspected for the BIC: author and committer are both rotimi-best <best@classroomio.com>, the message is only "Upload avatar", and there are no trailers or AI/bot markers.
